articles.title: स्मार्टको सम्पत्ति कौडीमा एनसेलले हात पारेपछि हंगामा, भुपेन्द्र भण्डारी पक्राउपछि चासो बढ्यो
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणमा नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणका पूर्वअध्यक्ष भूपेन्द्र भण्डारी पक्राउ परेका छन्। नेपाल प्रहरीको सीआइबीले भण्डारीलाई अनुसन्धानका लागि पक्राउ गरेको छ। भण्डारी किन पक्राउ परे? स्मार्ट प्रकरणमा भण्डारीको भूमिका के? चासो देखिन्छन्।

नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणका पूर्वअध्यक्ष भूपेन्द्र भण्डारी पक्राउ परेका छन्। स्मार्ट सेलको सम्पत्ति बेचेर राज्यलाई हानी नोक्सानी पु¥याएको आरोपमा उनी पक्राउ परेका हुन्। तत्कालीन समयमा रेखा शर्मा सञ्चार तथा सूचना प्रविधिमन्त्री हुँदा भण्डारी विज्ञको रूपमा उनको सचिवालयमा नियुक्त भएका थिए ।

सचिवालयमा विज्ञ भनिएका भण्डारीलाई टेरामक्स प्रकरणले चिठ्ठा नै पर्ने स्थिति बन्यो। त्यसपछि टेरामक्स प्रकरणमा प्राधिकारणका तत्कालीन अध्यक्ष पुरुषोत्तम खनाल भ्रष्टाचार मुद्दाका कारण निलम्बित भएपछि उनले प्राधिकरणको अध्यक्ष पदमा सहजै पुग्ने स्थिति निर्माण गरे। तर, भण्डारी अध्यक्ष बनेपछि नै स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति कौडीको भाउमा वेच्ने काम भएको बताइन्छ। राज्यको नाममा आईसकेको टेलिकमको सम्पत्तिलाई निजी कम्पनी एनसेललाई कौडीको भाउमा बेच्न सघाएको आरोपमा भण्डारी पक्राउ परेका हुन्।

के भन्यो सीआइबीले ?

नेपाल प्रहरीको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआईबी)ले शुक्रबार ललितपुरको धापाखेलबाट पक्राउ गरेको जनाएको छ। उनलाई स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणमा अनुसन्धानका लागि पक्राउ गरिएको बताइएको छ। सीआईबीले सरकारको स्वामित्वमा आएको स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति बेइमानीपूर्वक सरकारको हक टुटाउन काम गराएको आरोपमा भण्डारी माथि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको थियो।

दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणबाट आधारभूत टेलिफोन सेवा सञ्चालन गर्न स्मार्ट टेलिकमले २०७० वैशाखमा अनुमति पाएको थियो। तर अनुमतिपत्र नवीकरण नगरेपछि स्मार्ट टेलिकमको लाइसेन्स स्वतः रद्द भएको थियो। यसरी सरकारको नाममा पुगिसकेको सम्पत्तिलाई बेचबिखन गर्नका निम्ति सघाएको आरोप भण्डारीमाथि समेत लागेको छ। प्राधिकरण नियामक निकाय समेत भएकाले पनि उनीमाथि अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने माग पहिलेदेखि नै उठ्दै आएको थियो । यता, ब्युरोले वैशाखमा स्मार्ट टेलिकमका तत्कालीन प्रबन्ध निर्देशक सर्वेश जोशीलाई पक्राउ गरिसकेको छ।

स्मार्टमा एनसेलको चलाखी

इजाजत खारेजीपछि विवादास्पद रूपमा सम्पत्ति लिलाम बिक्री भएको स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणमा निजी क्षेत्रको दूरसञ्चार सेवाप्रदायक कम्पनी एनसेल, त्यहाँका प्रमुख लगानीकर्ता र राजनीतिक नेतृत्वबीच शंकास्पद सम्बन्ध देखिएको भन्दै सीआइबीले अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ।

स्मार्टको सम्पत्ति बिक्रीबाट प्रमुख लाभग्राही एनसेल देखिएको छ। नेपाल दूरसञ्चार नियमावलीको नियम १० क मा एकै कम्पनीले एकभन्दा बढी दूरसञ्चार सेवा प्रदायकको अनुमति नपाउने उल्लेख छ। तर एनसेलमा लगानी गरेकाहरुले नै गैरकानुनीरूपले लिलामी गरिएको स्मार्ट टेलिकममा पनि लगानी सकारेकोे सीआईबीको ठहर छ ।

अहिले अनुसन्धानमा स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सेयर बिक्री, सेयर स्वामित्वको इतिहास, बैंक ऋण, सम्पत्ति हस्तान्तरण र एनसेलसँग जोडिएका विभिन्न कारोबार हेरिएको छ। प्रहरीले स्मार्ट टेलिकम, त्यसका सेयरधनी, सम्पत्ति व्यवस्थापन, उपकरण बिक्री र एनसेलसँग जोडिएका आर्थिक सम्बन्धबारे अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

सीआईबीका अनुसार सम्पत्ति लिलाम प्रक्रियाभन्दा अगाडि नै स्मार्ट टेलिकम र एनसेलबीच सम्बन्ध देखिन्छ। यही आधारमा एनसेलसँग जोडिएका केही उच्च तहका व्यक्तिलाई पनि छानबिनको दायरामा ल्याइएको छ। स्मार्टको सम्पत्ति लिलाम प्रकरणमा एनसेलको नेपालस्थित सञ्चालकहरू सतिशलाल आचार्य, भावना सिंह श्रेष्ठ र सचिनलाल आचार्य पनि अनुसन्धानको राडारमै रहेका छन्।

दुरसञ्चार ऐन र स्वार्थको द्वन्द्ध

दुरसञ्चार ऐन २०५३ को दफा नंवर ३३ को उपदफा १ बमोजिम नेपाल सरकारले स्वामित्वमा आएको सम्पत्ति पूर्व अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्तिले उपदफा (३) बमोजिम निर्धारण गरिने मूल्य नेपाल सरकारलाई बुझाई पुनः अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त गरी दूरसञ्चार सेवा सञ्चालन गर्न सक्नेछ भनिएको छ ।

फेरि उपदफा २ बमोजिमको मूल्य निर्धारण गर्ने प्रयोजनको लागि नेपाल सरकारले प्राधिकरणको परामर्श लिई बमोजिम विशेषज्ञ व्यक्तिहरुको एक समिति गठन गर्न सक्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको छ । तर, प्राधिकारणले सरकारको स्वामित्वमा आइसकेको स्मार्ट टेलिकम एनसेललाई बेच्ने कुरा नै असंगत, पदीय दुरुपयोग र भ्रष्टाचार हुने दाबीहरु सार्वजनिक भइरहेका छन्।

यस्तो अवस्थामा प्राधिकरणको अध्यक्ष बनेका भण्डारीले पनि कानूनको उल्लङ्घन गर्दै स्मार्टको पक्षमा काम गरेकाले उनी अनुसन्धानमा तानिएका हुन्। तत्कालीन माओवादी केन्द्रबाट सञ्चारमन्त्री बनेकी शर्माले अध्यक्ष नियुक्त गरेका भण्डारीमाथि पदीय दुरुपयोगको गम्भीर आरोप लाग्दै गर्दा नियुक्ति दिने शर्मामाथि समेत केहिले प्रश्न उठाएका छन्। कतै यो सबै सेटिङमै त भएन?

प्रहरीले अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने बाटो यसतर्फ समेत केन्द्रित गर्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिन थालिएको छ। यद्यपी शर्मामाथि यस्ता आरोप भने सार्वजनिक रुपमा लागेको देखिन्न। तर, सचिवालयको विज्ञ भनिएको कर्मचारीलाई अध्यक्ष नियुक्त गरेपछि कानून मिचेको देखिदा उनीमाथि समेत यस्तो प्रश्न स्वभाविक बन्न पुगेको छ ।

articles.title: ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुप नेपाल प्रवेश : जेम होम कलेक्सन आधिकारिक वितरक नियुक्त
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं। भारतको अग्रणी होम टेक्सटाइल कम्पनी ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुपले नेपाली बजारमा औपचारिक रूपमा प्रवेश गरेको छ। कम्पनीले नेपालका लागि आफ्ना होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरूको एकमात्र आधिकारिक वितरकको रूपमा जेम होम कलेक्सन प्राइभेट लिमिटेडलाई नियुक्त गरेको घोषणा गरेको छ। यस सहकार्यसँगै नेपाली उपभोक्ताहरूले अब ट्राइडेन्टका प्रिमियम बेड लिनेन, बाथ लिनेन, तौलियालगायतका होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरू आधिकारिक तथा भरपर्दो माध्यमबाट प्राप्त गर्न सक्नेछन्।

यसअघि नेपाली बजारमा ट्राइडेन्टका उत्पादनहरू प्रायः अनौपचारिक माध्यमबाट भित्रिने गरेकोमा यस नियुक्तिपछि गुणस्तर र प्रामाणिकताको सुनिश्चितता हुने कम्पनीहरूको दाबी छ। यस साझेदारीले नेपालमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रियस्तरका होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरूको पहुँच विस्तार गर्ने र नेपाली ग्राहकहरूलाई विश्वस्तरीय गुणस्तर, आधिकारिक आपूर्ति शृंखला तथा उत्कृष्ट ग्राहक सेवा उपलब्ध गराउने लक्ष्य राखेको छ।

जेम होम कलेक्सन प्राइभेट लिमिटेड विगत ३० वर्षदेखि नेपालको फ्लोरिङ तथा फर्निसिङ क्षेत्रमा सक्रिय रहेको कम्पनी हो। यसले आतिथ्य र खुद्रा दुवै बजारका लागि विविध गुणस्तरीय उत्पादनहरू निरन्तर आपूर्ति गर्दै आएको छ। यही दीर्घकालीन बजार अनुभव र स्थापित वितरण सञ्जालका कारण कम्पनीलाई ट्राइडेन्टको आधिकारिक साझेदारका रूपमा छनोट गरिएको बताइएको छ।

ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुपको स्थापना सन् १९९० मा भारतीय उद्यमी पद्मश्री राजिन्दर गुप्ताले पञ्जाबबाट सुरु गरेका थिए। सुरुमा एउटा मात्र धागो उत्पादन एकाइबाट सुरु भएको यो समूह हाल विश्वकै सबैभन्दा ठूला टेरी तौलिया उत्पादक र समग्र होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादकहरूमध्ये एक बनेको आर्थिक हिसाबले हेर्ने हो भने पछिल्लो प्रतिवेदन अनुसार ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुपले आर्थिक वर्ष २०२६ मा ६५ अर्ब २१ करोड भारतीय रुपैयाँ बराबरको आम्दानी हासिल गरेको थियो, जुन अघिल्लो वर्षको तुलनामा सामान्य घटेको भए पनि खुद नाफा भने बढेको थियो।

चालु आर्थिक वर्षको हालसालैको प्रगति हेर्दा पनि, पहिलो त्रैमासमा आम्दानी १ हजार ८ सय ३० करोड रुपैयाँ पुगेको र खुद नाफा ५५ प्रतिशतले वृद्धि भएको देखिन्छ। कम्पनीको समग्र आकारका सन्दर्भमा हेर्दा, ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुप इन्डियामा हाल १६ हजार ३ सय तीनजना कर्मचारी कार्यरत रहेका छन् र यसको बजार पूँजीकरण करिब १।३२ बिलियन डलर बराबर रहेको पाइन्छ। समूह लामो समयदेखि आफूलाई एक बिलियन डलरभन्दा बढी मूल्यको वैश्विक व्यापारिक समूहको रूपमा चिनाउँदै आएको छ, जसको होम टेक्सटाइल, कागज र रसायन क्षेत्रमा सशक्त उपस्थिति रहेको दाबी गरिन्छ।

यसआधिकारिक वितरण सम्झौतापछि नेपाली उपभोक्ताहरूले अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरका होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरू प्रामाणिकताको सुनिश्चितताका साथ प्राप्त गर्न सक्नेछन् भने होटल तथा रिसोर्ट जस्ता आतिथ्य व्यवसायहरूले पनि विश्वसनीय आपूर्ति स्रोत भेट्टाउने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ। साथै यसले नेपालको होम फर्निसिङ बजारमा स्वस्थ प्रतिस्पर्धा र गुणस्तर सुधारमा समेत योगदान पुर्‍याउने कम्पनीको भनाइ छ।

articles.title: मेची राजमार्ग ठप्प ! सडक बन्द हुँदा बिरामीदेखि ढुवानीसम्म संकट
articles.summary:
इलाम । मेची राजमार्ग अन्तर्गत इलाम माइखोला राजदुवालीकमाथि सडक अवरुद्ध भएको तीन सात भयो । सडक खुल्ने अझै छाँटकाँट छैन । सडक बन्द भएपछि इलाम मात्र हैन पुर्वी पहाडी जिल्ला पाँचथर ताप्लेजुङ लगायतका स्थानीयलाई समेत सास्ती भएको छ ।

मेची राजमार्ग अन्तर्गत इलामको माइखोला (राजदुवाली) माथिको सडक भासिएर तीन सातादेखि अवरुद्ध हुँदा इलामसँगै पाँचथर र ताप्लेजुङका नागरिकले सास्ती भोगिरहेका छन् । सडक बन्द भएपछि सवारी साधन वारिपारि नै रोकिने गरेका छन् भने यात्रुहरू करिब एक किलोमिटर भिरको बाटो पैदल हिँड्न बाध्य छन् ।

बिरामीलाई जनपथ प्रहरी, सशस्त्र प्रहरी र नेपाली सेनाले स्टे«चरमार्फत वारपार गराइरहेका छन् भने एम्बुलेन्स पनि दुवैतर्फबाट सेवा दिन बाध्य छन् । अत्यावश्यक खाद्यान्न, ग्यास र तरकारी ढुवानीसमेत प्रभावित बनेको छ । इलाम नगरपालिकाले सरोकारवाला निकायसँग छलफल गरी पुनः इलामलाई संकटग्रस्त क्षेत्र घोषणा गर्न सरकारसँग माग गरेको छ ।

राजदुवाली खण्डको पहिरो नियन्त्रण, ट्रस्ट पुल मर्मत तथा जोरकलश–हर्कटे सडक स्तरोन्नतिको लागि २४ करोड ९३ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढीको ठेक्का जे एन्ड जे निर्माण सेवा प्रालिले २०८४ असारसम्म सम्पन्न गर्ने गरी लिएको भएपनि हालसम्म समग्रमा १८–२० प्रतिशत मात्र काम भएको सडक डिभिजन कार्यालयले जनाएको छ । स्थानीयले मुख्य सडकभन्दा वैकल्पिक सडक तत्काल सञ्चालनमा ल्याउन माग गरेका छन् ।

गत वर्ष तीन महिनासम्म संकटग्रस्त क्षेत्र घोषणा गरिए पनि प्रभावकारी काम नभएको भन्दै स्थानीय आक्रोशित छन् । सरकारले सडक बनाउन नसके इलामेली आफैंले श्रमदान र चन्दा उठाएर सडक तथा पुल निर्माण गर्ने चेतावनी दिएका छन् ।

सडक अवरुद्धकै कारण बिरामीले समयमै उपचार नपाएर ज्यान गुमाउनुपर्ने अवस्था रहेको भन्दै तत्काल समाधानको माग गरिएको छ ।

उता वैकल्पिक सडकका रूपमा प्रयोग गरिने सिमलगोलाई–तिल्केनी तथा केचना–कञ्चनजंघा सडकको बेलासी–भन्ज्याङ खण्ड पनि निर्माणमा ढिलाइका कारण सञ्चालन योग्य छैन । माइजोगमाई र पुवा खोलाका पुल गत वर्षको बाढीले बगाएपछि अहिलेसम्म पुनर्निर्माण हुन सकेको छैन । यस वर्ष बजेटमै इलामलाई बेवास्ता गरिएको भन्दै स्थानीयले सरकारसँग तत्काल सडक सञ्चालनको सुनिश्चितता गर्न माग गरेका छन् ।

articles.title: बौद्धनाथमा अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिमा राजनीतिक हस्तक्षेप, कसले रोक्यो सम्पूर्णकुमार लामाको नियुक्ति पत्र ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समिति तीन महिनादेखि अध्यक्षविहीन छ । संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्रालय मातहतको यो महत्वपूर्ण निकायमा मन्त्रिपरिषद्बाट अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिको सिफारिस भइसके पनि राजनीतिक स्वार्थका कारण नियुक्तिले अझै पूर्णता पाउन सकेको छैन । अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिको निर्णय भइसकेको एक महिना बित्न लाग्दा पनि नियुक्तिपत्र रोकिँदा सरकारको नियतमाथि नै प्रश्न उठ्न थालेको छ ।

गत असार १८ गते मन्त्रिपरिषद्को निर्णयअनुसार संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्रालयले बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिको अध्यक्षमा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामालाई नियुक्त गर्ने निर्णय गरेको थियो । तर विडम्बना, निर्णय भएको यति समय बितिसक्दा पनि लामाले नियुक्तिपत्र पाएका छैनन् ।

समितिका अध्यक्षसहित पाँच पदाधिकारी नियुक्त गरिए पनि अध्यक्ष लामाबाहेक सबै सदस्यले नियुक्तिपत्र बुझिसकेका छन् । अध्यक्षलाई मात्रै रोक्नुको कारण काठमाडौं–३ का रास्वपा सांसद राजुनाथ पाण्डे रहेको आरोप छ ।

स्थानीयका अनुसार सांसद पाण्डेले आफ्ना निकट व्यक्तिलाई अध्यक्ष बनाउन दबाब दिएपछि लामाको नियुक्तिपत्र रोकिएको हो । लामो समयदेखि समिति नेतृत्वविहीन हुँदा गुठियारदेखि स्थानीय सरोकारवालासम्म सरकारसँग जवाफ माग्न थालेका छन् । उनीहरूको चेतावनी छ, ‘रास्वपाभित्रको जुंगाको लडाइँको छायाँ बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिमा पार्न मिल्दैन ।’

दुई कार्यकाल सफलतापूर्वक अध्यक्षको जिम्मेवारी सम्हालिसकेका सम्पूर्णकुमार लामाको पुनः नियुक्तिका लागि गुठियार, स्थानीय जनप्रतिनिधि, विभिन्न संघसंस्था र बुद्धिजीवीहरूले एकमत सिफारिस गरेका थिए । स्थानीयका अनुसार लामा सबैले स्वीकार गरेका र समन्वयकारी क्षमता भएका व्यक्ति हुन् । अध्यक्ष नहुँदा बौद्धनाथमा प्रशासनिक कामदेखि सामाजिक, धार्मिक, सांस्कृतिक तथा विकास निर्माणका गतिविधि प्रभावित भएका छन् । बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिले यहाँका विभिन्न धार्मिक तथा सामाजिक संघसंस्थाबीच समन्वय गर्दै आएको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका पनि अहिले नेतृत्व अभावकै कारण कमजोर बनेको छ ।

अलमलमा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामा

अध्यक्षमा नियुक्ति भइसकेको एक महिना बित्न लाग्दा पनि नियुक्तिपत्र नपाउँदा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामा अन्योलमा परेका छन् । नियुक्ति भइसकेको व्यक्तिलाई नै बदर गराएर अर्को व्यक्तिलाई ल्याउने प्रयास सांसद पाण्डेले गरिरहेको स्थानीयको आरोप छ ।

उनीहरू भन्छन्, ‘सर्वस्वीकार्य व्यक्तिको नियुक्ति रोक्नु सरकारकै लागि ‘ब्याकफायर’ हुन सक्छ ।’ यसअघि पनि सरकार विभिन्न नियुक्ति र निर्णयका कारण विवादमा परिसकेको छ । धार्मिक तथा सांस्कृतिक संस्थामा राजनीतिक भागबन्डा होइन, योग्य र सबैले स्वीकार गर्ने व्यक्तिलाई नेतृत्व दिनुपर्ने स्थानीयको जोड छ । यही विषयलाई लिएर काठमाडौं–३ का सांसद राजुनाथ पाण्डे र संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्री खडकराज पौडेल ९गणेश० बीच पनि मतभेद उत्पन्न भएको बताइएको छ ।

समितिका पाँच सदस्यमा विशाल लामा, निर्भिक्ता थिङ लामा, सेनाङ ग्याम्जो तामाङ, रोशनकुमार श्रेष्ठ र मणिभद्र पोखरेल नियुक्त भइसकेका छन् । तर अध्यक्षको नियुक्तिपत्र अझै रोकिँदा बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समिति नेतृत्वविहीन अवस्थामै अल्झिएको छ र राजनीतिक हस्तक्षेपको आरोप झन् गहिरिँदै गएको छ ।

articles.title: पूजारी भन्छन्– बृहस्पति अन्ध रहेको भ्रमले दर्शनार्थी घटे
articles.summary:
म्याग्दी । म्याग्दीको बेनी नगरपालिका ९ स्थित देशकै ऐतिहासिक र धार्मिक महत्व बोकेको गलेश्वरधाममा यस वर्षको साउन महिनामा विगतका वर्षको तुलनामा भक्तजनको चहलपहलमा कमि आएको छ ।

बृहस्पति अन्ध रहेको अवधिमा शुभकार्य गर्न नहुने धार्मिक मान्यताका कारण पनि दर्शनार्थीहरुको कमी आएको हो ।

साउन महिना भगवान शिवको अत्यन्त प्रिय महिना भएकाले यस अवधिमा शिवको आराधना, रुद्राभिषेक, बेलपत्र चढाउने तथा जल चढाउनु विशेष फलदायी मानिन्छ । तर बृहस्पति अन्ध भएकै कारण मन्दिरमा दर्शन गर्न हुँदैन भन्ने भ्रम फैलिएको छ ।

बृहस्पति अन्ध रहेको अवधिमा शुभकार्य गर्न नहुने धार्मिक मान्यतालाई लिएर दर्शनसमेत गर्न नहुने भन्ने भ्रमका कारण भक्तजनको संख्या घटेको छ ।

गलेश्वर शिवालयका गलेश्वरधामका मूल पुजारी चन्द्रमणि आचार्यका अनुसार धार्मिक शास्त्रमा भगवानको दर्शन र पूजा–अर्चना गर्न कुनै निषेध गरिएको छैन । बरु साउन महिनामा शिवको आराधना गर्दा विशेष पुण्य प्राप्त हुने धार्मिक विश्वास छ ।

गलेश्वरधाममा रहेको प्राकृतिक शिलामाथि अवस्थित स्वयं प्रकट शिवलिङ्ग विशेष आकर्षणको केन्द्र हो । एउटै ९ रोपनी क्षेत्रफलको विशाल चट्टानमाथि रहेको यो शिवलिङ्ग देश–विदेशका भक्तजनका लागि श्रद्धाको केन्द्र बनेको छ ।

विशेषगरी साउन महिना, महाशिवरात्रि, बालाचतुर्दशी तथा तीजका अवसरमा यहाँ हजारौँ श्रद्धालुको भीड लाग्ने गर्दछ ।

धेरै धार्मिक स्थलहरुमा पछि स्थापना गरिएको शिवलिङ्गमा पुजा गरिन्छ भने गलेश्वरधाममा स्वयं उत्पत्ती ज्योतिर्लिङ्ग भएको हुँदा पनि यस स्थानको छुट्टै धार्मिक महत्व हुने बताइन्छ ।

साउनको दोस्रो सोमबार भक्तजनले चढाएको भेटी गणना गरी बेनीस्थित गरिमा विकास बैंकमा दाखिला गरिएको छ । पहिलो सोमबार करिब दुई लाख रुपैयाँ भेटी संकलन भएको गलेश्वरधाममा दोस्रो सोमबार पनि करिब सोही हाराहारी रकम संकलन भएको थियो । भक्तजनको संख्या केही घटे पनि धार्मिक आस्थाका साथ दर्शन गर्ने क्रम भने निरन्तर भइरहेको छ ।

गलेश्वर शिवालय क्षेत्र परिसरमा निर्माण गरिएको १०८ शिवलिङ्ग भक्तजनका लागि अर्को प्रमुख आकर्षण बनेको छ ।

गलेश्वर शिवालय क्षेत्र विकास कोषका उपाध्यक्ष बमबहादुर पुनको अगुवाइमा चन्दा तथा सहयोगबाट संकलित करिब साढे १३ लाख रुपैयाँमध्ये साढे ७ लाख रुपैयाँ खर्च गरेर शिवलिङ्ग निर्माण गरिएको थियो ।

२०७६ सालमा निर्माण गरीएको यो धार्मिक महत्व दिने आकृति एकै स्थानमा १०८ शिवलिङ्गको दर्शन र पूजा गर्न सकिने भएपछि दैनिक रूपमा भक्तजन पुग्ने गरेका छन् ।

धार्मिक, सांस्कृतिक र प्राकृतिक सम्पदाको अनुपम संगमका रूपमा रहेको गलेश्वरधामले म्याग्दीको धार्मिक पर्यटन प्रवद्र्धनमा समेत महत्वपूर्ण योगदान पु¥याउँदै आएको छ । २०८२ सालका चार वटा सोमबार गरी झण्डै १७ लाख रुपियाँ भेटी संकलन भएको थियो ।

articles.title: बैतेश्वर गाउँपालिकामा भूमि प्रशासनसम्बन्धी सेवा शुरु
articles.summary:
दोलखा । नेपालको संविधानले स्थानीय तहबाटै भूमि प्रशासनसम्बन्धी सेवा प्रवाह गर्ने व्यवस्था गरेको ११ वर्षपछि दोलखाको बैतेश्वर गाउँपालिकाले जिल्लामै पहिलो पटक भूमि व्यवस्थापन शाखामार्फत मालपोत र नापीसम्बन्धी सेवा सञ्चालनमा ल्याएको छ ।

अब नागरिकले आफ्नै पालिकाबाट भूमि प्रशासनसम्बन्धी सेवा पाउने भएका छन् । २०७२ सालको संविधानले स्थानीय तहलाई भूमिसम्बन्धी सेवा प्रवाह गर्ने अधिकार दिएको थियो ।

त्यसलाई कार्यान्वयन गर्न नेपाल सरकारको भूमि व्यवस्था, सहकारी तथा गरिबी निवारण मन्त्रालय तथा संघीय मामिला तथा सामान्य प्रशासन मन्त्रालयले इच्छुक स्थानीय तहबाट आवेदन माग गरेपछि बैतेश्वर गाउँपालिका छनोटमा परेको हो ।

आवश्यक तयारी पूरा गरेपछि भूमि प्रशासन कार्यालय दोलखाले सेवा हस्तान्तरण गरेको छ । भूमि व्यवस्थापन शाखा सञ्चालनसँगै जग्गा किनबेच, नामसारी, अंशबण्डा, दानपत्र, हकछोड, सट्टापट्टा, नक्सा प्रिन्ट, कित्ता रेखाङ्कन लगायतका विभिन्न सेवा चरणबद्ध रूपमा गाउँपालिकाबाटै उपलब्ध हुने जनाइएको छ ।

सेवा लिन चाहने नागरिकमध्ये डिजिटल प्रणालीमा आबद्ध भइसकेकाले पालिकाबाटै सेवा लिन सक्नेछन्। डिजिटल प्रणालीमा आबद्ध नभएकाले भने पहिलो पटक भूमि प्रशासन कार्यालयमा गई आफ्नो अभिलेख डिजिटल प्रणालीमा दर्ता गराउनुपर्नेछ ।

नयाँ प्रणाली लागू भएसँगै सेवा नागरिकको घरदैलोमा पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिए पनि केही प्राविधिक चुनौती भने बाँकी नै छन् । भूमि प्रशासनसम्बन्धी सम्पूर्ण अभिलेख डिजिटल प्रणालीमा आधारित भएकाले श्रेस्ता (मूल अभिलेख) गाउँपालिकामा नहुँदा केही कानुनी तथा प्राविधिक जटिलता आउन सक्ने बताइएको छ । स्थानीय तहबाटै सेवा उपलब्ध हुन थालेपछि नागरिकको समय, खर्च र सदरमुकाम चरिकोट धाउनुपर्ने बाध्यता कम हुने भन्दै स्थानीय भने खुसी देखिन्छन् ।

संविधानले परिकल्पना गरेको स्थानीय तहबाट भूमि प्रशासन सेवा प्रवाहको व्यवस्था दोलखामा पनि कार्यान्वयनमा आएको हो । यसको प्रभावकारिता भने सेवा प्रवाहको गुणस्तर, डिजिटल प्रणालीको विश्वसनीयता र बाँकी प्राविधिक चुनौती समाधानमा निर्भर रहनेछ ।

articles.title: बुद्धकै पालादेखि शुरु भएको वर्षावास, किन शुरु भयो यस्तो परम्परा ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । असार पूर्णिमासँगै बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीहरूको तीन महिने वर्षावास सुरु भएको छ । गौतम बुद्धकै समयदेखि चल्दै आएको २५ सय वर्ष पुरानो यो परम्परा आत्मअनुशासन, ध्यान, साधना र आध्यात्मिक उन्नतिको प्रतीक मानिन्छ । बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीहरूको अत्यन्तै महत्वपूर्ण धार्मिक परम्परा तीन महिने वर्षावास शुरु भएको छ । हरेक वर्ष असार पूर्णिमादेखि कार्तिक पूर्णिमासम्म चल्ने यो परम्परा भिक्षुहरू एकै ठाउँमा बस्ने अभ्यास मात्रै होइन, यो अनुशासन, ध्यान, आध्यात्मिक साधना र बुद्धको जीवनसँग प्रत्यक्ष जोडिएको ऐतिहासिक अभ्यास पनि हो । बुद्धकै समयदेखि सुरु भएको यो परम्परा आखिर २५ सय वर्षपछि पनि किन उस्तै सान्दर्भिक छ ?

वर्षावासको सुरुवात

बुद्धले आफ्ना भिक्षुहरूलाई एउटा महत्वपूर्ण निर्देशन दिनुभएको थियो, “चरथ भिक्खवे चारिकं बहुजन हिताय, बहुजन सुखाय ।’ अर्थात्, “हे भिक्षुहरू ! बहुजनको हित र सुखका लागि गाउँ–गाउँ, नगर–नगर जाऊ, धर्म प्रचार गर ।’ बुद्धत्व प्राप्त गरेपछि भिक्षुहरू वर्षभरि विभिन्न स्थानमा धर्म प्रचार गर्न जान्थे । तर वर्षायाम सुरु भएपछि यात्रा कठिन हुन्थ्यो । बाटो बिग्रिन्थ्यो ।

नदीहरू बढ्थे । जीवजन्तु र बोटबिरुवामा क्षति पुग्ने सम्भावना पनि हुन्थ्यो । यही कारणले बुद्धले वर्षाको तीन महिना एकै स्थानमा बसेर ध्यान, अध्ययन र साधना गर्न निर्देशन दिनुभयो ।

यही अभ्यास नै पछि वर्षावासका रूपमा स्थापित भयो । धेरैलाई थाहा नहुन सक्छ, बौद्ध ग्रन्थमा उल्लेख भए अनुसार भगवान बुद्धले आफ्नो जीवनकालमा ४५ पटक वर्षावास बिताउनुभएको उल्लेख पाइन्छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष वर्षायाममा उहाँ कुनै न कुनै विहार, वन वा उपासकले बनाइदिएको आरामस्थलमा बस्नुहुन्थ्यो । यसले देखाउँछ, बुद्धले केवल उपदेश मात्र दिनुभएन । आफूले सिकाएको अभ्यासलाई जीवनभर पालना पनि गर्नुभयो ।

वर्षातको समयमा प्राकृतिक विपतिहरुबाट जोगिन र जोगाउनका साथै एकै ठाउँमा बसी नियमपुर्वक धार्मिक किसिमले जिवनयापन गर्नु नै यसको मुख्य उद्देश्य हो ।

वर्षावास किन विशेष छ ?

वर्षावास भिक्षुहरूको बसाइ मात्रै होइन । यो आत्मअनुशासनको समय हो । यस अवधिमा भिक्षुहरूले गहिरो ध्यान, विनयको अध्ययन, धर्म छलफल र आध्यात्मिक अभ्यासलाई प्राथमिकता दिन्छन् । उता गृहस्थ उपासक–उपासिकाहरू पनि विहारमा पुगेर दान, शील, ध्यान र धर्मश्रवणमार्फत आफ्नो आध्यात्मिक जीवनलाई अझ सुदृढ बनाउने प्रयास गर्छन् ।

वर्षावासपछि आउने कथिना चिवरदान

वर्षावास सकिएपछि बौद्ध समाजमा अर्को महत्वपूर्ण परम्परा सुरु हुन्छ कथिन चिवरदान । तीन महिना अनुशासित जीवन बिताएका भिक्षुहरूलाई श्रद्धालुहरूले सामूहिक रूपमा चिवर अर्पण गर्छन् । बौद्ध परम्परामा यसलाई सबैभन्दा ठूलो सामूहिक दानमध्ये एक मानिन्छ । यसले भिक्षु र गृहस्थबीचको सम्बन्धलाई अझ मजबुत बनाउने विश्वास गरिन्छ ।

बाइट–भिक्षु कौन्डण्य, विहार प्रमुख, बुद्ध विहार

विशेषगरी यो समयमा बौद्धमार्गीहरु विभिन्न विहारमा गई बुद्ध, धर्म, संघको गुणानुस्मरण गरी ध्यान भावना गरी आध्यात्मिक उन्नती तर्फ अग्रसर हुने गर्दछन् । विशेषगरी थेरवाद बुद्धधर्मको प्रभाव रहेको मुलुकमा वर्षावास परम्पराले धार्मिक आध्यात्मिक क्षेत्रमा सकारात्मक प्रभाव पारेको कारणले यसलाई बुद्धकालिन समयदेखि अहिलेसम्म पनि निरन्तरता दिइरहेको छ ।

२५ सय वर्षदेखि नटुटेको परम्परा

विश्वका धेरै धार्मिक अभ्यास समयसँगै परिवर्तन भएका छन् । तर वर्षावास भने बुद्धकालदेखि आजसम्म मूल स्वरूपमै कायम छ । नेपाल, श्रीलंका, थाइल्याण्ड, म्यानमार, कम्बोडिया, लाओस लगायत थेरवाद बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बी देशहरूमा आज पनि लाखौं भिक्षुहरू वर्षायाममा एकै स्थानमा बसेर यही परम्परा निर्वाह गर्छन् । समय फेरियो । प्रविधि फेरियो, समाज फेरियो । तर ध्यान, अनुशासन र आत्मशुद्धिको मूल्य कहिल्यै फेरिएन । सायद यही कारणले वर्षावास आज पनि उत्तिकै जीवित र सान्दर्भिक बनेको छ । बुद्धले सुरु गर्नुभएको वर्षावास अहिले एउटा धार्मिक अनुष्ठानमा मात्रै सिमित छैन ।

यो आत्मसंयम, करुणा, अनुशासन र आध्यात्मिक विकासको तीन महिने यात्राको रुपमा समेत स्थापित भइसकेको छ । बुद्धकै पालादेखि सुरु भएको यो परम्पराले आज पनि संसारभरका लाखौं बौद्ध अनुयायीलाई ध्यान, धर्म र आत्मपरिवर्तनतर्फ प्रेरित गरिरहेको छ ।

articles.title: घरभाडा व्यवस्थापन अब डिजिटल : घरधनी र भाडावालाको झन्झट अन्त्य गर्न ‘भाडासेवा’ बजारमा
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालमा घर, फ्ल्याट, सटर तथा व्यावसायिक भवनको व्यवस्थापनलाई डिजिटल बनाउने उद्देश्यले एजिनेक्स क्लाउडले ‘भाडासेवा’ नामक क्लाउड–आधारित प्रणाली सार्वजनिक गरेको छ। ‘व्यवस्थित र सुमधुर सम्बन्धका लागि भाडासेवा’ मूल नारासहित आएको यो प्रणालीले कागजी अभिलेख र एक्सेल फाइलको झन्झट अन्त्य गर्दै घरभाडा व्यवस्थापनका सम्पूर्ण प्रक्रियालाई एकै डिजिटल प्लेटफर्ममा समेटेको छ।

यस प्रणालीमार्फत प्रयोगकर्ताले भवन तथा कोठाहरुको रियल–टाइम अनुगमन, भाडावालाको डिजिटल प्रोफाइल, अनलाइन सम्झौता र डिजिटल हस्ताक्षर गर्न सक्नेछन्। साथै, मासिक भाडा र बिजुली–पानीको बिल स्वतः तयार हुने, अनलाइन भुक्तानी गर्न मिल्ने तथा स्वचालित रसिद आउने सुविधा यसमा रहेको छ।

अपार्टमेन्ट तथा व्यावसायिक कम्प्लेक्सका साझा खर्च (CAM) व्यवस्थापन, मर्मतसम्भार ट्र्याकिङ, कर्मचारी व्यवस्थापन र आम्दानी–खर्चको विस्तृत रिपोर्टिङसमेत यसैबाट गर्न सकिन्छ।

साना घरधनीदेखि ठूला सपिङ मल र व्यावसायिक कम्प्लेक्ससम्मका लागि उपयोगी यो प्रणाली कम्प्युटर, ट्याब्लेट र मोबाइलबाटै सजिलै चलाउन सकिन्छ।

articles.title: इनड्राइभ नेपालद्वारा ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ प्रमाणपत्र प्रदान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं, नेपाल । विश्वव्यापी मोबिलिटी तथा डेलिभरी प्लेटफर्म इनड्राइभले महिलालाई ड्राइभिङ पेसामा अघि बढ्न समान अवसर सिर्जना गर्ने उद्देश्यले सञ्चालन गरेको ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ कार्यक्रमको पहिलो चरण सफलतापूर्वक सम्पन्न गरेको छ ।

कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत काठमाडौंमा आयोजित प्रमाणपत्र वितरण समारोहमा तीन महिनाको प्रशिक्षण पूरा गरेका १० जना महिलालाई सम्मान गरिएको छ । सुरक्षित र आत्मनिर्भर रूपमा दुईपाङ्ग्रे सवारी चलाउने पेसामा अघि बढ्न आवश्यक सीप, आत्मविश्वास र स्रोतसाधन प्रदान गर्ने उद्देश्यले सहभागीहरूलाई विभिन्न चरणमा प्रशिक्षण दिइएको थियो ।

अप्रिल २०२६ मा सुरु भएको ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ कार्यक्रम विशेषगरी अवसरबाट वञ्चित समुदायका महिलालाई मोबिलिटी क्षेत्रमा आर्थिक अवसरमा पहुँच दिलाउने उद्देश्यले सञ्चालन गरिएको हो । महिलालाई परम्परागत रूपमा पुरुषको वर्चस्व रहेको पेसामा प्रवेश गर्न बाधा पु¥याउने सामाजिक तथा व्यावहारिक अवरोधलाई कम गर्न पनि कार्यक्रमले जोड दिएको छ ।

प्रशिक्षण अवधिभर सडक सुरक्षालाई व्यावसायिक दक्षताको महत्वपूर्ण पक्षका रूपमा समेटिएको थियो । सहभागीहरूलाई व्यावहारिक राइडिङ प्रशिक्षणसँगै सडक सुरक्षासम्बन्धी मार्गदर्शन प्रदान गर्नुका साथै औपचारिक सवारी चालक अनुमतिपत्र (लाइसेन्स) प्राप्त गर्ने प्रक्रियामा समेत सहयोग गरिएको थियो ।

प्रत्येक सहभागीलाई सुरक्षात्मक हेल्मेट तथा प्राथमिक उपचार र स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी सामग्रीसहितको सुरक्षा किट प्रदान गरिएको थियो ।

व्यक्तिगत सुरक्षालाई पनि प्रशिक्षणको छुट्टै महत्वपूर्ण पक्षका रूपमा समेटिएको थियो । फाइटब्याक नेपाल सँगको सहकार्यमा उन्नत आत्मरक्षा तालिम सञ्चालन गरिएको थियो, जसले सहभागीहरूलाई सम्भावित सुरक्षा चुनौती पहिचान गर्न, आत्मविश्वास बढाउन र आवश्यक अवस्थामा व्यवहारिक रूपमा सामना गर्न सक्ने सीप विकास गर्न सहयोग गरेको थियो ।

काठमाडौं उपत्यका ट्राफिक प्रहरी कार्यालयका डीएसपी सुनिलजंग शाहले भने, “सडक सुरक्षा सबैको साझा जिम्मेवारी हो र यसमा प्रत्येक चालकको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका हुन्छ । हामी सहभागीहरूलाई ट्राफिक नियमको पालना गर्न, सडकमा सधैं सचेत रहन र अनुभव बढाउँदै निरन्तर सिकिरहन आग्रह गर्छौं । सबै सहभागीलाई बधाई दिँदै व्यावसायिक चालकका रूपमा उनीहरूको सुरक्षित र सफल यात्राका लागि शुभकामना व्यक्त गर्दछौं ।”

मोबिलिटीमा महिलाको पहुँच विस्तार यस समूहका महिलाका लागि सवारी चालक अनुमतिपत्र केवल आम्दानीको माध्यम मात्र नभई आफ्नो काम, शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य सेवा तथा बजारसम्म आफ्नै समयअनुसार स्वतन्त्र रूपमा पुग्ने अवसर पनि हो । यसले सार्वजनिक यातायातको समयतालिका वा परिवारका अन्य सदस्यमा निर्भर रहनुपर्ने अवस्थालाई कम गर्न सहयोग पु¥याउँछ ।

दुईपाङ्ग्रे सवारीमा आधारित राइड–हेलिङ सेवाले चारपाङ्ग्रे सवारी पुग्न कठिन हुने साँघुरा गल्ली तथा अन्तिम गन्तव्यसम्म पनि सेवा पु¥याउन सक्छ । सामान्यतया यसको भाडा पनि चारपाङ्ग्रे सवारीको तुलनामा कम हुने गर्दछ । राइड–हेलिङ सेवामा महिलाको सहभागिता बढ्दा यात्रुहरूले आफूलाई उपयुक्त चालक छनोट गर्ने थप अवसरसमेत पाउनेछन् ।

प्रमाणपत्र वितरण समारोह प्रमाणपत्र वितरण समारोहमा साझेदार संस्थाका प्रतिनिधि, सरकारी निकायका सरोकारवाला, सञ्चारकर्मी तथा विशिष्ट अतिथिहरूको सहभागिता रहेको थियो ।

समारोहमा इनड्राइभका प्रतिनिधि तथा इनड्राइभ नेपालकी ब्रान्ड एम्बेसडर स्वस्तिमा खड्काले कार्यक्रम सफलतापूर्वक सम्पन्न गरेका १० जना सहभागीलाई प्रमाणपत्र, सुरक्षा किट तथा मायाको चिनो प्रदान गरे । कार्यक्रममा सहभागी १० जना महिलाको ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ यात्रालाई समेटिएको भिडियोसमेत प्रदर्शन गरिएको थियो ।

समारोहका क्रममा सहभागीमध्ये एक जनालाई विद्युतीय स्कुटर, तीन जनालाई स्मार्टफोन र छ जनालाई स्मार्टवाच प्रदान गरिएको थियो । यी सामग्रीले उनीहरूलाई व्यावसायिक ड्राइभिङ यात्राको सुरुवातमा थप सहयोग पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ ।

इनड्राइभ साउथ एसियाकि कम्युनिकेसन म्यनाजर शेरिन एर्विना कौरले भनिन्, “हामीले विभिन्न बजारमा एउटै अवस्था देखिरहेका छौं, राइड माग्ने यात्रुमध्ये धेरै महिला छन्, तर उनीहरूलाई राइड दिने चालकमा महिलाको संख्या निकै कम छ । यो महिलाले यस्तो काम गर्न चाहन्छन् कि चाहँदैनन् भन्ने विषय थिएन। मुख्य प्रश्न उनीहरूका लागि यो पेसामा प्रवेश गर्ने बाटो उपलब्ध थियो कि थिएन भन्ने थियो । नेपालमा सञ्चालन गरिएको पहिलो समूहले तालिम, लाइसेन्स र प्लेटफर्ममा पहुँचलाई एउटै यात्राका रूपमा जोड्दा कस्तो परिवर्तन सम्भव हुन्छ भन्ने देखाएको छ। हामी अन्य बजारमा पनि यसबाट सिक्दै कार्यक्रमलाई अघि बढाउनेछौं ।”

इनड्राइभ नेपालकी कम्युनिकेसन्स म्यानेजर मञ्जिता गुरुङले भनिन्, “सीप विकास तालिम यस यात्राको एउटा हिस्सा मात्र हो । सामाजिक सोच र धारणाले पनि उत्तिकै महत्व राख्छ, र महिलाले ड्राइभिङ सुरु गरेपछि उनी प्रवेश गर्ने वातावरण पनि महत्वपूर्ण हुन्छ । ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ महिलालाई लाइसेन्स प्राप्त गर्नेदेखि आत्मविश्वास विकास गर्ने, परिवारमा यसबारे संवाद गर्ने र आम्दानीको अवसर सिर्जना गर्नेसम्म हरेक पक्षमा सहयोग गर्ने गरी तयार गरिएको हो । जब धेरै महिलाहरू यो पेसामा आउँछन्, यात्रुहरूले पनि लाभ पाउँछन्, उनीहरूसँग आफूलाई राइड गराउने चालक छनोट गर्ने थप विकल्प हुन्छ ।”

इनड्राइभ नेपालकी सिनियर ड्राइभर अपरेसन्स स्पेसलिस्ट सुनिता जीमी राईले भनिन्, “इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ महिलाका लागि थप सहयोगी वातावरण निर्माण गर्ने दिशामा महत्वपूर्ण कदम हो । जब धेरै महिलाहरूले सवारीको स्टेयरिङ समाउँछन्, उनीहरूले नेपाललाई थप समावेशी भविष्यतर्फ अघि बढाउन पनि भूमिका खेलिरहेका हुन्छन् ।”

इनड्राइभ नेपालकी ब्रान्ड एम्बेसडर स्वस्तिमा खड्काले भनिन्, “‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ ले अन्यायलाई चुनौती दिँदै समुदायमा सकारात्मक परिवर्तन ल्याउने इनड्राइभको प्रतिबद्धतालाई प्रतिबिम्बित गर्छ । मानिस र समानतालाई केन्द्रमा राखेर अघि बढाइएको यस पहलको हिस्सा बन्न पाउँदा म गर्व गर्छु ।”

articles.title: पार्टी निर्माणमा सि जिनपिङको अवधारणाबारे नेपालमा चर्चा
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालसहित विश्वमा राजनीतिक दलको निर्माण र त्यसको प्रभावकारी संचालनका लागि चिनियाँ राष्ट्रपति सि जिनपिङको अवधारणा उपयोगी हुने विज्ञहरुले बताएका छन् । फ्रेन्डस अन क्लाउडले काठमाडौंमा गरेको कार्यक्रममा राजनीतिज्ञ जगन्नाथ खतिवडा, परराष्ट्रविद डा गोपाल खनाल, पूर्व राजदूत महेशराज दाहाल, अनुसन्धानकर्ता डा। दीपक देवकोटा र क्लाउडका अध्यक्ष शोभित उप्रेतीले पार्टी निर्माणमा राष्ट्रपति सी का विभिन्न आयामबारे धारणा राखेका हुन् ।

कार्यक्रममा बो्ल्दै पूर्व राजदूत दाहालले राष्ट्रपति सिको अध्ययनशिल बानी नै पार्टी र राष्ट्र निर्माणका लागि आधारशिला बनेको उल्ले गरे ।

दाहालका अनुसार श्रम शिविरमा हुँदा पनि निकै अध्धयन गर्ने सी लामो र नयाँ सोचका थिए । सृजनशीलता परिवर्तनकारी सोचका धनी सीले पार्टी सदसयता पाउन पनि निकै संघर्ष गरेकाले पार्टी कस्तो हुनुपर्छ भन्ने पनि उनले राम्रोसँग बुझेका थिए ।

राम्रो दृष्टिकोण भए पार्टी र देश बन्छ भन्ने कुरा उनले प्रमाणित गरेर देखाए । भ्रष्टाचार विरुद्वका कार्यक्रम र दल भित्रको शुद्वतामा उनको जोड थियो । नेतृत्वको जिम्मेवारी र कर्तव्य । प्रविधि विकास, जनताको सहभागीता, विज्ञानमा लगानी उनको पार्टी निर्माणका प्रमुख साधन हुन ।

यस्तै , डा दिपक देवकोटाले राष्ट्रपति सीले राज्यबाट डर नभई भरोसा जगाउने काम गरेर सफलता प्राप्त गरेको धारणा राखे । जनतालाई केन्द्रमा राखेर पार्टी र देश निर्माण गर्न उनी सफल भए ।

जनताले विश्वास गर्ने पार्टी बनाउन राष्ट्रपति सी ले सुशासन र सुरक्षालाई प्राथमिकता दिएको उनले बताए । परराष्ट्र विद डा गोपाल खनालले विश्वव्यापी सुशासन अभियान र नयाँ युगका लागि चिनियाँ विशेषतासहितको समाजवाद नै सि जिनपिङको पार्टी निर्माणको स्पष्ट अवधारणा भएको बताए ।

पार्टी नियम र देश कानुनबाट चल्छ भन्ने कुरा राष्ट्रपति सी ले स्थापित गरेको उनको भनाइ छ । जनतालाई विकास दिने सोच नै सिको सोच भएको खनालको निष्कर्ष छ।

आर्थिक अनियमितता गर्ने ७० लाख भन्दा बढीलाई चीनमा कारबाही गरिएको जानकारी दिंदै खनालले राष्ट्रपति सी को सुशासन अभियानको प्रशंसा गरे ।

नेता जगन्नाथ खतिवडाले अनुशासन, अनुगमन र आत्मसमीक्षाको सुत्र न‌ै राष्ट्रपति सि को पार्टी र देश निर्माणको आधारशिला रहेको धारणा राखे ।

राष्ट्रपति सि ले विचार निर्माण, राजनीति निर्माण र संगठन निर्माणमा जोड दिंदै पार्टीमा गुणस्तरीय सदस्यलाई मात्र स्थान दिएको खतिवडाले बताए । चीन जस्तो शक्तिशाली राष्ट्र हाम्रो छिमेकी भएकाले दलीय एकता तथा दीर्घकालीन सोच र योजनाका साथ अघि बढ्ने कुरा नेपालले सिक्नुपर्ने खतिवडा बताउँछन् ।

articles.title: ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंकमा नागरिक एपबाटै खाता खोल्न सकिने
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंक लिमिटेडले नागरिक एपसँगको सहकार्यमा नागरिक एपमार्फतै बैंक खाता खोल्न सकिने नयाँ सुविधा सुरु गरेको छ ।

राष्ट्रिय परिचयपत्रका आधारमा नागरिक एपमा आबद्ध नेपाली नागरिकले बैंकको वेबसाइटमा उपलब्ध क्यूआर कोड स्क्यान गरी व्यक्तिगत बचत खाता अनलाइनबाटै खोल्न सक्नेछन् ।

यो सेवा १८ वर्ष वा सोभन्दा माथिका राष्ट्रिय परिचयपत्र भएका तथा नागरिक एपमा आबद्ध व्यक्तिका लागि उपलब्ध हुनेछ । खाता खोल्ने क्रममा बैंकले ग्राहकको पूर्वसहमतिमा आवश्यक व्यक्तिगत विवरण नागरिक एपबाट सुरक्षित रूपमा प्राप्त गर्ने भएकाले पुनः विवरण भर्नुपर्ने झन्झट हट्ने, गोपनीयता कायम रहने र सूचनाको सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित हुने बैंकले जनाएको छ ।

नागरिक एपमार्फत खोलिएको खाता सञ्चालनका लागि भने ग्राहकले नजिकको शाखामा गई वा भिडियो केवाईसीमार्फत प्रमाणीकरण गर्नुपर्नेछ ।

बैंकका अनुसार सरकारी डिजिटल पूर्वाधारको उपयोग गर्दै सुरु गरिएको यो सेवाले खाता खोल्ने प्रक्रियालाई थप सहज, सुरक्षित, पारदर्शी र प्रविधिमैत्री बनाउनेछ । ग्राहकलाई आधुनिक डिजिटल बैंकिङ अनुभव प्रदान गर्ने विश्वास बैंकको छ ।

ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंक ७७ वटै जिल्लामा शाखा सञ्जाल विस्तार गर्ने निजी क्षेत्रको पहिलो वाणिज्य बैंक हो ।

हाल बैंकले ३४२ शाखा, ३६८ एटिएम, १४७ शाखारहित बैंकिङ सेवा, ६९ एक्सटेन्सन तथा राजस्व सङ्कलन काउन्टर र ३ वटा वैदेशिक प्रतिनिधि कार्यालयसहित १ हजारभन्दा बढी सेवा केन्द्रमार्फत सेवा दिँदै आएको छ ।

articles.title: मेलम्चीमा स्थानीय उत्पादन प्रवर्द्धनका लागि ‘कोशेली घर’ उद्घाटन
articles.summary:
मेलम्ची । स्थानीय कृषि र हस्तकला उत्पादनलाई प्रवर्द्धन गर्ने उद्देश्यले सिन्धुपाल्चोकको मेलम्ची बजारमा नयाँ व्यावसायिक केन्द्र “कोशेली घर” सञ्चालनमा आएको छ। साउन ८ देखि हरेक दिन बिहान ७ बजेदेखि राति ७ बजेसम्म खुल्ने यो कोशेलीघरको उद्घाटन नगरप्रमुख आइतमान तामाङले गरेका छन् ।

नगरप्रमुख तामाङले कोशेलीघरबाट ताजा फलफूल तथा तरकारी, घरेलु अचार, मह, भान्साका आवश्यक परिकार, हस्तकला सामग्री, अण्डा, माछा, गेडागुडी, चिया, कफी तथा हर्बल सामग्रीलगायत स्थानीय रैथाने उत्पादनको सीधा बिक्री वितरणमा जोड दिने बताए । उनले यहाँ राखिने विशेष परिकार तथा उत्पादनहरू आवश्यक परेमा जिल्ला बाहिर पनि पठाइने समेत जनाए ।

कोशेलीघरले स्थानीय उत्पादक र उपभोक्तालाई एउटै छानामुनि प्रत्यक्ष भेटघाटको व्यवस्था गराउँदै बजारसम्म पहुँच सहज बनाउने लक्ष्य लिएको प्रमुख तामाङले बताए ।

साथै प्रमुख प्रशासकीय अधिकृत निमेष मिश्रले ‘फार्म देखि किचनसम्म अवधारणाअनुरूप उत्पादक र उपभोक्ताको मागअनुसार नयाँ वस्तु तथा उत्पादनहरू परिष्कृत गरी सार्वजनिक गरिने र उद्यमीहरूको भेटघाट हुने उपयुक्त स्थलको रूपमा यसलाई विकास गर्ने योजना रहेको बताए । प्रारम्भिक अनुमान अनुसार नगरपालिकाले दैनिक हजारौंले यहाँबाट किनमेल गर्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

मेलम्ची आसपासका सरकारी तथा निजी कार्यालयका कर्मचारी, घुम्न आउने पर्यटक, स्थानीय टोल तथा छिमेकी पालिकाका बासिन्दाहरू प्रमुख लक्षित ग्राहक रहने कोशेलीघरबाट स्थानिय रोजगारी र व्यवसायिक गतिविधिलाई थप सक्रिय बनाउन मद्दत पुग्ने उपस्थित उपभोक्ताले विश्वास व्यक्त गरिएको थियो ।

articles.title: Madhesh tensions ease after all-party talks, heightened security
articles.summary:
Tensions across parts of Madhesh and Koshi provinces have begun to ease following a series of all-party meetings involving senior political leaders, local administrations, civil society representatives, religious leaders and community elders, backed by a heightened security presence in sensitive areas.

Security forces remain on alert after several days of unrest triggered by local communal disputes that spread to multiple districts. Curfews remain in force in parts of Sunsari, Siraha, Saptari and Dhanusha, while the District Administration Office has continued restrictions on public gatherings and demonstrations in Parsa.

The Nepali Army has been deployed alongside reinforced contingents of the Nepal Police and the Armed Police Force to maintain order. Nepal Police Headquarters has also dispatched senior officers to Koshi and Madhesh provinces to oversee security operations and coordinate the response.

Deputy Inspector General Abi Narayan Kafle, central spokesperson of police, noted that the situation across the Tarai is gradually returning to normal following appeals for calm from political leaders and peace initiatives led by local administrations and community groups.

“We have taken 38 people into custody from various locations in Koshi and Madhesh provinces on charges of disturbing public order, spreading inflammatory content and attempting to incite communal discord,” said Kafle, who is stationed in Saptari to supervise security operations.

He said plainclothes personnel have been deployed in sensitive areas for round-the-clock surveillance, while drones are being used to monitor large gatherings and identify potential security risks.

Kafle said the situation improved after Home Minister Sudan Gurung visited Sunsari and Siraha where he held talks with victims’ families and community representatives, leading to agreements late on Thursday.

Amid the heightened security measures, Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Friday convened a meeting at the Prime Minister’s Office with lawmakers from the Rastriya Swatantra Party and other elected representatives from the Tarai-Madhesh region to discuss the government’s response.

According to participants, the prime minister said the government’s immediate priority was to provide relief to affected families, ensure public safety and conduct an impartial investigation into the incidents.

“The government has adopted a comprehensive approach to maintain law and order, protect vulnerable communities and prevent any further escalation,” Shah told the meeting. He also urged lawmakers to return to their constituencies and help strengthen trust between local communities and the state.

Before meeting lawmakers, Shah held separate consultations with leaders representing Madhesh-based parties. Those attending included Janamat Party chair CK Raut, Janata Samajbadi Party Nepal leaders Upendra Yadav and Mahantha Thakur, Rastriya Mukti Party Nepal leader Rajendra Mahato, Rastriya Nirman Dal chief Samim Miya Ansari, and lawmakers Prabhu Sah, Amaresh Kumar Singh and Sharat Singh Bhandari.

The discussions focused on measures to maintain public order and prevent similar incidents in the future.

After the meeting, CK Raut said the government should establish permanent district-level mechanisms for dialogue instead of responding only after violence erupts. He proposed creating local religious and civic councils comprising faith leaders, youth representatives and respected community members to hold regular discussions aimed at preventing tensions.

“In every community there are individuals capable of provoking conflict. We need preventive measures at the local level before such incidents escalate,” Raut said.

Rajendra Mahato said lasting peace would require both effective policing and sustained political commitment to address underlying grievances.

Samim Miya Ansari, however, questioned the government’s initial response, saying the home minister’s visit to Sunsari came several days after the first incidents were reported.

“We spent more than two hours discussing the situation with the prime minister. It is concerning when a local dispute develops into wider communal unrest,” Ansari said. “There is a public perception that the state did not respond decisively during the initial phase of the crisis.”

The developments also prompted concern from the country’s highest constitutional offices.

President Ramchandra Paudel held consultations at Sheetal Niwas with former President Ram Baran Yadav and former Vice President Paramananda Jha on the situation in Tarai.

The meeting focused on ways to ease communal tensions, strengthen social harmony and preserve national unity. Speaking to reporters afterwards, Yadav said security measures alone would not resolve the crisis and urged the government to build trust with political parties, civil society and local communities through dialogue.

National Assembly chair Narayan Prasad Dahal also expressed concern over growing polarisation and appealed to all sections of society to uphold Nepal’s tradition of religious tolerance and social harmony.

Nepali Congress president Gagan Thapa on Friday held a meeting with party leaders, mayors and provincial assembly members from Koshi and Madhesh provinces, urging them to help prevent the spread of misinformation.

“Misinformation can cause irreversible harm before it is exposed,” Thapa said, urging citizens to verify information through official sources before sharing or reacting to content on social media.

He also called on party workers to help defuse tensions.

“Regardless of how the incidents began, our collective responsibility is to restore peace through restraint, dialogue and mutual trust,” he said.

While political leaders met in Kathmandu, local administrations, religious leaders, business organisations and community groups stepped up peace-building efforts in several districts.

In Panchthar, local residents gathered at the Sumhalung Temple in Phidim Municipality to release doves as a symbolic appeal for peace and communal harmony.

In Biratnagar, political parties, civil society groups and local organisations organised a peace march that passed through the city’s main streets.

“Only dialogue, respect for the law and mutual trust can restore normalcy,” said Wasim Alam, one of the participants.

In Parsa, the Birgunj Chamber of Commerce and Industry appealed for calm, warning that prolonged unrest was disrupting businesses and daily life. It urged all sides to resolve differences through dialogue and safeguard Nepal’s social harmony.

Chamber president Hari Prasad Gautam said curfews and violence had affected trade, businesses and supply chains, adding that stability was essential for economic activity to resume.

Authorities also intensified local coordination efforts in districts that have remained peaceful but are considered sensitive.

In Rautahat, Chief District Officer Dinesh Sagar Bhusal chaired an all-party meeting attended by local representatives, security officials and civil society members. Participants agreed to strengthen coordination to preserve communal harmony and take legal action against anyone attempting to disturb public order.

In Saptari’s Khadak Municipality, Rastriya Swatantra Party lawmaker Sitaram Sah led a goodwill march through Kalyanpur market, where participants carrying banners promoting harmony urged people of all communities to maintain peaceful coexistence.

At Lumbini, Buddhist monks from the Theravada and Mahayana traditions gathered at the Mayadevi Temple to offer joint prayers for peace. Organised by the Lumbini Development Trust, the gathering called for non-violence, reconciliation and peaceful resolution of disputes.

In Banke, Chief District Officer Dil Kumar Tamang convened an all-party security meeting in Nepalgunj, where participants agreed to organise a social harmony march on Saturday.

The district administration also banned the use of high-volume sound boxes in public places and prohibited the display of weapons or objects that could be used as weapons during religious and public processions.

With political outreach continuing in Kathmandu and reconciliation efforts gathering pace in affected districts, authorities say their immediate priority is to maintain public order and strengthen confidence among communities as normal life gradually returns across the southern plains.

articles.title: National ID authentication failures disrupt public services
articles.summary:
Widespread technical glitches have affected 13 government agencies integrated with the National Identity Management Information System (NIDMIS) since early July. The disruptions have made it difficult for people to access government services linked to the national identity card.

Officials have urged the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Department of National ID and Civil Registration to resolve the problem as soon as possible, saying continued disruptions could delay services and cause inconvenience to the public.

In a statement issued on Monday, the Department of National ID and Civil Registration said it had observed that, over the past several days, people enrolling for the national identity card through NIDMIS had been issued National Identity Numbers (NINs), but their records were not being authenticated or approved by the system.

“As a result, service recipients have submitted complaints to the department, stating that they are facing difficulties obtaining services from 13 different organisations, including the Department of Passports, several private banks and offices,” the statement said.

Krishna Poudel, director general of the Department of National ID and Civil Registration, told the Post that the department’s information technology team had been working to resolve the issue for the past week with technical support from the France-based vendor IN Groupe.

IN Groupe had earlier provided the NIDMIS and the Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) to the department. The government recently decided to procure 10 million ABIS licences from the same company.

The problem was first noticed around a month ago, but had not been resolved as of Friday. Two senior officials at government agencies whose services are linked to NIDMIS told the Post that they were increasingly frustrated by the delay in fixing the problem and had repeatedly raised the issue with the Department of National Identity and Civil Registration.

The technical glitches have also raised questions about the future management of NIDMIS after the government, on May 8, cancelled a global tender for the operation, maintenance and technical support of the system. The government instead decided to manage the system in-house (by the department itself) despite concerns over its technical capacity and growing delays in issuing national identity cards.

The decision marked a significant shift in the management of one of the country’s largest digital infrastructure projects. Since the rollout of the national identity card programme, critical functions—including biometric enrolment, data storage, system maintenance and card printing—have relied heavily on foreign technology providers.

The international tender was published on December 17, 2025. Three international firms submitted bids: Gravity Group IND LLC of Dubai, Iris Corporation of Malaysia and In Smart Identity France SAS.

The cancellation also came as Prime Minister Balendra Shah's administration moved to centralise information technology and digital governance. The government is preparing to establish an Information Technology and Electronic Governance Office under the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, alongside the newly created Ministry of Science, Technology, and Innovation.

However, the policy shift has coincided with growing operational challenges that have sharply reduced the department's capacity to issue national identity cards.

Soon after the tender was cancelled, a technician warned that the department lacked the expertise needed to restore the system in the event of a major technical failure.

The slowdown has significantly increased the backlog in card production.

According to department data, biometric information has been collected from around 20 million people across Nepal. However, only 7.8 million national identity cards have been printed so far and millions of applicants are waiting for their cards.

Following the cancellation of the tender, the department has continued to receive technical support from its previous vendor, IN Groupe. The government plans to take full control of the system with support from the Prime Minister’s Office. However, officials have yet to explain how the system will be managed or how uninterrupted services will be ensured.

Poudel said that while applications for national identity cards were continuing to be enrolled, the authentication of records had become more complicated, particularly for people who applied after July 1.

“Our system has been unable to verify the data updated in the system,” he said.

The department has requested the agencies integrated with NIDMIS to continue providing services by accepting the confirmation page currently available through the system as proof of an individual’s enrollment until the system is fully functional and the authentication problem is resolved.

IN Groupe has sent a team of IT professionals to Kathmandu and has begun restoring the system, an official at the Prime Minister’s Office said. “We expect services to be fully restored next week,” the official told the Post.

The affected agencies include the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology; the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Transport of Bagmati province; Medical Education Commission; Department of Passports; Department of Transport Management; National Information Centre; Inland Revenue Department; Department of Immigration; Department of Land Management and Archives; Nepal Telecommunications Authority; Social Security Fund; Credit Information Centre; Department of National Personnel Records (Civil Service); Nepal Rastra Bank; the Pension Management Office; and the Office of the Company Registrar.

“We have deployed 12 information technology professionals to the Department of Passports to facilitate services, including authentication,” Poudel said.

After the South Korean government opened vacancies of 7,800 people for language tests for the Employment Permit System, the Department of Passports has witnessed a sharp rise in applicants. Prospective workers cannot apply without a valid passport, while an NID number is required to apply for a passport.

“It is true that there is a problem with the NIDMIS service. We are doing our best to resolve the issue,” he said.

“Banks have made it mandatory for customers to update their KYC records with their national identity number. The same number is also required for passport-related services. The ongoing authentication problem has delayed services at banks and the Department of Passports.”

Poudel said the department should not be blamed for the crowds at the Department of Passports and other government offices, adding that technical teams were working intensively to resolve the problem.

“After several agencies were unable to verify data through our system, we urged them to continue providing services by accepting the confirmation page,” he said. “Our team is working intensively on the issue, and we have repeatedly informed the agencies concerned about the situation.”

Poudel said applicants who enrolled before July 1 had not faced the problem, but those who applied after that date were experiencing difficulties.

The delays are becoming increasingly significant as the government expands the mandatory use of the national identity card.

The card is now required—or being made mandatory in phases—for a growing range of public services, including obtaining passports, citizenship certificates, and driving licences; receiving social security allowances; accessing banking services; registering for Permanent Account Number; insurance services; carrying out property transactions; and sitting university entrance examinations.

As more government services become linked to the national identity system, delays in printing and distributing cards could affect millions of citizens who need them to access essential public services.

While the government argues that bringing the system under domestic management will strengthen national control over sensitive data and reduce long-term dependence on foreign contractors, officials and technical staff within the department remain concerned about whether it has sufficient expertise and resources to manage the system without causing further disruptions.

articles.title: As demand for human milk grows, ministry to operate van for collecting surplus from mothers at home
articles.summary:
In a bid to address a growing demand for human breast milk from maternity and children’s hospitals, the Ministry of Health and Food Safety is preparing to mobilise a van in the Kathmandu valley to collect breast milk from mothers with a surplus.

Officials say that a specialised mobile unit is dispatched by a human milk bank for safe transport, to visit donors at home and to transport fresh or frozen expressed breast milk under cold-chain storage conditions to the human milk bank run by the Paropakar Maternity and Women’s Hospital, Thapathali.

“Demand for human milk for newborns is much higher than the collection,” said Lila Bikram Thapa, chief of the Nutrition Section at the Family Welfare Division of the Department of Health Services. “Since it is impractical for new mothers to travel a long distance to the hospital to donate milk, we have introduced the concept of a human milk bank.”

Officials say that the United Nations Children’s Fund will provide a state-of-the art vehicle for collecting human milk to operationalise the service within two months. With the financial and technical assistance of the UN agency, the Thapathali hospital has been operating a human milk bank since August, 2022.

The hospital administration said that demand for breast milk is very high and the bank has not been able to supply to vulnerable infants as per the demands.

“Vulnerable infants, whose mothers are sick or died after giving birth or their breasts do not yield milk or critically ill newborns in neonatal intensive care units, premature babies with low birth weights need breast milk supplement,” Dr Sailendra Bir Karmacharya, a senior consultant paediatrician at the hospital.

“Since demand is excessively high and collection is low, we have been prioritising the infants as per the low weight and those critically ill to provide breast milk.”

Around 300 infants are admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit of the Thapathali hospital every month, and most of those infants require breast milk. Apart from that, several other hospitals in the Valley, including Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, Patan Hospital, and several other community and private hospitals, also seek breast milk at the bank for ailing and underweight infants.

Doctors say breast milk is collected mainly from mothers of ailing babies who are unable to breastfeed their infants admitted to intensive care units, as well as from mothers with an excess milk supply who wish to donate their surplus. The milk is then tested, pasteurised, and stored at minus 40 degrees Celsius.

Every day, 60 to 80 women deliver babies at the Maternity Hospital, which is the main source of breast milk collection. As most of the normal new mothers get discharged within a day or two, the bank cannot collect milk from such mothers.

“As breast milk cannot be manufactured, some new mothers have to donate it, and new mothers with surplus breast milk cannot visit the hospital for donation,” said Karmacharya. “So we have been preparing to operate a human breast milk collection van so that we can collect more.”

The hospital itself needs 1.5 to 2.5 litres of breast milk for babies admitted to the intensive care unit every day.

Doctors say human milk helps in reducing necrotising enterocolitis (NEC), a serious gastrointestinal problem that mostly affects premature babies.

Health officials say that the van will make rounds of all three districts of the Valley—Kathmandu, Lalitpur and Bhaktapur—to collect breast milk from mothers who are willing to donate their surplus.

Collected milk will be stored at the bank and can be used for six months, they say.

Doctors say human breast milk is the best source of nutrition and ensures the survival and healthy growth of babies. It bolsters brain development and has lifelong benefits for both the baby and the mother.

The human milk bank, launched in August 2022, aims to reduce neonatal deaths, which remain constantly high. The Ministry of Health and Food Safety has launched various programmes, including hiring staff nurses to promote exclusive breastfeeding. Exclusive breastfeeding has the potential to prevent 13 percent of under-five deaths, according to doctors.

A recent Nepal Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey carried out by the National Statistics Office in partnership with UNICEF shows that neonatal deaths are still 17 per 1,000 live births. The global target for Sustainable Development Goals is to reduce neonatal mortality to 12 deaths for every 1,000 live births by 2030.

The SDGs, a follow-up on the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs), aim to end poverty, hunger, and all forms of inequality in the world by 2030. Nepal has committed to meeting the goals.

articles.title: World awaits status of missing climbers, including Nirmal Purja
articles.summary:
Rescue teams on Pakistan’s Broad Peak located six additional climbers by drone late Friday, a day after an avalanche swept away a 10-member climbing team that included Nirmal Purja, the Nepali mountaineer known as “Nimsdai”.

The discovery brings to nine the number of climbers who have either been found or sighted, more than 30 hours after the Thursday morning avalanche, though Pakistani authorities had not released full identifications by Friday evening. The condition of the tenth climber remained unknown.

Three bodies had already been recovered earlier Friday by a ground and helicopter operation: Nepali climber Pur Bahadur Gurung, Omani climber Nadhira Al Harthy, found intact, and a single leg belonging to American climber Mallory Geis. The six additional climbers located by drone late Friday afternoon had not been identified as of late Friday evening.

Among those whose status is unknown is Purja, one of the most recognisable figures in modern mountaineering, who completed a self-described Project Possible in 2019. He climbed all 14 of the world’s eight-thousanders in six months and six days, shattering a previous record by more than seven years.

The avalanche struck Purja and his team around 9 am on Thursday at roughly 6,600 metres, between Camp 2 and Camp 3, as they pushed towards the summit of the 8,051-metre peak, the world’s 12th-highest mountain, in Pakistan’s Karakoram range. The climbers included six Nepalis and four foreign climbers, drawn from several expedition outfits: three from Seven Summit Treks, three from Purja’s own team, two from Imagine Nepal, and one each from Pakistan and the United States, according to Thaneshwar Guragain, Seven Summit Treks’ general manager. The climbers had radioed base camp that morning to say they were heading up. No alarm was raised until evening, when the team remained out of contact.

The first sign that something had gone wrong came from GPS tracking data, according to Changdawa Sherpa, an expedition leader with Seven Summit Treks who has been coordinating the search from Pakistan. “The GPS track showed people coming straight down from above 7,000 metres,” he told the Post. “That’s when I understood the situation wasn’t good.”

A tracking device carried by Purja himself had continued to show movement until Friday morning. Purja’s location appeared to shift downhill immediately after the avalanche.

By the time Changdawa was alerted, around 9 pm on Thursday, it was too dark to mount a rescue operation. Search teams resumed at first light Friday, with a Nepali guide and local Pakistani staff hiking roughly 90 minutes from base camp to reach the site, where they recovered the first two bodies by mid-morning. A Pakistani Army helicopter later ferried the bodies down for transport to hospital.

Rescue operations in Pakistan have moved more slowly than they typically would in Nepal, Guragain said, since they are run mainly by the military rather than the immediate private helicopter response Nepal allows. Helicopters on Broad Peak are limited and subject to lengthy clearance procedures, meaning an effective rescue could not proceed until weather cooperated. Asked about the odds of finding the missing climbers alive, Guragain said hope was narrowing sharply.

The search stalled through the middle of the day as poor visibility limited aerial searching. It resumed in the afternoon when a Chinese climbing team on a nearby K2 expedition, led by Mingma G Sherpa of Imagine Nepal, flew a drone over the debris field. Within hours, the drone had located six more climbers — four in a rough line and two nearby, according to Changdawa, who said he was able to identify two of his own company’s Sherpas by their clothing from the drone images.

Recovering the climbers spotted by drone will likely require lowering rescuers from a helicopter on a long line, a high-risk operation given the terrain and thin infrastructure on the mountain. Unlike Everest, Broad Peak has no permanent camps or communication relays above base camp and this has slowed both the search and the flow of reliable information, Changdawa said. “It’s not like Everest,” he said. “Communication out there is very limited.”

Pakistani authorities deployed army personnel, helicopters, drones and ground crews to the mountain starting Friday morning, while Nepal's government said its Foreign Ministry, tourism authorities and embassy in Islamabad were coordinating with Pakistani counterparts. The Alpine Club of Pakistan, in a statement, called the initial reports of the avalanche “deeply concerning” and said the governments of Nepal and Pakistan are both engaged in the mission to support the search and rescue operation. Seven Summit Treks has since called off its remaining expeditions on both Broad Peak and K2. “It wouldn’t be right to take on further risk after an accident this large,” Changdawa said.

Additional Sherpas were expected to gather at Broad Peak on Saturday to assist local teams with the recovery operation, Changdawa said, adding that avalanche deaths on Broad Peak have historically involved one or two climbers at a time. “Losing an entire team like this at once — this is the first time we've seen anything like it,” he said.

articles.title: The parliament that cannot question its prime minister
articles.summary:
Late night on Tuesday, India’s Congress MP Shashi Tharoor stood up in the Lok Sabha with nine minutes on the clock. The bill under debate was India’s anti-paper-leak law. Tharoor’s point was engaging and harder to dismiss: the country’s public examination system needs structural reform that prevents leaks, rather than relying only on harsher punishment once the damage is done. Right then his mic was cut and the House moved to other business. But it didn’t really matter. Tharoor had built the argument anyway, on the record, in the shape a policy debate is supposed to take and it was covered widely in the Indian media.

The next afternoon, in the same chamber, opposition leader Rahul Gandhi produced a different kind of moment. Defending the nationwide student protests over the paper leak as a peaceful expression of youthful aspiration, he recounted a conversation with an eighteen-year-old who’d sorted people into three categories: students, idiots, and andhbhakts who follow the idiots. The side of parliament where ruling party MPs and ministers sit erupted. One of the ministers rose to demand that the word “idiot” be struck from the record as unparliamentary. Speaker Om Birla had to intervene repeatedly just to restore order.

The two instances, to outsiders and those in the ruling benches, may appear lacking in discipline. But this is what a parliamentary system actually looks like — those in the ruling segment can’t ignore the people arguing with it.

Go further out West and this model gets sharper. In the UK, British Prime Minister’s Questions is a much mocked ritual, one that has now outlasted seven different prime ministers just in the past decade. The thirty minutes of unscripted, grandiose session produces more heat than information. But beneath the mockery is a format that forces accountability. In April, Commons Speaker Lindsay Hoyle stopped Prime Minister Keir Starmer mid-session and told him plainly that it was Prime Minister’s Questions, not a chance to attack the opposition leader instead of answering. The rebuke was serious enough that Starmer, who left office earlier this month, confronted him about it afterward. Hoyle’s office was unapologetic, telling reporters that reminding a prime minister of the rules of engagement is simply part of the job, and that this wasn’t a one-off.

There’s a common thread in both examples: the Speaker’s party doesn’t decide which way he leans once he’s in the chair. Om Birla is a ruling Bharatiya Janata Party MP, but he has to rule on the minister’s objection. Lindsay Hoyle came up through Parliament as a Labour MP, and he still pulled up a Labour prime minister for dodging questions. In a parliamentary system, that chair asks something drastically different of the person than the party did.

Nepal’s Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal walked into the chair straight from being the Rastriya Swatantra Party’s vice-chair, elected unopposed because his party holds a near two-thirds majority in the House. Opposition lawmakers have spent months accusing him of failing to compel Shah’s appearance and of leaning toward the government. On Thursday, he faced a test: lawmaker after lawmaker rose demanding the government answer for the communal violence in Sunsari district and the prime minister’s absence from it, and Aryal had the authority to rule that the House was owed a response. He failed.

This brings us to the elephant in the room, the prime minister himself. Balendra Shah has faced the parliament exactly once, on May 31, and it looked nothing like the Question Hour. It was his first session answering lawmakers. He was asked about the old border dispute with India, he said Nepal had also encroached on Indian land in places — a fact, he said, he’d only learned after taking office — and suggested the UK be brought in to help resolve it alongside India. You’d think a government would spend days, even weeks, preparing a statement like that before saying it on the record. Shah delivered it like an aside.

The backlash was immediate. The Nepali Congress and CPN-UML demanded he retract the statement, produce evidence, and apologize. Former Nepali ambassadors to India said publicly that no such encroachment had ever been documented. Opposition lawmakers picketed the well of the House and called for his resignation. Shah did not come back to answer follow-up questions. When his own party’s chief whip was asked why, the answer was the government’s own defense: parliamentary rules don’t require the prime minister’s personal presence, and a minister can respond on his behalf.

When Shah did resurface again, this time on June 1, it wasn’t to answer for the substance. He arrived unannounced, addressed the House briefly through the Speaker, and repeated the claim rather than walk it back. Opposition Chief Whip Ain Bahadur Mahar’s complaint that day said as much about the moment as the remark itself: he objected not only to what Shah had said, but to what he’d worn as he said it, arguing the prime minister was dressed for the football pitch rather than Parliament. Two months later, Shah still hasn’t addressed the House on the matter again.

This week, the pattern became impossible to ignore. As communal unrest that started on Sunday spread across towns in the southern plains, the death toll rose to three. Shah skipped the all-party meeting his own coalition partner convened to address the situation, and he addressed the killings only through a Facebook post. Speaker Aryal met with Shah on Tuesday and told him “it would be good” if he kept the House informed about the country’s current situation. Shah’s response? “I’ll think about it.”

When the Parliament finally reconvened on Thursday after a 15-day recess, it gave the crisis unfolding in the southern plains a special hour. Shah, once again, was nowhere to be seen. Most of the lawmakers who spoke, including former prime minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal, used their time to ask where Shah was; Dahal pointedly noted that the prime minister and his home minister had also skipped the all-party meeting. Aryal had the chance to rule that the government owed the House an answer, but he said nothing. Instead of forcing one, he adjourned the session again — this time for five days. Hours later, Shah addressed the nation for the first time since taking office, in a pre-recorded video that was posted on his personal Facebook page.

Nepal has all the same paper machinery as Delhi or London. It has a chapter of procedure devoted to questioning the prime minister directly. Even KP Sharma Oli — a prime minister widely criticized for his governing style — kept showing up to take questions from the opposition, session after session. He’d occasionally refuse to answer one he didn’t like, calling it hostile, but he came back the next time anyway.

Balendra Shah has refused to come back at all.

articles.title: Come together, right now
articles.summary:
On Thursday evening, Prime Minister Balendra Shah finally addressed the nation after days of unrest across the Tarai-Madhesh triggered by a communal clash in Dewanganj, Sunsari. Since recent events in regions of the southern plains placed the country in a precariously tense situation, it was only right that PM Shah finally took off his sunglasses and peered into the eyes of all citizens, urging them to exercise restraint and maintain societal harmony. The loss of three young lives—Jay Prakash Mehta, Om Prakash Mehta and Ganesh Yadav—and the injuries to scores of citizens and security personnel represent a dreadful tragedy that has heightened a sense of insecurity across the country. With curfews placed in several districts and the spectre of arson and vandalism looming, the fear persists that the situation could spiral beyond control, leading to irreparable damage to the national fabric.

PM Shah’s address to the nation on Thursday was a necessary intervention comprising an appeal for restraint and wisdom. The PM rightly asserted that religion is a “force that unites society and spreads love,” noting that “no religion or culture in the world teaches violence, hatred or division.” By emphasising that the fundamental essence of all religions is compassion, kindness, love and peace, he has sought to steer the public discourse away from the flames of retaliation scourging the Tarai-Madhesh. Such a message is vital in a society that has historically remained liberal towards diverse identities, viewing a mosaic of religions, castes and languages as a defining strength rather than a source of fracture.

Whilst the PM’s commitment to an impartial investigation and his consultation with President Ramchandra Paudel after the broadcast signal mature high-level engagement, the state must also acknowledge its earlier shortcomings. In the initial days of the unrest, security forces struggled with crowd management, and the government’s subsequent reliance on security-centric measures over political strategy was notable. The promotion of harmony now requires more than just the presence of law enforcement. It demands an inclusive strategy of social support and proactive political dialogue.

Furthermore, the inactivity of people’s representatives, particularly those from the Rastriya Swatantra Party who received a significant mandate in these regions, is a matter of concern. True leadership is defined by the ability to manage crises and provide reassurance directly to the electorate. There is an urgent need for representatives at all levels to visit their constituencies, fostering an atmosphere of trust rather than remaining silent in the face of communal tension.

The role of civil society, the media and social media users is equally indispensable. It is imperative to discourage provocative speech and the dissemination of false or unverified information that incites communal disharmony. Instead, the focus must shift towards the promotion of factual, restrained expression that celebrates co-existence.

Ultimately, the responsibility to ‘clear the clouds of unrest’ lies with both the state and the citizenry. Every individual must exercise the wisdom to analyse long-term consequences and reject the malicious interpretations of those seeking to destabilise the nation for ulterior motives. National unity has always been the greatest strength of Nepal during its most challenging periods.

The advancement of security and social harmony within the collective consciousness of a nation must remain the paramount objective of any responsible administration. However, the cultivation of such a climate cannot be achieved through the solitary efforts of the state. It necessitates a sustained, open dialogue and the unwavering support of every stakeholder within the national tapestry. In the words of the Beatles, the entire nation needs to ‘come together, right now’. The government must now act without further delay, prioritising open communication and ensuring that the preservation of social harmony remains the supreme duty of the state. Only through such a concerted effort can the nation transition from this period of unrest towards a future defined by peace and mutual respect.

articles.title: Is Nepal repeating India’s mistake?
articles.summary:
On Wednesday morning, in an interaction with a closed group of Nepali civil society members, Indian social activist Harsh Mander said that the ‘Citadel of fear’ in India’s socio-political landscape has been dismantled, but the ‘citadel of hate’ still stands. Mander was reflecting on the seismic impact of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests in July. After Chief Justice of India Surya Kant labelled unemployed youth as ‘cockroaches’ on May 15, the CJP reclaimed the slur to forge a satirical, digitally organised group against the system. What began as an online campaign quickly transformed into a mass, leaderless uprising at New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, driven by fury over leaks in the NEET-UG medical entrance exams and a broader collapse of public trust.

The CJP movement was the inevitable explosion of friction points that have long simmered beneath the surface of the Indian state. For the middle and working class, standardised entrance exams are the primary vehicle for upward social mobility. When these papers leak, as they so often have over the years, years of family savings and student labour are erased. The system had normalised such leaks, with the perpetrators rarely receiving punishment. This was a breach of the meritocratic social contract.

While we regularly see opposition parties and their student wings, both politically motivated, protest paper leaks in India, the CJP protest marked a major departure from the nature of protests, somewhat mimicking September’s Gen Z protests in Nepal. Like Nepal’s movement, the ‘Instagram satyagrahis’ in India bypassed traditional, co-opted political student wings to build a ‘carnival of protest’ that used humour and meme warfare to strip the state of its ability to intimidate them. They forced the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and secured compensation for affected families.

While the current regime in Kathmandu rode to power on the popular anti-establishment rhetoric of September’s protest, Nepal still mirrors Mander’s analogy of citadels, albeit subtly, with a similar layer of digital toxicity that is quietly building a citadel of fear. Across social media platforms, there is an overwhelming, often blind support for the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) and the regime of Prime Minister Balendra Shah. RSP anti-establishment energy has curdled into an aggressive shield that suffocates democratic discourse. Anyone who dares to critique the government faces immediate, seemingly coordinated cyber-harassment.

This digital lynch-mob culture has become so intense that seasoned journalists and public intellectuals have started to self-censor their opinions. The new generation of civil society leaders have been forced to meet behind closed doors, as was the case in Mander’s interaction programme, similar to the underground meetings after Gyanendra’s coup d'état. A portion of these online enforcers can be traced to online groups like Men’s Room Reloaded (MRR)—a Facebook group founded by PM Shah’s chief adviser Kumar Byanjankar—that originated in toxic, pornographic subcultures. This, however, is not an avant-garde practice of the current regime. Previously, the CPN-UML erected an IT cell to cloud critiques against the party and its leaders with opinion-muzzling comments. That such groups are the digital enforcement arms for ruling parties has created a pervasive climate of fear. It was true of UML’s leadership, and it is true now: When citizens are afraid to speak, the vital feedback loops of a healthy democracy are severed.

While the digital citadel of fear rises in Kathmandu, a citadel of hate is simultaneously being constructed along the Tarai belt. The recent communal violence in Sunsari’s Dewanganj, which left one young man dead and 22 others injured, is a chilling warning for the Nepali state. Allegedly triggered by a dispute over loud music during a Bolbam procession, this was not an isolated event. The Armed Police Force (APF) had flagged this growing communal divide three years ago, warning that organised attempts were being made to foment religious and ethnic divisions. The report explicitly urged the government to learn from communal violence elsewhere in South Asia to resolve disputes before they escalated into widespread unrest. However, these warnings were ignored by the political leadership.

If the root causes of the Sunsari incident are not investigated with absolute transparency, Nepal risks normalising the same culture of mob-lynching and communal polarisation that has plagued India for over a decade. The high-handedness of the security response in Sunsari, where police reportedly fired indiscriminately, only deepens public anger.

Meanwhile, silence from PM Shah during this crisis does not help the cause. Except for a social media statement, the PM has been conspicuously absent from the necessary acts of statesmanship. He did not attend the all-party meeting held to address the Sunsari unrest. In a time of national tension, a PM should be the calming voice of the nation, perhaps through a televised address, rather than a distant figure operating through a digital screen.

Furthermore, PM Shah’s relationship with President Ramchandra Paudel has become virtually non-existent, with no substantive consultations taking place in four months. If he continues to govern in isolation, relying on security forces to contain violence rather than political dialogue to prevent it, Nepal will transform into a citadel of hate where the state’s only language is force.

This pattern of administrative arrogance extends to the education sector. The recent Tribhuvan University (TU) leak, where Master of Business Studies (MBS) question papers surfaced in a WhatsApp group of over 1,000 members just five minutes into the exam, is a direct echo of the Indian NEET scandal. While Education Minister Sasmit Pokharel has been praised by his supporters for the swift arrest of the teacher responsible, this is merely a cosmetic PR move if the structural flaws are not addressed. True accountability extends beyond just catching a single ‘Sulav Sir’ to a total restoration of meritocracy in systems like TU and Lok Sewa. As seen in India, when young citizens feel that honest routes to success are rigged, the meritocratic social contract is breached, and their frustration eventually spills onto the streets.

Nepal’s leadership must realise that an anti-establishment origin story does not grant permanent immunity. The same digital tools that built the current regime’s platform can just as easily turn against them if they absorb the ills of the old guard. Governance requires transparent delivery and the courage to engage with criticism rather than social media optics.

When I interviewed Nepali geopolitical analyst Chandra Dev Bhatta for this paper in the aftermath of Nepal’s Gen Z protest, he said that the events in Nepal must have made India restless. While many dismissed Bhatta’s claim as far-fetched, it turned out to be true to an extent. The Indian movement shows that when a government refuses to engage in honest dialogue and chooses intimidation, public anger evolves into an unstoppable, decentralised force. Now, conversely, the events in India have stirred restlessness into the new generation of civil society leaders in Nepal.

Nepal can choose proactive accountability today, or it can continue down a path of enforced silence and digital intimidation until the dam of public patience breaks. The state can either mend the land through trust and integrity now, or wait for the streets to demand a final, unforgiving reckoning.

articles.title: Track II diplomacy: Time to rethink Nepal’s diaspora
articles.summary:
‘Supreme organic investor’ sounds more like a high-grade crop fertiliser. Rather it is a prestigious status for the Nepali Diaspora community under the National Commitment. The 18-point governing plan was released by Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s Cabinet weeks after assuming office. A promising gesture of annual investment bonds, guaranteed ancestral property, a path to the ballot, and protection and continuity of citizenship were listed in the commitment.

The instinct is understandable, as remittances equal roughly a quarter of Nepal’s GDP—among the highest ratios in the world. More than 2.1 million Nepalis live outside the country, and closer to 4.5 million counting people of Nepali descent. The Non-Resident Nepali Association reaches into almost 90 countries. A reforming government is eager to translate patriotic feeling into hard capital, and a diaspora seated on decades of savings is a reasonable place to look at. But this reflects a consistent pattern of misunderstanding of what diaspora is actually worth and how to mobilise it for statecraft.

Nepal’s first integrated foreign policy adopted in 2020 explicitly lists ‘Track II diplomacy’ among the country’s instruments of statecraft. The phrase sits in the doctrine, unused like a treadmill in a spare room. American diplomat Joseph Montville coined the term ‘Track II diplomacy’ for the low-key, unofficial work by which private citizens and other non-state actors pry open channels that formal Track I diplomacy cannot. Nepal maintains roughly 40 missions for a diaspora spread across more than twice as many countries. This is where Track II diplomacy naturally steps in.

Diaspora networks do not replace state diplomacy. They lower the cost of access and improve the odds. For a country that cannot afford access at all, Nepal is badly in need of one.

Two decades ago, India faced the same issue: A constitution that would not permit dual citizenship and a diaspora that wanted one. Delhi’s answer was to invent a substitute, the Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, codified in the Citizenship Act. But its smarter move came in 2016 when the diaspora portfolio was folded into the Ministry of External Affairs, and diaspora work stopped being classified as welfare and became part of foreign policy.

Nepal does not need the constitution to plot the move. India could not grant dual citizenship either, so it built a formidable institution to house it where foreign policy is mandated. Nepal has the same constraint, and half the answer already exists: A Labour Migration and Diaspora Coordination Division sitting well within the foreign ministry. It needs coordination rather than convening.

Ireland managed to get the diaspora relationship right but the politics wrong.
