It lets the grandchild of an Irish-born citizen claim dual citizenship, keeping the second and third generations legally attached rather than merely sentimental. Since 2004, its Emigrant Support Programme has spent over 170 million euro funding some 600 Irish organisations abroad, paying into the diaspora’s own institutions. Dublin promised a referendum on presidential voting rights in 2013 and never held one. Kathmandu has made the same promise. Ireland shows the relationship can be built regardless. It did not wait for the franchise, and neither should Nepal.

Armenia is a cautionary tale. It got the law right with a 2005 referendum lifting the constitutional ban on dual citizenship and a 2007 amendment to the Law on Citizenship. But it suffered institutionally. The Ministry of Diaspora, established in 2008, concluded disastrously 11 years later. The Armenian journal EVN Report’s assessment mentions it as a bureaucratic fiefdom that cold-shouldered investors without connections, duplicated the foreign ministry and forfeited the trust of the people it served. Its replacement is small by design; an office under the prime minister mandated to map diaspora expertise. The technology sector has since reached roughly 7 percent of GDP on that expertise. The lesson is that the wrong kind of diaspora institution shadows the foreign ministry and spends down trust a generation in the making. This brings us back to the Brain Gain Centre that sits under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Reviving it as a bigger registry would repeat Yerevan’s mistake. It certainly needs a different stance, drawing on examples from the three countries above.

First, Nepal needs to keep the diaspora establishment small, accountable and housed inside the foreign ministry. Second, it needs to map the diaspora by institution and jurisdiction rather than by name and profession. This allows the state to know who sits where, on which board and how to revise lobbying. Lastly, we could borrow Dublin’s patience: build the relationship and let it percolate while the constitutional questions follow, because none of this waits on an amendment, a referendum, or a two-thirds majority.

Track II advises; it certainly does not govern. The Diaspora Community is powerful to influence and inform Nepal’s positions, not to vote on them. That is also why it fits the constitution rather than straining it. The charter binds the state to an independent, non-aligned foreign policy in the national interest and says nothing about who may help pursue one. Three nations have paid for three distinct lessons along the way.

The takeaways are entirely free. But whether Nepal learns from these nations and builds a real strategy is entirely up to Kathmandu. If executed correctly, it could yield actual leverage for the state. Executed incorrectly, the Supreme Organic Investor remains nothing more than the expensive fertiliser it sounds like.

articles.title: A rom-com that learns to let go
articles.summary:
Eventually, Sharanya Rajgopal’s ‘Musafir Cafe’ settles into the cosiness of a novel found in a railway station bookstall. Those unintimidating 200-page paperbacks, which one buys for an overnight journey. Here, it happens in the seventh episode of this eight-episode series. Sudha (Vedika Pinto) is a pretty, impulsive, recklessly-ambitious girl from Bhopal – a version of a metropolitan idea of a small-town firebrand. The kind who discovered ‘Carpe Diem’ in her adolescence and never looked back. She has a job offer from Mumbai, which she reluctantly accepts.

Unfortunately, she’s in love with Chander (Vikrant Massey), who she met a few months ago, and is currently vacationing with, in Mussoorie. Chander, a US-returned engineer who harbours dreams of owning a cafe on a hill station, is the opposite of Sudha. He’s excited about Mussoorie, his boss has agreed to become his loan guarantor, and he might have also found a business partner.

Sudha hasn’t told Chander about her plans yet. And when she does – he quashes his plans, and talks about moving with her to Mumbai. This disappoints her. In a rather pragmatic moment in the show, Sudha shames Chander for flippantly giving up on his dreams, and choosing to follow her instead. Some of her respect diminishes for him. This scene is what the entire series is building towards – and it reveals a sincere relationship drama embedded within the glossy design of a staple Netflix rom-com.

Based on Divya Prakash Dubey’s novel of the same name, Rajgopal’s series doesn’t begin with the same assurance. There’s an inherent clash between the show’s earthy source material and the frothy, urban Netflix aesthetic (that makes Bhopal look like Andheri). The actors, Pinto as Sudha and Massey as Chander, look (and sound) very protagonist-y. They’re not ‘ordinary’ by any measure.

Chander has been asked to meet with Sudha at a cafe, as an arranged-marriage prospect. Sudha is transparently cruel as he tells him marriage is not on her radar, and that she does this to please her mother. Chander, a pragmatic nerd with low self-esteem, finds himself charmed by her lack of filter. An unsuccessful arranged marriage meet-up improvises into an unintentional first date.

Directed by Ruchir Arun, who spearheaded the walk-and-talk relationship dramas on India’s Youtube (like Little Things), even ‘Musafir Cafe’ has plenty of the genre’s ‘relatable’ affectations. Massey, usually an effortless actor, initially looks at sea with the narrative sparseness. There’s very little to Chander beyond his desire to get married, and his infatuation with Sudha. A quirk added for effect, where he’s particular about his coffee, never feels like an innate part of him. Pinto is unconvincing as a girl from Ratlam, especially with that body language that belongs in Soho House.

The humour, and the abrupt relationship expediency, feel contrived at first.

Things become more easy-going in the third and fourth episode

However, things become more easy-going in the third and fourth episode, when Chander’s mother (Anubha Fatehpuria), shows up unannounced. A scene featuring Sudha’s roommate, a staple scene in such shows, when the two girls giggle over Sudha’s brand-new partner, is cute.

Even though they’re hopelessly in love, they’re both aware it could be a fleeting thing. He wants to settle down in the hills, she wants to go to Mumbai and afford a life many only dream about. They’ve fundamentally opposite goals in life, something one will invariably have to ‘adjust’ for.

The more mature track unfolds in the present, (Chander & Sudha’s love story is shown to have taken place eight years before), where Chander has realised his dream of Musafir Cafe, in Mussoorie. It’s run by him and his partner, Preeti (Manisha Makhwana). It looks 3-D printed out of Instagram, given how there’s not a single smudge on the cafe’s table cloths.

The surprising detail here is that Preeti knows about Chander’s lack-of-closure with Sudha. She’s the generous lover, who rationalises her partner’s flaws on his behalf, and doesn’t allow any form of negativity. It’s an interesting relationship dynamic, where a woman patiently waits for her man to leave behind his past.

Preeti is so close to an ideal, and so plainly characterised, I’m tempted to call her an invention of the male gaze. Which is not to say, she’s not disarming. Makhwana plays the stoic Preeti using a light touch, who would rather silently suffer for her lover, than show signs of jealousy. When Sudha visits them in Mussoorie late in the show, she puts up a brave front as a host, and then weeps at home.

Like Preeti’s sadness here, the show fetishises some other things too. A writer character (Rajeev Siddhartha), who talks like he’s writing prose. Always dressed immaculately in dark overcoats, sipping tea/coffee as young girls (his fans) giggle around him, he doesn’t miss a beat flirting with Preeti (an aspiring writer, we’re told).

Also, the dream of owning a cafe in the hills feels like a very city-bred fantasy. There’s nothing to indicate that Chander and Preeti are struggling at all, as the cafe appears to be running itself. People come in, and speak in Instagram affirmations. ‘Musafir’ assumes an Imtiaz Ali metaphor for many, who look forward to the journey, rather than the destination. Most of them appear to be in search of themselves.

It could seem laughable from a distance, but I found myself smitten by the fantasy. It’s the kind of show where a business partner signs away his palatial chalet to Chander and Preeti before moving back to the US for good – which they can use for expansion.

After trudging along cliches of the will they/won’t they rom-com, ‘Musafir Cafe’ becomes the strongest version of itself in the final two episodes, when an older couple enters the picture. Played by Adil Hussain and Sadiya Siddiqui, they become the (high) benchmark for Chander.

As Sudha visits Chander one last time, before moving abroad for good, they have an awkward at first, but ultimately cathartic conversation, bringing closure to both of them. It’s a rare sight of exes being shown as both graceful and grateful around each other. If not for the relationship, they wouldn’t be the people they are today. Each failed relationship is also a coming-of-age tale. That’s a realisation few relationship dramas seem to have.

Arun and Rajgopal take a good call of ending things on a crescendo of ambiguity, rather than a neatly-tied climax with a slate of ‘The End’. It mimics the beats of a life that goes on long after the ‘story’ has concluded. I’d love for them to just leave it at that, instead of using the open end for a season two. Sometimes closure isn’t about certainty, it’s about knowing when to let go. Let’s hope Netflix does too.

Published in special arrangement with TheWire.in

articles.title: Book review: When folklore becomes fear
articles.summary:
Nepali horror has often found itself caught between two impulses: imitating familiar western supernatural fiction or leaning so heavily on folklore that it becomes little more than a catalogue of ghosts and legends. ‘Aghortantra’ attempts something more ambitious.

It borrows from oral traditions, Tantric mysticism, village myths and psychological suspense to create a horror novel that feels unmistakably rooted in Nepal. While the novel occasionally loses momentum under the weight of its own mythology, it succeeds in proving that local landscapes and belief systems can be just as unsettling as any haunted castle or Gothic mansion.

The novel follows an unnamed narrator struggling with fragmented memories and recurring nightmares. Accompanying his friend Muskan to a remote village in Rukum, he expects little more than a visit to the countryside. Instead, he stumbles into a place haunted not merely by spirits but by its own forgotten history. Strange dreams, abandoned caves, unexplained disappearances and stories passed down through generations slowly reveal a web of ancient rituals and curses that binds the village to forces far older than its inhabitants.

What makes ‘Aghortantra’ compelling is that it never rushes towards its monsters. The novel understands that fear grows best through anticipation.

Long before anything overtly supernatural appears, the landscape itself begins to feel hostile. Forests seem to remember forgotten tragedies. Rivers separate more than villages. Caves cease to be geological formations and become living repositories of secrets. Animals react to unseen presences before humans do. By allowing atmosphere to carry much of the horror, the novel recalls the rhythms of oral ghost stories told in Nepali villages, where silence and suggestion often prove more frightening than revelation.

The book's greatest strength lies in its mythology. Rather than importing vampires, demons or other well-worn horror figures, it builds its supernatural world from local belief systems. Dhamis, ritual purification, sacred ash, village legends and Tantric practices are woven into the narrative not as exotic decoration but as living traditions that shape how the characters understand danger. The supernatural never feels detached from everyday life because, for the villagers, these beliefs are everyday life. Their understanding of the world is informed by inherited stories as much as by observable reality.

This cultural grounding gives ‘Aghortantra’ an identity that distinguishes it from much contemporary horror. Even readers familiar with the genre will find themselves navigating unfamiliar terrain. The horror emerges not simply from what lurks in the forest, but from the possibility that the stories dismissed as superstition may contain uncomfortable truths.

The novel also avoids reducing its characters to victims waiting for supernatural punishment. The friendship between the narrator and Muskan provides the emotional centre of the story. Their bond develops naturally through shared danger rather than melodramatic declarations, lending emotional weight to the increasingly bizarre events around them. Muskan, in particular, acts as the novel's moral compass: brave without being reckless, compassionate without becoming sentimental. Their relationship keeps the narrative grounded when the mythology threatens to become overwhelming.

Equally effective is the way the novel treats memory. The narrator's forgotten past mirrors the village's suppressed history. As buried legends resurface, so do fragments of his own identity. This parallel transforms the novel from a simple ghost story into something more reflective. The real horror is not merely that evil exists, but that communities and individuals alike cannot escape what they choose to forget. Ancient mistakes continue to shape the present, suggesting that the past is never truly buried.

Yet ‘Aghortantra’ is also a novel that asks for patience. Its fascination with mythology occasionally works against its storytelling. Lengthy explanations of village legends and ritual histories interrupt scenes just as they begin to gather momentum. There are moments when readers understand the implications of a legend before the narrative has finished explaining it.

Repetition, too, becomes noticeable. Characters frequently respond to danger in similar ways, and descriptions of fear sometimes echo one another closely. A firmer editorial hand could have tightened these sections without sacrificing the richness of world-building.

The supporting character, while colourful, rarely develops beyond their narrative function. Characters such as Kiran, Dorje and several villagers primarily exist to guide the protagonists through successive mysteries or supply pieces of folklore. Although this helps sustain the atmosphere, it occasionally leaves emotional investment concentrated almost entirely on the central friendship.

Perhaps the novel's boldest decision is its refusal to provide complete closure. While the immediate supernatural threat appears contained, the ending suggests that deeper mysteries remain unresolved. Instead of presenting evil as something permanently defeated, ‘Aghortantra’ portrays it as cyclical, waiting for history to repeat itself. The final pages imply that the protagonist's journey has only begun, resisting the temptation to explain every mystery. For some readers this ambiguity may prove frustrating; for others it will be precisely what lingers after the final page.

In recent years, Nepali genre fiction has steadily expanded beyond romance and social realism, and ‘Aghortantra’ demonstrates how horror can contribute meaningfully to that growth. Its greatest achievement is not that it frightens readers—though it often does—but that it trusts Nepali folklore to sustain an entire fictional universe. Rather than borrowing its fears from elsewhere, it discovers them in the country's own forests, rivers, rituals and oral traditions.

‘Aghortantra’ is an uneven novel, but it is also an imaginative and culturally confident one. It shows that horror need not abandon local identity to become compelling. By turning inherited myths into living nightmares, it opens intriguing possibilities for the future of Nepali speculative fiction.

———————————————

Aghortantra

Author: Yekendra Bahadur Rawal

Publisher: Yek Rawal

Published Year: 2026

articles.title: Exhibit review: The language of Paubha
articles.summary:
The more you look, the more there is to see in Shankar Kumar Joshi's and Sankha Narayan Shrestha’s Poubha paintings – such is the intricacy and attention to detail that the art form requires and that these two artists are able to supply.

At first viewing, the paintings feature a cast of religious characters familiar to the run-of-the-mill Nepali viewer, as they were to me, images that are unmistakably of Buddha, Ganesh or Bhairav. But these depictions of the deities are most unlike the commonplace ones.

As both artists said many times in the detailed tour of the exhibition they enthusiastically gave, “There are endless myths and stories behind these forms; even we are always learning something or other" – a statement that is made all the more noteworthy given the many years of experience and practice the two have had.

Joshi has been learning to draw for as long as he can remember, and he has been making Poubha art professionally for some three decades. Twice now, he has won first place in the Lalit Kala Award, a prestigious award organised by the Nepal Academy of Fine Arts.

Similarly, Shrestha has also been drawing since childhood. His training began with Thangka work and then eventually moved to Poubha painting. Shrestha too has won awards at exhibitions organised by the Nepal Academy of Fine Arts.

Sixteen of Shrestha’s works are being presented at the gallery. In discussing his artwork, he spent a lot of time talking about his Pancha Buddha or ‘Five Buddhas’. “They are in five colours because they represent five differing forms. One for each direction, the four cardinal ones and one facing the heavens. They also represent the five elements: earth, wind, fire, water and space,” he said.

The artists also get to have their say in certain matters. With the Buddhas, Shrestha shared that he had initially planned to paint them on one canvas. But the attention to detail required made it impossible to put them all together. Similarly, the background designs are his choice. “The background art behind the Buddhas is considered a traditional one; you will see it in other paintings by other people also. But I could have put something else there if I wanted to. Not every detail is dictated; we can have our say.”

Each of the five Buddhas is surrounded by different icons, animals and mythical figures. The Buddha painted yellow is a representation of wind, or vayu. As such, the form is supported by two horses, known for their speed, quick as the wind. Similarly, the Buddha in blue represents earth energy and so is supported by two elephants on either side, able to bear the heavy burden.

Twenty-one of Shrestha’s works are being presented at the gallery. He shared the story behind his rendering of Ganesh in one of them. “Ganesh has just managed to emerge victorious over his brother. The two are challenged to circumnavigate the universe three times over. Ganesh’s swift brother takes off on his peacock. Ganesh chooses to get on his mouse and take three laps around his seated parents. He wins and receives a boon. This is his victorious form," Shrestha shared.

Both artists stressed the importance of a good ‘guru’ in learning the art form. Gurus teach not only what and how but also the why – the reason a certain deity needs to be holding a certain item in one hand and not the other, the story behind the form a given deity has taken, etc.

These details in the paintings are important because Poubha, as an art form, emerged out of Poubha, a religious practice. “These paintings go to temples. They are used for religious prayer,” Shrestha said. “They need to be accurate to the traditional stories; otherwise, they are not fit for religious use,” he added.

“In the past, not everyone was allowed to look at the deities in their fearsome forms. One needed to be initiated into the practice. Now it has become open for everybody to see and keep,” Joshi said. When asked about how they felt about this change, the artists expressed a sense of practicality. “If the art is kept in the temples to be viewed only by a certain few, it will begin to disappear. This sort of exhibition gives the art style publicity. That is a necessary thing if we want to keep the art form alive,” Joshi added.

The exhibition is most definitely worthwhile. The fearsome rendering of the deities with their legendary names makes the viewer feel small in the presence of the depictions, yes, but also in front of the tradition and history behind the art itself.

What are these stories and icons? What do they mean? Where do they come from? These are some of the many questions the viewer is confronted by. The viewing could be peaceful and meditative; the artists share that the focused work that goes into making the art certainly is, or it could lead down many a rabbit hole in search for more answers.

articles.title: Budget-friendly places for Nepali students in Ohio
articles.summary:
Athens is a small, scenic college town in southeastern Ohio, shaped largely by Ohio University and its energetic student community. Surrounded by rolling hills, rivers and forests, the town combines historic streets, local businesses and easy access to nature.

The university campus, downtown shops and restaurants are concentrated within a compact area, making daily life manageable without a car. Ohio University students can also use Athens Public Transit free of charge, while nearby trails and forests provide inexpensive options for hiking and outdoor recreation.

Because Athens is a relatively small town, the number of professional internships available locally can be limited. Although Ohio University hosts career fairs and attracts employers from across the country, students may need to look beyond Athens or relocate temporarily for specialised opportunities.

Oxford is a compact, classic college town in southwestern Ohio, built almost entirely around Miami University at its core. Red-brick Georgian buildings, leafy streets and a walkable uptown give it a traditional campus-town character.

The compact layout means campus, uptown restaurants, shops and student housing are all within easy walking distance. The town is also considered quite safe, and Miami University's strong sense of community brings a steady calendar of campus events, traditions and activities that keep student life active without needing to travel elsewhere.

The town's economy is heavily tied to the university, so it can feel quiet or emptied out during breaks and summer months when students are away.

ColumbusColumbus is Ohio's capital and largest city, and it's where The Ohio State University, one of the biggest campuses in the country, is situated. Rather than a self-contained college town, Columbus functions as a full city with sprawling neighborhoods, a job market, and student population that's just one part of a much bigger urban picture.

Pros:Living costs stay reasonable even with everything a major city offers, and students get real exposure to internships and employers across finance, tech, healthcare and government without having to leave town.

Cons:The scale of the city brings more traffic and scattered housing options, so building a close community takes a bit more intention than it would in a smaller town.

Cincinnati is moving to universities like the University of Cincinnati and Xavier University. The city has 300,000 people and many residential areas.

Pros:The city offers people a diverse job market. It is home to many consumer goods, finance and healthcare companies. The cost of living is on the lower end for cities of this size.

Cons:Despite its universities, the city is not generally considered a college town. Younger residents have to actively seek college-town experiences since it is not part of city life. The city is also not walkable.

Toledo is Ohio’s fourth largest city, sitting on the edge of Lake Erie. It is a city of 600,000 people and home to the University of Toledo.

Pros: The University of Toledo sits at the centre of city life. It is the biggest school in town and also the town's biggest employer. Students have a solid pipeline to work experience and internships.

Cons: As a Rust Belt city, its growth has been stagnant over the years. And despite its size, it is considered to be falling behind the other major metros in Ohio.

Based on conversations with local Nepali students in Ohio.

articles.title: Migrant workers can strike under new Qatari labour law
articles.summary:
The Qatari government has introduced a conditional right for migrant workers to stage legal strikes as part of amendments to the country’s labour law.

Under the revised law, workers can go on strike for up to six working days after notifying their employer and the Ministry of Labour in writing, but only if a labour dispute cannot be resolved through negotiation, conciliation or mediation. The provision was introduced through Qatar’s Law No 9 of 2026, which amended the 2004 Labour Law (Law No 14) to strengthen workers’ rights and welfare.

The amended law requires companies with 100 or more employees to establish joint committees made up of management and worker representatives. The committees are intended to improve workplace dialogue, strengthen consultation and help resolve disputes before they escalate.

The reforms also introduce tougher penalties for labour violations. Employers that breach wage protection regulations may face suspension of ministry services, while the Labour Dispute Resolution Committee has been formally authorised to conduct virtual hearings. Recruitment agencies and companies involved in hiring violations may face fines ranging from QAR3,000 to QAR25,000. One Qatari riyal is equivalent to Rs41.66.

Workers exercising their right to strike will not be entitled to wages during the strike period. The law also allows companies to dismiss without notice workers who organise illegal or unjustified strikes without following the required procedures or who disrupt business operations through such actions.

Companies that fail to establish mandatory joint committees may face fines ranging from QAR2,000 to QAR5,000.

Qatar has also strengthened enforcement of its Wage Protection System. The amended law gives the labour ministry greater authority to take action against employers that delay or fail to pay salaries, including suspending services, imposing administrative measures and applying regulatory penalties against repeat offenders.

If a company repeatedly violates wage rules or triggers collective disputes because of unpaid salaries, other companies under the same ownership may also face penalties. The ministry may publish the names of non-compliant companies on its website.

Workers who remain unpaid can request a change of employer or terminate their contracts, with repatriation costs to be covered by the employer.

The Labour Dispute Resolution Committee’s new authority to conduct virtual hearings means workers no longer need to be physically present to pursue labour cases. Employers, workers and verified witnesses can now participate in proceedings online.

Workers must first register disputes with the ministry. Cases are referred to the dispute resolution committee only when efforts to settle them through negotiation fail. Agreements reached through ministry-led mediation will have the status of legally enforceable documents.

The amended law also increases penalties for recruitment-related violations.

Recruitment agencies can be fined between QAR3,000 and QAR25,000 for hiring workers without ministry approval for employment contracts, processing recruitment before mandatory medical examinations or committing other administrative and recruitment-related violations.

Qatari recruitment agencies generally recruit workers in partnership with manpower agencies in Nepal, although some employers also hire directly through Nepali firms.

The new rules also require workers seeking employment in designated technical and professional occupations to obtain certificates confirming that they have completed required training and passed examinations at ministry-approved centres before starting work.

Meanwhile, Qatar has extended the non-compete period, during which an employee can be restricted from joining a competing company after leaving a job, from one year to two years. The change restores a provision that existed before 2020.

If an employee has access to sensitive client information, trade secrets or confidential company data, an employer can prevent them from joining a competitor for up to two years after the termination of employment.

The labour law amendments are aimed at modernising Qatar’s labour market, improving regulatory oversight and creating a more flexible and competitive employment system in line with the Qatar National Vision 2030. Some provisions will require additional decrees and executive regulations before they come into full effect.

“These reforms represent significant shifts that will heavily impact employers, workers, recruitment agencies and the dispute resolution system alike,” Krishna Panthi, president of the Non-Resident Nepali Association Qatar, told Kantipur.

articles.title: 67 Nepalis died in Japan over ten months, 25 killed themselves
articles.summary:
As many as 67 Nepali citizens have died in Japan over the past ten months, including 25 suicides, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Most of the deceased were individuals who had travelled on student visas and were also working part-time.

The deaths were recorded between mid-July, 2025 and June 1, 2026. While some cases list medical or other causes, many certificates state the reason as “unknown”. Illness-related deaths remain relatively low, officials said.

Acting Nepali ambassador to Japan Harihar Kant Poudel said the rising number of deaths has made body management increasingly difficult. “In some cases, families perform the funeral rites in Japan. In others, the embassy is not informed even after cremation,” he said.

Repatriating a body from Japan to Nepal costs around Rs1.2 million. Educational institutions sending students abroad on student visas are not covering these expenses and are often not in contact with the embassy.

Many students arriving for language studies on student visas have been taking up work. However, they are not required to obtain labour permits from the Department of Foreign Employment. As a result, the Foreign Employment Board does not provide financial assistance for repatriation or related support when deaths occur outside the formal labour system.

Deaths and suicides have been reported mainly among workers in construction, Nepal-run hotels and restaurants, and supply companies. Around 6,000 Nepal-operated hotels and restaurants are estimated to be running in Japan, where labour protections such as health insurance and social security are not consistently ensured.

Education consultancies in Nepal have been sending students to Japan by charging high fees and making what critics describe as misleading promises. Japanese government data shows that by 2025, around 116,000 Nepali students were living in Japan, making Nepal the second-largest source of foreign students after China. Overall, Nepalis are the fifth-largest migrant group in Japan, with a total population of about 309,000, including 9,908 permanent residents.

According to the Non-Resident Nepali Association Japan, many students are under severe financial and psychological pressure due to high-interest loans taken in Nepal.

“Living costs in Japan are high, and earnings from 28 working hours a week are not enough for rent, food and tuition,” said NRNA Japan secretary Sachin Acharya. “When families in Nepal demand loan repayments, it adds mental stress. Switching from student visas to work visas requires language proficiency and other conditions, which are difficult. This is contributing to rising suicides.”

He said many students come on student visas due to easier access, but struggle to find stable work. “Some have to rely on money from Nepal. Many Nepalis are being arrested for exceeding the 28-hour work limit,” he said. “The Nepali embassy is understaffed, which makes it difficult to handle prison visits and related cases.”

Nepali student Uma Khatri, currently in Japan, said the reality is far more difficult than expected. “You need strong Japanese language skills before coming here. It is manageable for those who can work hard, but very difficult for students,” she said. “City living is expensive. Rural areas are cheaper, but jobs are scarce. Attendance requirements are strict, and visa renewal can be affected.”

Hira Shrestha from Baglung, who paid Rs1.35 million to reach Japan, said even working beyond permitted hours does not ease financial pressure. “People expect to repay loans quickly, but many struggle for years,” he said. Survival itself is hard.”

He said consultancy firms often present an overly optimistic picture. “They say you can study language for a year and work, but there is no job guarantee. Competition for part-time work is intense,” he said. “Some take multiple jobs to save money, which is illegal and can lead to visa cancellation.”

Only a small number of Nepalis go to Japan as skilled workers, while many enter as trainees in the agriculture and business sectors. The Nepali embassy has urged authorities to avoid sending workers under individual labour permits through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and labour channels.

In the last fiscal year, 18,744 Nepalis received labour approval from the Department of Foreign Employment, including both institutional and individual permits, with 5,800 women among them.

The embassy said it mainly tracks trainee workers sent through approved channels, where employers or agencies can be held responsible in case of death, making repatriation easier. However, it lacks records of students and individuals who arrive outside formal labour approval systems, complicating assistance and monitoring.

If you or someone you know is considering self-harm, please contact the following helplines.

Nepal Mental Hospital suicide hotline: 1166

Patan Hospital crisis helpline for suicide prevention: 9813476123

The Transcultural Psychosocial Organisation: 16600102005

articles.title: Nepali workers among injured in Qatar gas plant explosion, 13 killed
articles.summary:
Nepali workers were among those injured in an explosion and fire at a gas processing facility in Qatar, authorities said, as officials confirmed that 13 people were killed and 66 were injured in one of the country’s deadliest industrial accidents in recent years.

The blast occurred on Sunday night at the Barzan gas processing facility inside the Ras Laffan Industrial City complex, according to Qatar Energy officials. The injured include workers from Nepal, Qatar, India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Kenya, Ghana, Tanzania and Nigeria. Authorities said none of the injured is in a critical condition.

Energy minister and president and CEO of QatarEnergy, Saad bin Sherida al-Kaabi, said in Doha that the incident was a “technical accident” and not linked to sabotage or hostile activity. He said emergency teams and civil defence units brought the fire under control quickly.

Al-Kaabi said production at the Barzan facility had been halted for maintenance since December 2025 and was restarted only two days before the incident. He added that Qatar’s liquefied natural gas operations, export systems and port facilities were not affected.

The people killed were Indian and Pakistani nationals, he said.

Al-Kaabi said Qatar has sufficient gas reserves and alternative supply capacity, and the country’s export commitments will not be affected. He also expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished the injured a speedy recovery.

Authorities have launched an investigation into the cause of the explosion, Reuters reported.

Al-Kaabi said the incident is under review, while reiterating that there is no impact on wider energy infrastructure.

Qatar hosts one of the world’s largest liquefied natural gas export hubs at Ras Laffan.

articles.title: गृहमन्त्री र पीडितबिच ७ बुँदे सहमतिपछि सिरहा, जनकपुर र वीरगञ्जको जनजीवन सामान्य बन्दै
articles.summary:
गत पाँच दिनदेखि विभिन्न घटनाका कारण तनावग्रस्त बनेको मधेस प्रदेश बिस्तारै सामान्य अवस्थातर्फ फर्किन थालेको छ।

सुनसरीको देवानगञ्ज गाउँपालिका–३ कप्तानगञ्जमा डिजे बजाउने विषयलाई लिएर भएको विवादमा दुई युवाको गोली लागेर मृत्यु भएपछि सुरु भएको तनाव सिरहा, धनुषा, पर्सालगायत जिल्लामा फैलिएको थियो। अहिले भने प्रशासन, राजनीतिक दल तथा स्थानीय समुदायको पहलसँगै अधिकांश स्थानमा जनजीवन क्रमशः सामान्य बन्दै गएको छ।

सिरहाको गोलबजारमा बिहीबार भएको प्रदर्शनका क्रममा ज्यान गुमाएका १५ वर्षीय गणेश यादवका परिवारलाई भेट्न गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङ शुक्रबार मध्यरातमा औरही गाउँपालिका–२ तुलसियाहीस्थित निवास पुगेका थिए। भेटका क्रममा गृहमन्त्री र मृतकका परिवारबीच ७ बुँदे सहमति भएको छ।

सहमतिअनुसार गणेश यादवलाई शहीद घोषणा गर्ने प्रक्रिया तत्काल अघि बढाइने, नेपाल सरकारका तर्फबाट परिवारलाई १० लाख रुपैयाँ राहत उपलब्ध गराइने, घटनाको निष्पक्ष छानबिन गरी दोषीलाई कानुनी दायरामा ल्याइने, परिवारका एक सदस्यलाई रोजगारीको व्यवस्था मिलाइने तथा स्थानीय तहसँग समन्वय गरेर मृतकको सम्झनामा स्मृति पार्क निर्माण गरिने उल्लेख छ। साथै, छानबिन समितिको प्रतिवेदनका आधारमा आवश्यक कानुनी प्रक्रिया अघि बढाइने र शनिबार बिहान १० बजे अन्त्येष्टि गर्ने सहमति भएपछि सिरहाको अवस्था क्रमशः शान्त बन्दै गएको छ।

स्थानीय प्रशासनले पनि सर्वसाधारणलाई अत्यावश्यक उपभोग्य सामग्री खरिद गर्न सहज होस् भन्ने उद्देश्यले शनिबार बिहान १० बजेसम्म कर्फ्यु आदेश खुकुलो पारेको जनाएको छ।

यता धनुषाको जनकपुरधाममा सामाजिक सद्‌भाव कायम राख्ने उद्देश्यले शनिबार बिहान सद्‌भाव र्‍याली आयोजना गरिएको छ। शुक्रबार साँझ जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालयको रोहबरमा बसेको सर्वपक्षीय बैठकले समुदायबिच आपसी विश्वास र सहिष्णुता कायम राख्न संयुक्त रूपमा सद्‌भाव र्‍याली निकाल्ने निर्णय गरेको थियो।

बारा प्रशासनको पहलमा कलैयामा सदभाव र्‍याली निकालिएको छ। यस्तै पर्साको वीरगञ्जमा पनि अवस्था सामान्य बन्दै गएको छ। शुक्रबार निकालिएको सद्‌भाव र्‍यालीपछि घण्टाघर क्षेत्रमा केही युवाले विरोध प्रदर्शन गरे पनि त्यसको प्रभाव सीमित रहेको प्रहरीले जनाएको छ। शनिबार बिहानदेखि बजार, व्यापार तथा यातायात सेवा क्रमशः सञ्चालनमा आउन थालेको पर्साका प्रहरी प्रमुख एसपी पवन भट्टराईले जानकारी दिएका छन्।

उता सर्लाही सदरमुकाम मलङ्गवासहित अन्य प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा पनि जनजीवन सामान्य बन्दै गएको जिल्ला प्रशासनले जनाएको छ।

लगातार पाँच दिनसम्म अशान्त बनेको मधेस प्रदेशमा अहिले सुरक्षा निकायको सतर्कता, प्रशासनको सक्रियता र समुदायबीच सद्‌भाव कायम गर्ने प्रयासका कारण अवस्था बिस्तारै सहज बन्दै गएको देखिएको छ। यद्यपि, सम्भावित अप्रिय घटना हुन नदिन सुरक्षा व्यवस्था भने अझै कडा पारिएको छ।

articles.title: सुनसरीमा कर्फ्यु हट्यो, निषेधाज्ञा जारी
articles.summary:
जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय सुनसरीले जिल्लाका विभिन्न क्षेत्रमा जारी कर्फ्यु आदेश हटाउँदै निषेधाज्ञा जारी गरेको छ।

प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी इश्वरीप्रसाद अर्यालद्वारा जारी सूचनाअनुसार साउन १६ गते बिहान ८:३० देखि बेलुका ५:०० बजेसम्मका लागि कर्फ्यु हटाइएको हो। यसअघि साउन १२ गते राति ९:०० बजेदेखि अनिश्चितकालीन कर्फ्यु आदेश लागू गरिएको थियो।

कर्फ्यु हटाइए पनि स्थानीय प्रशासन ऐन, २०२८ को दफा ६ को उपदफा ३(क) बमोजिम अर्को सूचना जारी नभएसम्म सम्बन्धित क्षेत्रमा एकै स्थानमा पाँच जनाभन्दा बढी व्यक्ति भेला हुन, जुलुस, प्रदर्शन, सभा, बैठक तथा घेराउ गर्न निषेध गरिएको प्रशासनले जनाएको छ।

निषेधाज्ञा लागू भएका क्षेत्रहरूमा इटहरी उपमहानगरपालिका–१६ र १७ अन्तर्गत महेन्द्र राजमार्गको दायाँ–बायाँ २०० मिटर क्षेत्र, रामधुनी नगरपालिका–१ र ५ अन्तर्गत महेन्द्र राजमार्गको दायाँ–बायाँ २०० मिटर क्षेत्र, इनरुवा नगरपालिका, दुहबी नगरपालिका, भोक्राहा नरसिंह गाउँपालिका, कोशी गाउँपालिका, गढी गाउँपालिका, देवानगञ्ज गाउँपालिका, हरिनगर गाउँपालिका र बर्जु गाउँपालिकाको सम्पूर्ण क्षेत्र समावेश छन्।

प्रशासनले निषेधाज्ञाको पूर्ण पालना गर्न सर्वसाधारणसँग आग्रह गर्दै सुरक्षा अवस्था र परिस्थितिको मूल्याङ्कनका आधारमा थप निर्णय गरिने जनाएको छ।

articles.title: नेपाली महावाणिज्यदूतावासको सेवा प्रभावकारिताबारे छलफल
articles.summary:
दुबईस्थित नेपालको महावाणिज्यदूतावासले सेवा सञ्चालनको एक वर्ष पूरा हुन लागेका अवसरमा युएईस्थित गैरआवासीय नेपाली सङ्घ (एनआरएनए), नेपाली समाजलगायत विभिन्न नेपाली सङ्घसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधिसँग शुक्रबार छलफल गरेको छ।

कार्यक्रममा महावाणिज्यदूतावासको सेवा प्रवाह, राहदानी तथा कन्सुलर सेवा, श्रमिकको हित संरक्षण, आपत्कालीन सहायता तथा नेपाली समुदायसँग सम्बन्धित विविध विषयमा सुझाव आदानप्रदान भएको महावाणिज्यदूतावासले जनाएको छ। छलफलमा सहभागी विभिन्न सङ्घसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूले सेवा प्रवाहलाई थप प्रभावकारी, सहज र समुदायमैत्री बनाउन सुझाव दिएका थिए।

त्यस अवसरमा महावाणिज्यदूत हरिप्रसाद ओडारीले प्राप्त सुझाव आफ्ना निम्ति मार्गदर्शक हुने बताउँदै सबै सहभागीप्रति आभार व्यक्त गरे। साथै, उनले नेपाली समुदायसँगको सहकार्यलाई आगामी दिनमा पनि निरन्तरता दिइने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरे। सरकारले संयुक्त अरब इमिरेट्स (युएई) मा रहेका विशेषगरी दुबई तथा उत्तरी इमिरेट्समा बसोबास गर्ने नेपाली नागरिकलाई कन्सुलर सेवा सहज रूपमा उपलब्ध गराउने तथा उनीहरूको हित संरक्षण गर्ने उद्देश्यले दुबईमा महावाणिज्यदूतावास स्थापना गरेको हो।

महावाणिज्यदूतावासले राहदानी नवीकरण, यात्रा अनुमतिपत्र जारी, कागजात प्रमाणीकरण, श्रमसम्बन्धी सेवा तथा आपत्कालीन कन्सुलर सहायता उपलब्ध गराउँदै आएको छ।

articles.title: खेलाडीलाई छैन विश्राम
articles.summary:
फिफा विश्वकपको सकिएको एक महिनाजति पनि नबित्दै विश्वकै चर्चित लिगमध्ये एक इङ्लिस प्रिमियर लिगको नयाँ सिजन सुरु हुँदै छ।

आगामी अगस्ट २१ तारिखदेखि सुरु हुने लिग र जुलाई १९ तारिखमा अमेरिकामा सम्पन्न विश्वकप फाइनलबिचको अन्तर मात्र ३३ दिनको छ। यो समय व्यावसायिक क्लबका लागि पर्याप्त मानिएको छैन। किनभने फिफाकै नियमअनुसार विश्वकप खेलेका खेलाडीले कम्तीमा तीन साताको विश्राम पाउनुपर्छ। त्यसपछि मात्र उनीहरू क्लबमा फर्किएर टोलीसँग अभ्यास गर्न पाउँछन्। यसले विशेष गरी विश्वकपको अन्तिम चरणसम्म पुगेका खेलाडी रहेका क्लबलाई अप्ठ्यारो परेको छ। इङ्लिस प्रिमियर लिग क्लब टोटेनहम त्यसको उदाहरण हो। क्रिस्टियन रोमेरो र नयाँ अनुबन्धित खेलाडी मार्कोस सेनेसी अर्जेन्टिनासँग फाइनल पुगे। पेड्रो पोरो स्पेनको विश्वकप विजेता टोलीका सदस्य हुन्। उनी टोटेनहमकै स्टार पनि हुन्।

यही क्लबका डिजेड स्पेन्स इङ्ल्यान्डसँग तेस्रो स्थानको प्लेअफसम्म पुगेका थिए। फिफाको विश्रामसम्बन्धी प्रावधान लागू गर्दा फाइनल खेलेका खेलाडीहरू ९ अगस्टअघि क्लबमा फर्किन सक्दैनन्। स्पेन्सको हकमा त्यो मिति ८ अगस्ट हुन्छ। महत्त्वपूर्ण खेलाडी नहुँदा क्लबहरूले सुरुमा नै क्षति बेहोर्न सक्छन्।

अगस्ट २२ मा ब्रेन्टफोर्डविरुद्ध प्रिमियर लिगको पहिलो खेल खेल्नुअघि टोटेनहमसँग अभ्यास गर्ने समय करिब दुई साता मात्र हुनेछ। यद्यपि, अर्जेन्टिनाको टोलीमा अन्तिम समयमा समावेश भएका र विश्वकपमा दुई खेल खेलेका सेनेसी प्रिसिजन परीक्षणका लागि क्लबको प्रशिक्षण केन्द्र पुगिसकेको टोटेनहमले जनाएको छ। तर प्रशिक्षकहरूको चिन्ता खेलाडी ढिलो फर्किनुमा मात्र सीमित छैन।

प्रिसिजनको अधिकांश समय नयाँ रणनीति अभ्यास गर्ने, खेलाडीको फिटनेस सुधार्ने र मैत्रीपूर्ण खेलमार्फत टोलीलाई लयमा ल्याउने काममा खर्च हुन्छ। विश्वकपबाट ढिलो फर्किने खेलाडीले यी सबै प्रक्रिया गुमाउँछन्। त्यसपछि उनीहरूलाई पुनः टोलीमा घुलमिल गराउँदै फिटनेस पनि कायम राख्नुपर्ने चुनौती प्रशिक्षकसामु हुन्छ। म्यानचेस्टर सिटी र आर्सनलको पनि उस्तै चिन्ता छ।

विश्वकपको अन्तिम चरणसम्म सबैभन्दा धेरै खेलाडी पुग्ने प्रिमियर लिग क्लबमा म्यानचेस्टर सिटी र आर्सनलका हुन्। सिटीका रोड्रीले ७२६ मिनेट खेल्दै स्पेनलाई दोस्रोपल्ट पुरुष विश्वकप उपाधि जिताउन भूमिका खेले। उनी विश्वकपको महत्वपूर्ण खेलाडी पनि चयन भएका थिए। उनले विश्वकपमा गोल्डेन बल पाएका थिए।

मार्क गुएही र इलियट एन्डरसन इङ्ल्यान्डको अन्तिम सप्ताहसम्मको यात्रामा सहभागी थिए। निको ओ राइली इङ्ल्यान्डबाट सेमिफाइनलसम्म पुगे भने एर्लिङ हालान्ड र जेरेमी डोकु क्वार्टरफाइनलसम्म खेले। आर्सनलका डेक्लान राइस र बुकायो साका पनि तेस्रो स्थानको प्लेअफसम्म इङ्ल्यान्ड टोलीमा रहे। मार्टिन जुबिमेन्डी र मिकेल मेरिनो स्पेनसँग फाइनल पुगे। विलियम सालिबाले फ्रान्सलाई तेस्रो स्थानको प्लेअफसम्म पु¥याउन मद्दत गरे। तर त्यसपछि उनी ढाडको चोटका कारण बाहिरिए। नोनी माडुके अन्तिम सप्ताहसम्म इङ्ल्यान्ड टोलीमा रहे। तर उनी क्वार्टरफाइनलपछि मैदान उत्रिन पाएनन्। नर्वेका कप्तान मार्टिन ओडेगार्ड भने क्वार्टरफाइनलसम्म पुगे।

देखिन थाल्यो खेलभारको असर

फिफा विश्वकप सकिएलगत्तै केही खेलाडी चोटका कारण केही समय मैदानबाहिर रहने निश्चित भएको छ। म्यानचेस्टर सिटीका रोड्रीको हालै ढाडको शल्यक्रिया भएको छ।

उनी सिजनको सुरुआती केही खेल गुमाउने सम्भावना छ। आर्सनलका सालिबाले शल्यक्रिया गर्नुपरेन। तर ढाडको समस्याका कारण उनी लामो समय मैदानबाहिर रहने क्लबले जनाएको छ। यी चोटलाई विश्वकपकै प्रत्यक्ष परिणाम भन्न सकिँदैन तर निरन्तर बढिरहेको खेल संख्या र व्यस्त तालिकाले खेलाडीमाथि कति ठूलो शारीरिक दबाब परेको छ भन्ने संकेत भने यसले दिन्छ। केही प्रमुख खेलाडीसँग पूर्ण प्रिसिजन तयारी नै नगरी सिटी, आर्सनल, टोटेनहम र चेल्सीले नयाँ सिजन सुरु गर्नुपर्ने अवस्था आउन सक्छ।

विश्वकपमा सबैभन्दा धेरै समय मैदानमा बिताउने प्रिमियर लिग खेलाडी एस्टन भिल्लाका गोलरक्षक एमिलियानो मार्टिनेज रहे। अर्जेन्टिनाको फाइनल यात्रामा उनले सबै ८१० मिनेट खेले। लिभरपुलका एलेक्सिस म्याक एलिस्टर ७४९ मिनेटसहित दोस्रो र स्पेनका रोड्री ७२६ मिनेटसहित तेस्रो स्थानमा रहे। धेरै खेलाडीले विश्वकपभर आठ खेल बराबरको समय मैदानमा बिताएका छन्।

फिफाको नियमअनुसार फाइनल खेलेका रोड्री, पेड्रो पोरो, मार्टिन जुबिमेन्डी, एलेक्सिस म्याक एलिस्टर, एन्जो फर्नान्डेज, एमिलियानो मार्टिनेज र लिसान्ड्रो मार्टिनेज ९ अगस्टअघि क्लबमा फर्किन पाउने छैनन्। इङ्ल्यान्डका तेस्रो स्थानको प्लेअफ खेलेका खेलाडी भने एक दिनअघि फर्कनेछन्। यसले नयाँ सिजन सुरु हुनुअघि आफ्ना प्रमुख खेलाडीलाई पुनः टोलीमा समायोजन गर्न क्लबहरूसँग झन्डै १२ दिनमात्र बाँकी रहने अवस्था बनाएको छ।

व्यस्त हुँदै तालिका

चिन्ता यस वर्षको विश्वकपसम्म सीमित छैन। विश्व फुटबलका धेरै शीर्ष खेलाडीले लगातार तीन ठूला प्रतियोगिता खेलेका छन्। सन् २०२४ को युरोपियन च्याम्पियनसिप र कोपा अमेरिका, त्यसपछि विस्तारित क्लब विश्वकप र अहिलेको विश्वकप। स्पेनका रोड्रीले सन् २०२४ मै अत्यधिक खेलभारका कारण खेलाडी हडतालसम्म जान सक्ने चेतावनी दिएका थिए। आर्सनलका प्रशिक्षक मिकेल आर्टेटा र म्यानचेस्टर सिटीका प्रशिक्षक एन्जो मारेस्काले पनि पटकपटक व्यस्त खेल तालिकाप्रति चिन्ता व्यक्त गर्दै आएका छन्।

विश्वकपका क्रममा देखिएका चोटहरूले पनि ती चिन्तालाई थप बल दिएका छन्। एस्टन भिल्लाका अमाडु ओनानाले बेल्जियमका लागि खेल्दा घुँडाको गम्भीर चोट बेहोरे। म्यानचेस्टर युनाइटेडका मानुएल उगार्टेको विश्वकप पनि चोटकै कारण समयअघि समाप्त भयो।

ह्यामस्ट्रिङ समस्याबाट फर्किरहेका रिसे जेम्सको खेल समय इङल्यान्डले सावधानीपूर्वक व्यवस्थापन गर्‍यो। विश्वकपको यात्रा सकिएलगत्तै प्रिमियर लिग सुरु हुन दिनगन्ती सुरु भइसकेको छ। तर धेरै खेलाडीका लागि अहिले पहिलो प्राथमिकता प्रतिस्पर्धा मात्र होइन शरीरलाई पूर्ण रूपमा तयार बनाउनु हुनेछ।

articles.title: गृहमन्त्री र पीडितबिच ७ बुँदे सहमतिपछि सिरहा, जनकपुर र वीरगञ्जको जनजीवन सामान्य बन्दै
articles.summary:
गत पाँच दिनदेखि विभिन्न घटनाका कारण तनावग्रस्त बनेको मधेस प्रदेश बिस्तारै सामान्य अवस्थातर्फ फर्किन थालेको छ।

सुनसरीको देवानगञ्ज गाउँपालिका–३ कप्तानगञ्जमा डिजे बजाउने विषयलाई लिएर भएको विवादमा दुई युवाको गोली लागेर मृत्यु भएपछि सुरु भएको तनाव सिरहा, धनुषा, पर्सालगायत जिल्लामा फैलिएको थियो। अहिले भने प्रशासन, राजनीतिक दल तथा स्थानीय समुदायको पहलसँगै अधिकांश स्थानमा जनजीवन क्रमशः सामान्य बन्दै गएको छ।

सिरहाको गोलबजारमा बिहीबार भएको प्रदर्शनका क्रममा ज्यान गुमाएका १५ वर्षीय गणेश यादवका परिवारलाई भेट्न गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङ शुक्रबार मध्यरातमा औरही गाउँपालिका–२ तुलसियाहीस्थित निवास पुगेका थिए। भेटका क्रममा गृहमन्त्री र मृतकका परिवारबीच ७ बुँदे सहमति भएको छ।

सहमतिअनुसार गणेश यादवलाई शहीद घोषणा गर्ने प्रक्रिया तत्काल अघि बढाइने, नेपाल सरकारका तर्फबाट परिवारलाई १० लाख रुपैयाँ राहत उपलब्ध गराइने, घटनाको निष्पक्ष छानबिन गरी दोषीलाई कानुनी दायरामा ल्याइने, परिवारका एक सदस्यलाई रोजगारीको व्यवस्था मिलाइने तथा स्थानीय तहसँग समन्वय गरेर मृतकको सम्झनामा स्मृति पार्क निर्माण गरिने उल्लेख छ। साथै, छानबिन समितिको प्रतिवेदनका आधारमा आवश्यक कानुनी प्रक्रिया अघि बढाइने र शनिबार बिहान १० बजे अन्त्येष्टि गर्ने सहमति भएपछि सिरहाको अवस्था क्रमशः शान्त बन्दै गएको छ।

स्थानीय प्रशासनले पनि सर्वसाधारणलाई अत्यावश्यक उपभोग्य सामग्री खरिद गर्न सहज होस् भन्ने उद्देश्यले शनिबार बिहान १० बजेसम्म कर्फ्यु आदेश खुकुलो पारेको जनाएको छ।

यता धनुषाको जनकपुरधाममा सामाजिक सद्‌भाव कायम राख्ने उद्देश्यले शनिबार बिहान सद्‌भाव र्‍याली आयोजना गरिएको छ। शुक्रबार साँझ जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालयको रोहबरमा बसेको सर्वपक्षीय बैठकले समुदायबिच आपसी विश्वास र सहिष्णुता कायम राख्न संयुक्त रूपमा सद्‌भाव र्‍याली निकाल्ने निर्णय गरेको थियो।

बारा प्रशासनको पहलमा कलैयामा सदभाव र्‍याली निकालिएको छ। यस्तै पर्साको वीरगञ्जमा पनि अवस्था सामान्य बन्दै गएको छ। शुक्रबार निकालिएको सद्‌भाव र्‍यालीपछि घण्टाघर क्षेत्रमा केही युवाले विरोध प्रदर्शन गरे पनि त्यसको प्रभाव सीमित रहेको प्रहरीले जनाएको छ। शनिबार बिहानदेखि बजार, व्यापार तथा यातायात सेवा क्रमशः सञ्चालनमा आउन थालेको पर्साका प्रहरी प्रमुख एसपी पवन भट्टराईले जानकारी दिएका छन्।

उता सर्लाही सदरमुकाम मलङ्गवासहित अन्य प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा पनि जनजीवन सामान्य बन्दै गएको जिल्ला प्रशासनले जनाएको छ।

लगातार पाँच दिनसम्म अशान्त बनेको मधेस प्रदेशमा अहिले सुरक्षा निकायको सतर्कता, प्रशासनको सक्रियता र समुदायबीच सद्‌भाव कायम गर्ने प्रयासका कारण अवस्था बिस्तारै सहज बन्दै गएको देखिएको छ। यद्यपि, सम्भावित अप्रिय घटना हुन नदिन सुरक्षा व्यवस्था भने अझै कडा पारिएको छ।

articles.title: ब्रोड पिक हिमपहिरो : निर्मल पुर्जासहित ६ को खोजी तथा उद्धार अभियान पुनः सुरु
articles.summary:
पाकिस्तानको काराकोरम पर्वतमालामा अवस्थित विश्वको १२औँ अग्लो हिमाल ब्रोड पिक (८ हजार ४७ मिटर) मा गएको भीषण हिमपहिरोमा परी बेपत्ता भएका अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय पर्वतारोहीहरूको खोजी तथा उद्धार कार्य शनिबार (आज) बिहानदेखि पुनः सुरु गरिएको छ।

प्रतिकूल मौसमका कारण शुक्रबार साँझ स्थगित भएको खोजी तथा उद्धार कार्य मौसममा सुधार आएसँगै आज बिहानैबाट पुनः सुचारु भएको अधिकारीहरूले जानकारी दिएका छन्।

गिलगिट–बाल्टिस्तान प्रहरीका प्रवक्ताका अनुसार उच्च हिमाली भरिया (हाइ-अल्टिच्युड पोर्टर) तथा उद्धार टोलीले बेपत्ता आरोहीहरूको खोजी जारी राखेका हुन्।

यसैबीच, हिजो स्कर्दु ल्याइएको ओमानी आरोहीको शव आज बिहान हवाईमार्फत स्कर्दुबाट इस्लामाबाद पठाइएको छ। नेपाली आरोहीको शव भने हाल स्कर्दुमै रहेको छ।

जानकारी अनुसार खोजी अभियानका क्रममा चार जना आरोहीको शव फेला परेको छ भने तीन जनाको मात्रै औपचारिक पहिचान भएको छ। गिलगिट-बाल्टिस्तान सरकारले दिएको जानकारी अनुसार तीन जनाको शव शुक्रबार नै पाकिस्तानी सेनाको हेलिकप्टरमार्फत ब्रोड पिक बेस क्याम्पबाट स्कार्दुस्थित सीएमएच अस्पताल ल्याइएको छ। फेला परेका शवहरूमा नेपालका पुरबहादुर गुरुङ (युक्त), ओमानकी पहिलो सगरमाथा आरोही नादिरा अहमद अब्दुल्लाह अल हार्थी र अमेरिकाकी पर्वतारोही म्यालोरी गेइस (सारा म्यालोरी गेइस, टेक्सासकी ३९ वर्षीया) रहेका छन्। चौथो शवको बारेमा औपचारिक पहिचान हुन बाँकी रहेको छ। उद्धार टोलीले ड्रोन फुटेज र जीपीएस संकेतहरूको सहायताले क्षेत्रको निगरानी गरिरहेको छ।

articles.title: राष्ट्र बन्नै बाँकी छ
articles.summary:
२०८३ साउन ६ गते ‘चक्रप्रसाद बाँस्तोला: बौद्धिकता र विद्रोह’ वार्तालाप पुस्तक प्रथम राष्ट्रपति डा. रामवरण यादवको प्रमुख आतिथ्यमा विमोचन भयो। प्रसिद्ध साहित्यकार कृष्ण धरावासीद्वारा सम्पादित र चक्र बाँस्तोलाकी धर्मपत्नी कुसुम बाँस्तोला प्रकाशक हुन्। यस पुस्तक विमोचनमा डा. यादवले भने– ‘मलाई अचम्म लागेको छ। हिजोआज अधिकांश लेखक तथा स्तम्भकार किन मौन छन् ? के देश ठिक बाटो हिँडेको छ? विगतका कठिन राजनीतिक समयमा सशक्त कलम चलाउने बुद्धिजीवी कहाँ छन्?’

प्रथम राष्ट्रपतिका यी सवाल बिपी कोइराला र बाँस्तोलाबिचको पुस्तकसँग पनि जोडिन्छन्। यसमा बिपीले बाँस्तोलालाई भनेका छन्– ‘हेर ! इतिहासमा धेरै राष्ट्र बने। कति राष्ट्र पहिलो विश्वयुद्धमा रहेनन्। दोस्रो विश्वयुद्धपछि कति नयाँ बने, कति पुराना हराए, के–के भए? त्यसो भए नेपालको नियति के छ त? एउटा राष्ट्र भएर बसिरहने नियति छ कि छैन? ...हाम्रा सारा लडाइँ नेपाल राष्ट्रसँग त जोडिन्छन्। अधिकारसम्पन्न नेपाली जनताका लागि हुन्। सुन्यौ ! नेपाल राज्य बनेको छ, राष्ट्र बन्नै बाँकी छ।’

यसको व्याख्या बाँस्तोलाले गरेका छन्।

धर्मपत्नी कुसुम बाँस्तोलाले चक्र बाँस्तोलाको ६ वर्षसम्म अचेत अवस्थामा गरेका सेवा मर्मस्पर्शी छन्। एक क्षण पनि ओझेलमा नपारी, अत्यावश्यकताले बाहिर जाँदा पनि घर फर्कने हतारो हुन्थ्यो। राजनीतिमा सक्रिय हुँदा कुसुमले आगन्तुकप्रति गरेका व्यवहारको प्रशंसा गर्थे। चर्को स्वरमा बहस वा वादविवाद भए पनि कोठामा आएपछि कुसुमबाट पाएको शीतलताले शान्त हुन्थे।

कहिल्यै दुःखी नदेखिने चक्र बाँस्तोलाले पोखरा पार्टी महाधिवेशनमा भोगेको पराजय पीडादायी भएको कुसुमले बताएकी छन्। प्रहरीले गरेको घर खानतलासी, सरिता प्रसाईं र उनकी आमा दिव्य प्रसाईंको गिरफ्तारी, टोरुप प्रसाईंले पठाएको ‘पम्प्लेटको आपतबोरा’ र चलाखीपूर्वक बिना प्रसाईंको घरमा स्थानान्तरण गरेका २०४६ आन्दोलनको राजनीतिक पाटो, परिवारप्रतिको जिम्मेवारी, विवाह तथा पदीय राजनीतिलगायत कुसुमसँगको संवादले पुस्तकले केही पूर्णता पाएको धरावासीको कथन छ।

भोला चेटर्जीसँगको एक अन्तर्वार्तामा बिपीले चक्र बाँस्तोलालाई ‘तेजस्वी युवक’को संज्ञा दिएका छन्। उनको राजनीतिक जीवन भारतको बनारसबाट सुरु भयो। बनारसको बिएचयुमा पढ्दै गर्दा बिपीसँगको भेटघाट तथा प्रदीप गिरीसँगको संगतको गहिरो प्रभाव थियो। प्रदीप गिरीले सदस्य लिन नभनी उनी कांग्रेसी कार्यकर्ता भएछन्।

साहित्यमा रुचि राख्ने व्यक्तिलाई उनले राजनीतिक शास्त्र पढ्न उत्प्रेरित गरे। युनिभर्सिटीको चुनावमा पहिलो पटक कांग्रेसबाट प्यानल उठाएर प्रदीप गिरी अध्यक्ष र उनी उपाध्यक्ष भएको प्रसंग रोचक छ। यसअघिको विपरीत विचारधारा भए पनि ‘कोठामित्र’ तेजराज खतिवडाको (कम्युनिस्ट पन्थी) भनाइमा कम्युनिस्टलाई भोट हालेछन्।

चक्र बाँस्तोला निडर र क्रान्तिकारी विचार बोकेका युवा थिए। एक प्रसंगमा उनले भने– ‘कुसुम, राजनीतिमा खुट्टा कमाउने हो भने घरै बसे हुन्छ, मैदानमा उत्रेपछि डराउनु हुन्न।’

आमकांग्रेसीभन्दा फरक थिए उनी। बिपीका कुरा सुन्न मात्र नभई बौद्धिक प्रश्न गर्ने क्षमता राख्थे। थप जवाफ खोज्न मन्त्रीमण्डलमा राज्यमन्त्री भइसकेका योगेन्द्रमान शेरचनलाई बिपीले ‘उहाँ वाकिङ इन्साइक्लोपिडिया हुनुहुन्छ’ भनेर परिचय गराएका थिए।

२०२८ सालमा नेपाली कांग्रेसले सशस्त्र क्रान्तिको घोषणा गरेपछि बिपीको निर्देशनमा हतियार खोज्ने र भण्डारण गर्ने जोखिमपूर्ण काममा लागे। पाकिस्तानी सरकारसँग सशस्त्र संघर्षरत मुक्तिवाहिनीको अनुरोध र जयप्रकाश नारायणको सल्लाहमा बिपीले क्रान्तिका लागि राखिएको हतियार बंगलादेशमा पुर्‍याएको र मृत्युको मुखबाट बालबाल बचेको कथा रोचक छ। यसको जानकारी प्रधानमन्त्री इन्दिरा गान्धीलाई भएको अनुमान उनले गरेका छन्।

२०३० जेठ २८ गते बिहान साढे ८ बजे दक्षिण एसियामा नेपालमा भएको हवाईजहाज अपहरण पहिलो हो। यसका योजनाकार गिरिजाप्रसाद कोइराला थिए। सेकेन्ड–सेकेन्डका योजनामा अपहरण भयो। अपहरणकारीसँग चक्र बाँस्तोलाको चिनजान थिएन। जे आदेश भयो, त्यही गरे। देशभित्र क्रान्ति गर्न भारु तीस लाख हात पार्न यो मिसन सफल भयो। चक्र बाँस्तोला गिरिजाबाबुको ‘साइलेन्ट सिपाही’ थिए।

ओखलढुंगाबाट पहिलो आक्रमणबाट सुरु गरिएको क्रान्ति तत्कालीन पञ्चायती शासनले असफल पार्‍यो। जुम्लिया युवा दाजुभाइ रामलक्ष्मणसहित २६ होनहार युवाले ज्यान गुमाए। सशस्त्र क्रान्तिको योजना तुहियो। यसका कमान्डर यज्ञबहादुर थापा र सहकमान्डर अमरसिंह राई थिए। पाकिस्तानमा भुट्टोलाई फाँसी दिएको १५ दिनअघि थापालाई गोली हानी मृत्युदण्ड दिएको थियो।

अपहरण काण्डबाट ‘डकैतीको मुद्दा’ चल्यो। फलामे बेडी हातखुट्टा र घाँटीमा लगाई डाँकासास्ती तथा लखनउ जेलमा दादाका यातना अपत्यारिलो थियो। आरएसएसमा लागेका एक सहपाठी भेटेपछि १० दिनको बसाइँ केही सहज भयो। हातखुट्टाका साङ्लीसहितको हत्कडी भुइँमा र रेलमा घिसार्दै हिँड्नु र बस्नुपर्थ्याे। सन् १९७५ मा एक राजनीतिक समझदारीपछि उनी रिहा भए। २०३७ वैशाख १ गते आममाफी घोषणापछि नेपाल फर्किए। २०४६ सालपछिको पहिलो चुनावमा पराजय भोगे तर दोस्रोमा जितेर मन्त्री भए। माओवादीसँगको वार्तामा पहिलो सरकारी सहजकर्ता थिए।

सन् १९९६ ताका, एम्नेस्टी इन्टरनेसनलले चीनको मानवअधिकारको सम्बन्धमा ‘चीनमा कोही सुरक्षित छैनन्’ प्रकरणसहित विश्व अभियान चलायो। नेपाल शाखाको म सभापति थिएँ। एक जुलुससहित चिनियाँ दूतावासमा जाने योजना बन्यो। न्युरोडबाट जुलुस सुरु नहुँदै पक्राउ पर्‍यौं, भृकुटीमण्डपमा राखियो। पहिलेदेखि नै करिब तीन–चार सय तिब्बती शरणार्थीलाई ठाउँ–ठाउँबाट त्यहाँ ल्याइएको रहेछ। ‘फ्रि तिब्बत’को संलग्नता देखाउन सरकारले त्यसो गरेको थाहा भयो। राति १२–१ बजेतिर हामी करिब २० जना र १५ शरणार्थीलाई हनुमानढोकामा सारियो।

हामी छुटेपछि दबाबमा ती बन्दीलाई चीन फर्काउने निर्णय सरकारले गर्न लागेको चाल पायौं। चक्र बाँस्तोला शेरबहादुर देउवा क्याबिनेटमा एक शक्तिशाली मन्त्री थिए। बिहान ६ बजे थापागाउँ निवासमा पुगेँ। हामीबिच निकै चर्काचर्की भयो।

मानवअधिकारका दृष्टिले गलत हुँदैछ भन्ने मेरो राय थियो तर सरकारको बचाउ उनले गरे। कुसुम भाउजूले ल्याएको चियासमेत नपिई तनावबिच म हिँडेँ। पछि थाहा भयो, सरकार पछि हटेछ। सायद उनले प्रधानमन्त्रीलाई ‘कन्भिन्स’ गरे होलान्। यस घटनाले घरमा केकस्तो असर पार्‍यो भन्ने मलाई चिन्ता थियो तर यो पुस्तक पढेपछि कुसुम भाउजूका अगाडि उनी शान्त हुने स्वभाव भएकाले केही ‘रिलिफ’ महसुस गरें।

articles.title: सवारी दुर्घटनामा ३ जनाको मृत्यु
articles.summary:
पछिल्लो २४ घण्टामा देशका विभिन्न स्थानमा भएका सवारी दुर्घटनामा तीन जनाको मृत्यु भएको छ भने ६२ जना घाइते भएका छन्। नेपाल प्रहरीको तथ्यांकअनुसार दुर्घटनामा सबैभन्दा बढी लुम्बिनी प्रदेशमा १६ जना र कोशी प्रदेशमा १५ जना घाइते भएका छन्।

प्रहरीका अनुसार कर्णाली प्रदेशमा तीन, सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशमा १० र बागमती प्रदेशमा पाँच जना घाइते भएका छन् । त्यसैगरी गण्डकी प्रदेशमा एक जनाको मृत्यु भएको छ भने नौ जना घाइते भएका छन्। कोशी प्रदेशमा एक जनाको मृत्यु र १५ जना घाइते भएका छन्। मधेश प्रदेशमा ११, काठमाडौं उपत्यकामा ११ र लुम्बिनी प्रदेशमा १६ जना घाइते भएका छन्। देशभरका दुर्घटनामा कुल तीन जनाले ज्यान गुमाएका छन्।

मृत्यु हुनेमध्ये मोरङको विराटनगर महानगरपालिका ३ निवासी ५० वर्षीय अजयकुमार राजवंशी रहेका छन्। उनी साइकलमा घर फर्कने क्रममा अचानक खाल्डोमा परी गम्भीर घाइते भएका थिए। उपचारका लागि विराट टिचिङ अस्पताल लगिए पनि उपचारकै क्रममा चिकित्सकले मृत घोषणा गरेका थिए।

यस्तै, कास्कीको पोखरा महानगरपालिका १४ मा चेकजाँचबाट बच्न खोज्दा स्कुटर अनियन्त्रित भई दुर्घटना हुँदा पोखरा२६ निवासी १७ वर्षीय संयोग भण्डारी गम्भीर घाइते भएका थिए। उनलाई उपचारका लागि जीएमसी अस्पताल, पोखरा लगिएकोमा चिकित्सकले मृत घोषणा गरेका हुन्।

त्यसैगरी, नवलपरासी (पूर्व) को विनयी त्रिवेणी गाउँपालिका २ स्थित बिसहडी मोडमा अनियन्त्रित भएको रिक्सा दुर्घटनामा रूपन्देहीको देवदह नगरपालिका ९ निवासी ४९ वर्षीय शिव बर्याल गम्भीर घाइते भएका थिए। उपचारका लागि मध्यबिन्दु प्रादेशिक अस्पताल, डण्डा पुर्‍याइए पनि उपचारकै क्रममा उनको मृत्यु भएको प्रहरीले जनाएको छ।

articles.title: सहकारी ठगीका मुद्दा छिटो टुंग्याउन मन्त्री रावलले प्रधानन्यायाधीशलाई बुझाइन् प्रतिवेदन
articles.summary:
सहकारी ठगीसम्बन्धी मुद्दाको शीघ्र न्याय निरूपणका लागि मुद्दाको चाप बढी रहेका जिल्ला अदालतहरूमा तत्काल ‘सहकारी कसुर हेर्ने समर्पित इजलास’ गठन गर्न माग गर्दै भूमि व्यवस्था, सहकारी, संघीय मामिला तथा सामान्य प्रशासन मन्त्रालयले प्रधानन्यायाधीशलाई प्रतिवेदन बुझाएको छ।

उक्त विषय अध्ययन गर्न मन्त्रालयले कार्यदल गठन गरेको थियो। कार्यदलले बुझाएको प्रतिवेदनको सिफारिस अनुसार मन्त्रालयले समर्पित इजलास गठन गरिदिन सर्वोच्च अदालतमा अनुरोध गरेको हो।

सर्वोच्च अदालतले २०८२ माघ ११ गते जारी गरेको निर्देशनात्मक आदेशमा सहकारी कसुरसम्बन्धी मुद्दाको चाप बढी भएका जिल्ला अदालतहरूमा आवश्यकताअनुसार समर्पित इजलास स्थापना गर्न अध्ययन गरी निष्कर्षका आधारमा कार्यान्वयन गर्न भनेपछि मन्त्रालयले अध्ययन कार्यदल गठन गरेको थियो।

सहकारी क्षेत्रका समस्या समाधानलाई उच्च प्राथमिकता दिँदै मन्त्री प्रतिभा रावलले कार्यदलका सदस्यहरूसहित उक्त प्रतिवेदन सर्वोच्च अदालतका प्रधानन्यायाधीश डा. मनोज शर्मालाइ प्रतिवेदन बुझाएकी हुन्।

कार्यदलको प्रतिवेदनमा सहकारी कसुरलाई सामान्य ठगीको घटनाभन्दा फरक, ठूलो संख्यामा नागरिकको जीवन, सम्पत्ति र मुलुकको वित्तीय प्रणालीसँग प्रत्यक्ष सम्बन्धित सामाजिक–आर्थिक अपराधका रूपमा व्याख्या गरिएको छ। यस्ता मुद्दाको प्रभावकारी र छिटो सुनुवाइका लागि विशेष प्राथमिकतासहित समर्पित इजलास आवश्यक रहेको निष्कर्ष प्रतिवेदनले निकालेको छ।

प्रतिवेदनमा सहकारी ठगीका मुद्दा लामो समयसम्म विचाराधीन रहँदा पीडित बचतकर्ताले आफ्नो बचत फिर्ता पाउन नसक्ने, न्यायमा ढिलाइ हुने तथा दोषीलाई विभिन्न प्रकारका संरक्षण हुने जोखिम बढ्ने उल्लेख गरिएको छ। त्यसैले पीडितलाई समयमै न्याय दिलाउन, सहकारी क्षेत्रप्रतिको जनविश्वास पुनःस्थापित गर्न तथा वित्तीय सुशासन कायम गर्न समर्पित इजलास गठन अपरिहार्य रहेको कार्यदलको निष्कर्ष छ।

articles.title: Nepse drops 1.79 percent on cautious trading
articles.summary:
The Nepal Stock Exchange (Nepse) index snapped its recent rally this week, falling 49.06 points, or 1.79 percent, to close at 2,685.54 points during the trading week from July 27 to July 31.

Market activity also weakened as investors turned cautious, with weekly turnover dropping to Rs21.67 billion, down 23.51 percent from Rs28.33 billion in the previous week. Average daily turnover fell to Rs4.33 billion from Rs5.66 billion.

The decline wiped out Rs80 billion in market value, with overall market capitalisation shrinking to Rs4.62 trillion from Rs4.70 trillion.

Other major indices also ended lower. The Sensitive Index declined 3.34 points, or 0.71 percent, to 470.13 points, while the Float Index dropped 2.81 points, or 1.50 percent, to 184.59 points. The Sensitive Float Index fell 1.05 points, or 0.65 percent, to close at 159.48 points.

The downturn was broad-based, with 12 of Nepse’s 13 sub-indices ending the week in negative territory. The Commercial Banking sub-index was the only sector to post gains, rising 2.17 points, or 0.15 percent, to 1,491.29 points.

The Manufacturing and Processing sub-index recorded the steepest fall, declining 389.63 points, or 3.53 percent, to 10,659.55 points. Development Banks and Hydropower also saw sharp losses, dropping 2.82 percent and 2.63 percent respectively.

Newly listed Everest Colour Limited led the gainers, surging 101.09 percent to close at Rs1,309.30. Saptakoshi Development Bank gained 6.56 percent to Rs858.90, while Global IME Bank rose 5.01 percent to Rs262.

Corporate Development Bank was the biggest loser, falling 27.70 percent to Rs1,120. Aatmanirbhar Laghubitta and Reliance Spinning Mills declined 15.17 percent and 14.17 percent respectively.

Reliance Spinning Mills recorded the highest turnover during the week at Rs1.038 billion, followed by Ridi Power with Rs858.3 million and Central Finance with Rs834.2 million. Global IME Bank had the highest trading volume, with 2.988 million shares changing hands.

Market analyst Jagannath Dhungel said profit booking contributed to the decline, as some traders opted to exit after the recent rise. However, he said institutional investors had started entering the market gradually.

“Companies’ financial performance is expected to improve. But investors are waiting for government policies and assurances to translate into results,” Dhungel said.

An experienced investor, who requested anonymity, said unrest in the Tarai may have affected market sentiment, but it was only one of several factors behind the decline. He said institutional investors, considered the backbone of the capital market, remained unconvinced about the government’s commitment to implementing policies supporting the market.

He also pointed to ongoing investigations into capital market-related incidents as a factor weighing on investor confidence.

“Investor confidence remains weak due to oversupply, uncertainty surrounding investigations, and poor financial health of many listed companies,” he said.

The investor said investigations into market-related issues should be carried out through established regulatory channels. The Securities Board of Nepal is the designated market regulator and should be allowed to perform its role, he said.

He cautioned that investigations launched in the name of good governance should also consider their wider impact on the economy.

Despite the short-term pressure, he said the recent movement in the banking sector, which is considered a fundamental driver of the market, suggests institutional investors may be gradually returning, which could support the market over the longer term.

articles.title: Source code theft emerges as a growing threat to Nepal’s software industry
articles.summary:
Every software application people use is built through years of engineering effort and significant financial investment. But when the source code, the underlying codebase that forms the backbone of a software product, is stolen, copied and repackaged under a different name, software companies can lose both their competitive edge and their business.

The problem is becoming increasingly common in Nepal. In the last fiscal year 2025-26, the Cyber Bureau of Nepal Police received 10 complaints involving the theft of computer source code. The Nepal Copyright Registrar’s Office also received similar complaints, some of which have already reached the courts. As demand for digital systems continues to grow, software piracy has emerged as a serious commercial threat to technology companies.

A case filed recently at the Kathmandu District Court illustrates the scale of the problem.

Kathmandu-based Diyalo Technologies Pvt Ltd developed an enterprise resource planning (ERP) platform called WaterMark for water distribution and customer management. According to the company, several former employees later left, established a new company called Wash TechNepal, and launched a competing product, WashBilling, which allegedly replicated Diyalo’s software.

PR Khanal, chief executive officer of Diyalo Technologies, said the company became suspicious after learning that a strikingly similar product had entered the market.

“The software looked almost identical in both appearance and functionality,” Khanal said. “When our technical experts examined the fonts and code architecture, they found clear evidence of copying. The logical structure, database design and coding patterns all matched ours. Even spelling mistakes embedded in our source code were reproduced exactly. That prompted us to file a complaint with the Cyber Bureau. Since the identical errors appearing independently would be virtually impossible, the police presented them before the court as strong evidence of source code theft.”

Following an investigation by the Cyber Bureau, the District Government Attorney Office, Kathmandu, filed charges against five individuals. Prosecutors claim the defendants copied Diyalo’s source code and sold the resulting software to several community drinking water committees in Kaski district.

Khanal says the incident is far from isolated.

“Over the past few years, several other Nepali software companies have also had their source codes stolen,” he said.

According to Chandra Bilash Bhurtel, general secretary of the Federation of Computer Association Nepal (CAN Federation), the problem is particularly prevalent in accounting software and financial technology products.

“In most cases, employees who are dissatisfied with their organisations or frequently change jobs replicate the products of companies they previously worked for after moving elsewhere,” Bhurtel said. “Proving source code theft is technically difficult. Investigators must conduct a detailed comparison of database architecture, internal data structures and other technical elements. Since many software components are available through open-source platforms, determining what constitutes proprietary code and what is publicly available often becomes a complex legal and technical challenge.”

Most complaints received by the Cyber Bureau point to insiders or former employees rather than external hackers.

Cybersecurity experts say Nepal experiences relatively few sophisticated cyberattacks compared with internal fraud. Employees with legitimate access to software systems often misuse that access to copy or sell proprietary code.

One case involved an online learning platform whose former employee allegedly stole the source code and sold it to a competitor. The Cyber Bureau began investigating, but the complaint was later withdrawn after both parties settled outside of court. According to officials familiar with the case, the accused feared the impact on their career, while the company sought to avoid reputational damage through a public legal battle.

Dilip Kumar Giri, spokesperson for the Cyber Bureau, said outsiders rarely succeed in stealing source code because access is tightly controlled within companies.

“Most cases involve insiders who see a commercial opportunity, leave the company and either establish their own business or sell the code to competitors,” Giri said.

He added that investigators are also dealing with fake versions of government websites created to harvest sensitive user information.

One recent case involved a counterfeit version of Nepal’s Nagarik App portal hosted on a privately owned domain. Nepali technology news outlet TechPana reported that developer Nirdesh Subedi had recreated the application’s previous interface to produce a website that closely resembled the official platform. After concerns were raised that the cloned site could be used to steal users’ personal information, Subedi modified the website by removing the copied interface and replacing it with a separate login page.

The issue extends beyond outright theft.

Government reports have also highlighted the risks created when public agencies procure software without obtaining ownership of the underlying source code.

A committee formed to recommend information technology reforms for the Ministry of Finance and its subordinate agencies found that several proprietary software systems used in public financial management had been purchased without source code ownership. As a result, government agencies remain fully dependent on vendors whenever they need to modify, upgrade or troubleshoot those systems.

Legal experts say prosecuting source code theft remains difficult because the cases require both legal interpretation and highly specialised technical expertise.

Advocate Atit Rijal, who has handled such cases, said Nepal’s courts and investigative agencies still lack sufficient expertise to fully understand the complexity and commercial significance of software source code.

Although Section 44 of the Electronic Transactions Act, 2008, criminalises the theft of computer source code, he argues that the penalties are too weak to deter offenders.

“The maximum punishment is three years’ imprisonment or a fine of up to Rs200,000,” Rijal said. “Most defendants are released on bail with relative ease. They continue using the stolen code while the case is pending and often make substantial profits before the legal process concludes. Ultimately, the consequences are minimal. The law does little to discourage this type of crime.”

In some cases, lawyers say, victims struggle to obtain justice because software piracy is still viewed as little more than ordinary business competition.

One advocate recalled that during a court hearing on a source code theft case, a judge questioned the government prosecutor by asking: “If I’m selling instant noodles, does that mean nobody else in the world can sell the same brand of noodles?”

The lawyer described the comparison as both inappropriate and absurd.

“Source code theft cannot be equated with ordinary market competition,” he said. “There is still a significant lack of understanding within Nepal’s legal profession and judiciary about software-related crimes.”

Source code is the human-readable programming language developers write to create software, applications and computer programs. Nepal’s Electronic Transactions Act defines it as “computer source code”, including programme listings, commands, computer designs and layouts.

In practical terms, source code contains the software’s underlying logic, database architecture, programming structure and variable naming conventions. It represents the intellectual property at the core of a software company’s business.

Baburam Aryal, a cyber law expert, said that although Nepali courts have convicted defendants in source code theft cases, securing adequate compensation for victims remains a major challenge.

“The courts still lack a consistent methodology for calculating damages,” Aryal said. “As a result, companies often win the legal case but still fail to receive meaningful compensation for the commercial losses they have suffered.”

He said confidentiality agreements between employers and employees provide some legal protection, but are rarely enough to stop someone determined to steal proprietary code.

Rijal believes many companies weaken their own legal position by failing to require employees to sign robust non-disclosure agreements when they are hired.

Gaurav Raj Pandey, president of the Nepal Association for Software and IT Services Companies (NAS-IT) and chief executive of EKbana Solutions, warned that weak intellectual property protection threatens far more than individual software companies.

“If intellectual property cannot be protected, it undermines the entire knowledge economy,” he said. “Investors become reluctant to make large investments, and ultimately the growth of Nepal’s technology industry suffers.”

The problem is far from unique to Nepal.

Around the world, source code theft has become an increasingly serious concern for software companies. One of the most high-profile recent examples involved a supply chain attack targeting US-based technology firm Cisco. Attackers exploited vulnerabilities in software developed by Trivy, an open-source security scanner, to gain access to more than 300 GitHub repositories and steal source code linked to Cisco’s artificial intelligence products.

The rapid rise of generative AI has introduced new risks. Experts say even individuals with only basic programming knowledge can now use AI tools to modify stolen source code and quickly develop competing software.

AI has also created new legal uncertainty. As more software is produced with the assistance of AI tools or through so-called “vibe coding”, questions are emerging over who owns the intellectual property when AI-generated or AI-assisted source code is copied or stolen.

Industry experts say addressing these risks requires both stronger legal safeguards and tighter technical controls.

Companies should implement mandatory confidentiality agreements and comprehensive employment policies covering intellectual property when staff are hired and when they leave the organisation.

“They need stricter access controls for source code, regular security audits and better employee awareness about the legal consequences of intellectual property theft,” said Khanal. “At the same time, the government should amend the Electronic Transactions Act to strengthen protection for digital assets and establish a modern framework for compensation that reflects today’s technology industry.”

articles.title: Curfews lifted in parts of Madhesh as tensions ease
articles.summary:
Security restrictions have been eased in parts of Madhesh and the eastern Tarai after authorities reviewed the security situation following the Sunsari incidents.

On Saturday, curfew was lifted in the Janakpur area of Dhanusha and Lahan of Siraha, while prohibitory orders restricting public gatherings were introduced in some areas. Curfew remains in force in Golbazar of Siraha.

In Dhanusha, the administration lifted the curfew in the Janakpur area from 10 am on Saturday. Chief District Officer Prem Prasad Luitel said restrictions on gatherings remain in place in areas including Laxminiya, Nagarain, Belauni Road, Sinurjoda, Sohani, Manimandap, ISKCON Janakpur and Dudhmatipul until further notice.

Under the restrictions, gatherings of more than five people, as well as assemblies, processions and demonstrations, have been prohibited in the designated areas.

In Siraha, the administration also lifted the curfew in Lahan from 10 am on Saturday after reviewing the latest security situation, according to Chief District Officer Surendra Paudel.

Curfew remains in place in Golbazar despite signs of improvement, with the administration saying a further decision would be taken after assessing the situation there.

Authorities had imposed curfews and prohibitory orders in several districts across the eastern Tarai after protests and tensions intensified following incidents in Sunsari’s Kaptanganj.

District administrations said the situation was gradually returning to normal and urged residents to comply with restrictions aimed at maintaining peace, public order and communal harmony.

They warned that anyone violating the orders would face action under prevailing laws.

articles.title: ब्रोड पिक हिमपहिरो : आठ जनाको शव फेला पारेको दाबी, निर्मल पुर्जासहित दुईको खोजी हुँदै
articles.summary:
पाकिस्तानमा अवस्थित विश्वकै १२औँ अग्लो ब्रोड पिक (आठ हजार ४७ मिटर) हिमालमा गएको विनाशकारी हिमपहिरोमा परी बेपत्ता भएका पर्वतारोहीहरूको खोजी तथा उद्धार कार्य तीव्र पारिएको छ।

पाकिस्तानको प्रतिष्ठित सञ्चारमाध्यम जियो न्युजले उल्लेख गरे अनुसार हिमपहिरोमा परेका १० सदस्यीय अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय आरोहण दलका सदस्यहरूमध्ये हालसम्म आठ जनाको शव फेला परिसकेको छ भने बाँकी दुई जना पर्वतारोहीहरूको खोजी भइरहेको छ।

ब्रोड पिक बेस क्याम्पबाट बाहिर आएका रिपोर्टहरूले हिमपहिरोमा परेका सबै पर्वतारोहीको मृत्यु भएको हुन सक्ने आशंका व्यक्त गरेका छन्। यद्यपि, यी रिपोर्टहरूलाई पाकिस्तानी अधिकारीहरू वा पाकिस्तानको अल्पाइन क्लबले आधिकारिक रूपमा पुष्टि गरेका छैनन्।

बिहीबार बिहान हिमालको क्याम्प तीन नजिकै छ हजार ६ सय मिटरको उचाइमा आरोही टोलीमाथि हिमपहिरो खसेको थियो। प्रतिकूल मौसमका कारण शुक्रबार स्थगित भएको उद्धार कार्य शनिबार बिहानैदेखि पुनः सुचारु गरिएको हो। फेला परेका शवहरूमध्ये ओमानकी नाधिरा अहमद अब्दुल्लाह अल हार्थी, नेपालका पुरबहादुर गुरुङ (युक्त) र अमेरिकी म्यालोरी गीसको पहिचान भइसकेको छ भने अन्य शवहरूको पहिचान खुलाउने प्रयास भइरहेको छ।

उक्त अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय टोलीको नेतृत्व विश्वप्रसिद्ध नेपाली पर्वतारोही निर्मल पुर्जा (निम्स) ले गरेका थिए। हालसम्म फेला परेका शवहरूमा पुर्जा नपरेको र उनीसहित दुई जना अझै बेपत्ता सूचीमा रहेको जियो न्युजले जनाएको छ। ४३ वर्षीय पुर्जाले यसै हप्ता सामाजिक सञ्जाल एक्समार्फत अक्सिजनबिना दोस्रो पटक विश्वका सबै १४ वटा आठ हजार मिटरभन्दा अग्ला हिमाल आरोहण गर्ने कीर्तिमानको नजिक पुगेको जानकारी गराएका थिए।

यस घटनामा नेपालका प्रसिद्ध पर्वतारोहीहरू किली पेम्बा शेर्पा, निमा शेर्पा, नवाङ थिन्डु शेर्पा, ग्यालु शेर्पा, पाकिस्तानका सोहेल सखी तथा चीनका वाङ झोङ पनि समावेश थिए। बेपत्ता आरोहीहरूको खोजीका लागि अर्का चर्चित नेपाली पर्वतारोही मिङ्मा ग्याबु शेर्पाको नेतृत्वमा तीन सदस्यीय नेपाली उद्धार टोली ब्रोड पिकको आधार शिविर पुगिसकेको छ। यस्तै, बेलायती उद्धार टोली पनि पाकिस्तान आइपुग्ने क्रममा रहेको छ भने सरबाज खानको नेतृत्वमा उद्धार कार्य जारी छ।

उद्धार टोलीका अनुसार ड्रोन फुटेजमा हिमालको माथिल्लो भागमा थप शवहरू देखिएका छन्। तर बाक्लो हिउँ, निरन्तरको खराब मौसम, थप हिमपहिरोको जोखिम र कठिन भूभागका कारण उद्धार कार्य निकै चुनौतीपूर्ण बनेको छ। अहिले पाकिस्तानी सेनाको हेलिकप्टर र जमिनबाट उद्धारकर्मीहरूले एकसाथ खोजी कार्य जारी राखेका छन्।

पाकिस्तानको अल्पाइन क्लबकी नायला कियानीका अनुसार आरोहीहरूको ट्र्याकिङ उपकरण (जीपीएस) बाट प्राप्त तथ्यांकले उनीहरू पहाडको किनारबाट सयौँ मिटर तल खसेको संकेत गरेको छ। उत्तर पाकिस्तानको काराकोरम पर्वत श्रृंखलामा पर्ने ब्रोड पिक प्राविधिक रूपमा अत्यन्तै कठिन र जोखिमपूर्ण हिमाल मानिन्छ, जसको पहिलो पटक सन् १९५७ मा अस्ट्रियाली टोलीले आरोहण गरेको थियो।

articles.title: डा शशांकले भने: शेखर दाइ कार्यव्यस्तताले नआउनुभएको हो, उहाँको समर्थन छ
articles.summary:
नेपाली कांग्रेसका पूर्वसभापति शेरबहादुर देउवा निकट समूहले आगामी राष्ट्रिय भेलाको तयारीबारे जानकारी दिन शनिबार काठमाडौंको चुनदेवीस्थित सम्पर्क कार्यालयमा पत्रकार सम्मेलन आयोजना गरेको छ।

पत्रकार सम्मेलनमा समूहले पूर्वमहामन्त्री डा. शशांक कोइरालाको नेतृत्वमा ५५१ सदस्यीय आयोजक समिति गठन गरिएको जानकारी दिएको छ। भेलालाई व्यवस्थित र प्रभावकारी रूपमा सम्पन्न गर्न १६ वटा विभिन्न तयारी समिति समेत गठन गरिएको नेता मीन विश्वकर्माले बताए।

कार्यक्रममा देउवा समूहका अधिकांश शीर्ष नेताहरूको उपस्थिति रहे पनि पछिल्लो समय सोही समूहसँग नजिक देखिएका नेता डा. शेखर कोइराला भने उपस्थित भएनन्।

उनको अनुपस्थितिबारे सञ्चारकर्मीको जिज्ञासामा डा. शशांक कोइरालाले आफूले पटक–पटक सहभागी हुन आग्रह गरे पनि कार्यव्यस्तताका कारण आउन नसकेको जानकारी दिएका बताए।

उनका अनुसार, डा. शेखरले भेलाप्रति आफ्नो पूर्ण समर्थन रहेको जनाउँदै उपस्थित हुन नसकेकोमा क्षमायाचना गरेका छन्।

शशांकले भने, "शेखर दाइसँग मैले पटक–पटक अनुरोध गरेँ। उहाँले व्यस्तताका कारण आउन नसक्ने बताउनुभयो। 'मेरो सहमति त छँदै छ, समाचारमार्फत पनि मेरो समर्थन रहेको जानकारी दिनुहोस्। आउन नसकेकोमा क्षमा चाहन्छु,' भनेर उहाँले भन्नुभएको छ।"

articles.title: सार्वजनिक बिदामा पनि राहदानी सेवा सञ्चालन
articles.summary:
सेवाग्राहीको बढ्दो चापलाई व्यवस्थापन गर्न राहदानी विभागले दुई ‘सिफ्ट’ का साथै बिदाका दिन पनि सेवा सञ्चालन गरेको छ। त्रिपुरेश्वरथित विभागमा आज शनिबार पनि सेवा प्रवाह भइरहेको जनाइएको छ।

विभागमा यही साउन १४ गते देखि दुई सिफ्टमा सेवा दिँदै दैनिक एक हजार ५०० आवेदन फाराम खुलाइएको छ। कोरियाको रोजगार अनुमति प्रणाली (इपिएस) का लागि आवेदन दिएका नेपाली सेवाग्राहीलाई सहजता प्रदान गर्न विभागले विद्युतीय राहदानीसम्बन्धी सेवा साउन १४ गतेदेखि २२ गतेसम्म दुई सिफ्टमा सञ्चालन गरिएको विभागले जनाएको छ।

सो अवधिमा पहिलो सिफ्ट बिहान ७ः०० बजेदेखि दिउँसो २ः०० बजेसम्म र दोस्रो सिफ्ट दिउँसो २ः०० बजेदेखि बेलुकी ९ः०० बजेसम्म सञ्चालन हुनेछ। सार्वजनिक बिदाका दिन शनिबार र आइतबारसमेत बिहान १०ः०० बजेदेखि बेलुकी ४ः०० बजेसम्म विभागबाट सेवा प्रवाह हुनेछ।

articles.title: कोदो खेती गर्ने किसान सम्मानित
articles.summary:
