दोस्रो राष्ट्रिय कोदो दिवसको अवसरमा सिन्धुलीमा कोदोजन्य बालीको उत्पादन, संरक्षण र प्रवर्द्धनमा उल्लेखनीय योगदान पुर्‍याउने १० जना कृषक सम्मानित भएका छन्। जिल्लाका विभिन्न स्थानीय तहमा कोदो खेती गर्दै आएका १० जना किसानलाई जिल्ला कृषि विकास कार्यालय सिन्धुलीले सम्मान गरेको हो।

किसानलाई सम्मानपत्र प्रदान गर्दै कार्यालयले कोदो खेतीको संरक्षण, उत्पादन वृद्धि र बजारीकरणमा थप प्रोत्साहन गर्ने उद्देश्य रहेको जनाएको छ।

कार्यक्रममा कृषि विकास कार्यालय सिन्धुलीका प्रमुख अनुप अधिकारीले जिल्लामा हाल १० हजार ७४२ हेक्टर क्षेत्रफलमा कोदो खेती भइरहेको जानकारी दिए। उनका अनुसार कोदो पोषणयुक्त, जलवायु परिवर्तनको असर कम पर्ने तथा कम लागतमा उत्पादन गर्न सकिने महत्वपूर्ण खाद्यान्न बाली भएकाले यसको उत्पादन र उपभोग दुवैलाई प्राथमिकता दिन आवश्यक छ।

उनले कोदोबाट बन्ने विभिन्न परिकार, यसको पोषण मूल्य, स्वास्थ्यमा पुग्ने फाइदा तथा उत्पादनको वर्तमान अवस्थाबारे जानकारी गराउँदै परम्परागत बालीको संरक्षणसँगै आधुनिक कृषि प्रविधिको प्रयोग गरेर उत्पादन बढाउनुपर्नेमा जोड दिए।

कार्यक्रमका प्रमुख अतिथि जिल्ला समन्वय समिति सिन्धुलीका प्रमुख कार्साङ लामाले कोदो खेतीले किसानको आयआर्जन वृद्धि गर्नुका साथै स्थानीय खाद्य सुरक्षामा समेत महत्वपूर्ण योगदान पुर्‍याउने बताए। पछिल्लो समय युवापुस्ताको कोदो खेतीप्रतिको आकर्षण घट्दै गएको उल्लेख गर्दै उनले स्थानीय तह, कृषि कार्यालय र सरोकारवाला निकायबीचको सहकार्यबाट किसानलाई थप प्रोत्साहन गर्नुपर्ने धारणा राखे।

सम्मानित कृषकहरूको अनुभव र सफलताले अन्य किसानलाई पनि व्यावसायिक रूपमा कोदो खेतीतर्फ आकर्षित गर्ने विश्वास व्यक्त गर्दै उनले उत्पादनसँगै प्रशोधन र बजार विस्तारमा ध्यान दिन आग्रह गरे।

उद्योग वाणिज्य संघ सिन्धुलीका अध्यक्ष अर्जुन श्रेष्ठले कोदोबाट उत्पादन हुने विभिन्न खाद्य परिकारको व्यावसायिक विकास, ब्रान्डिङ र बजारीकरणमा जोड दिए। विशेषगरी कोदोबाट बन्ने परम्परागत मदिरा तथा अन्य परिकारलाई गुणस्तरीय रूपमा उत्पादन गरी कानुनी र कर प्रणालीभित्र ल्याउन सके बजार विस्तार हुने र किसानले उत्पादनको उचित मूल्य प्राप्त गर्ने बताए। स्थानीय उत्पादनलाई आधुनिक बजारसँग जोड्न सके कोदो खेतीलाई थप लाभदायी व्यवसायका रूपमा विकास गर्न सकिने उनको भनाइ थियो।

कार्यक्रममा जनप्रतिनिधि, कृषि क्षेत्रका सरोकारवाला निकाय, कृषक तथा विभिन्न संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधिको सहभागिता रहेको थियो। सहभागीहरूले कोदो उत्पादन वृद्धि, मूल्य अभिवृद्धि, प्रशोधन उद्योगको विकास, प्रभावकारी बजारीकरण तथा उपभोग प्रवर्द्धनका लागि सरकारी तथा निजी क्षेत्रबीच सहकार्य अपरिहार्य रहेकोमा जोड दिएका थिए।

दिवसको अवसरमा कोदोको महत्वबारे सर्वसाधारणलाई जानकारी गराउने उद्देश्यले सिन्धुलीमाढीस्थित लोकतान्त्रिक चौतारामा कोदोबाट बनेका विभिन्न परिकारको प्रदर्शनीसमेत गरिएको थियो। प्रदर्शनीमा कोदोको मिठाई, ढिँडो, रोटी, सेललगायत परिकार राखिएका थिए। स्थानीय उपभोक्ताले ती परिकारको स्वाद लिँदै कोदोको पोषण तथा व्यावसायिक सम्भावनाबारे जानकारी लिएका थिए।

आयोजकका अनुसार यस्ता कार्यक्रमले परम्परागत बालीको संरक्षण, किसानको उत्साह वृद्धि तथा स्थानीय उत्पादनको बजार विस्तारमा सकारात्मक योगदान पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

articles.title: ब्रोड पिक हिमपहिरो : आठ जनाको शव फेला पारेको दाबी, निर्मल पुर्जासहित दुईको खोजी हुँदै
articles.summary:
पाकिस्तानमा अवस्थित विश्वकै १२औँ अग्लो ब्रोड पिक (आठ हजार ४७ मिटर) हिमालमा गएको विनाशकारी हिमपहिरोमा परी बेपत्ता भएका पर्वतारोहीहरूको खोजी तथा उद्धार कार्य तीव्र पारिएको छ।

पाकिस्तानको प्रतिष्ठित सञ्चारमाध्यम जियो न्युजले उल्लेख गरे अनुसार हिमपहिरोमा परेका १० सदस्यीय अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय आरोहण दलका सदस्यहरूमध्ये हालसम्म आठ जनाको शव फेला परिसकेको छ भने बाँकी दुई जना पर्वतारोहीहरूको खोजी भइरहेको छ।

ब्रोड पिक बेस क्याम्पबाट बाहिर आएका रिपोर्टहरूले हिमपहिरोमा परेका सबै पर्वतारोहीको मृत्यु भएको हुन सक्ने आशंका व्यक्त गरेका छन्। यद्यपि, यी रिपोर्टहरूलाई पाकिस्तानी अधिकारीहरू वा पाकिस्तानको अल्पाइन क्लबले आधिकारिक रूपमा पुष्टि गरेका छैनन्।

बिहीबार बिहान हिमालको क्याम्प तीन नजिकै छ हजार ६ सय मिटरको उचाइमा आरोही टोलीमाथि हिमपहिरो खसेको थियो। प्रतिकूल मौसमका कारण शुक्रबार स्थगित भएको उद्धार कार्य शनिबार बिहानैदेखि पुनः सुचारु गरिएको हो। फेला परेका शवहरूमध्ये ओमानकी नाधिरा अहमद अब्दुल्लाह अल हार्थी, नेपालका पुरबहादुर गुरुङ (युक्त) र अमेरिकी म्यालोरी गीसको पहिचान भइसकेको छ भने अन्य शवहरूको पहिचान खुलाउने प्रयास भइरहेको छ।

उक्त अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय टोलीको नेतृत्व विश्वप्रसिद्ध नेपाली पर्वतारोही निर्मल पुर्जा (निम्स) ले गरेका थिए। हालसम्म फेला परेका शवहरूमा पुर्जा नपरेको र उनीसहित दुई जना अझै बेपत्ता सूचीमा रहेको जियो न्युजले जनाएको छ। ४३ वर्षीय पुर्जाले यसै हप्ता सामाजिक सञ्जाल एक्समार्फत अक्सिजनबिना दोस्रो पटक विश्वका सबै १४ वटा आठ हजार मिटरभन्दा अग्ला हिमाल आरोहण गर्ने कीर्तिमानको नजिक पुगेको जानकारी गराएका थिए।

यस घटनामा नेपालका प्रसिद्ध पर्वतारोहीहरू किली पेम्बा शेर्पा, निमा शेर्पा, नवाङ थिन्डु शेर्पा, ग्यालु शेर्पा, पाकिस्तानका सोहेल सखी तथा चीनका वाङ झोङ पनि समावेश थिए। बेपत्ता आरोहीहरूको खोजीका लागि अर्का चर्चित नेपाली पर्वतारोही मिङ्मा ग्याबु शेर्पाको नेतृत्वमा तीन सदस्यीय नेपाली उद्धार टोली ब्रोड पिकको आधार शिविर पुगिसकेको छ। यस्तै, बेलायती उद्धार टोली पनि पाकिस्तान आइपुग्ने क्रममा रहेको छ भने सरबाज खानको नेतृत्वमा उद्धार कार्य जारी छ।

उद्धार टोलीका अनुसार ड्रोन फुटेजमा हिमालको माथिल्लो भागमा थप शवहरू देखिएका छन्। तर बाक्लो हिउँ, निरन्तरको खराब मौसम, थप हिमपहिरोको जोखिम र कठिन भूभागका कारण उद्धार कार्य निकै चुनौतीपूर्ण बनेको छ। अहिले पाकिस्तानी सेनाको हेलिकप्टर र जमिनबाट उद्धारकर्मीहरूले एकसाथ खोजी कार्य जारी राखेका छन्।

पाकिस्तानको अल्पाइन क्लबकी नायला कियानीका अनुसार आरोहीहरूको ट्र्याकिङ उपकरण (जीपीएस) बाट प्राप्त तथ्यांकले उनीहरू पहाडको किनारबाट सयौँ मिटर तल खसेको संकेत गरेको छ। उत्तर पाकिस्तानको काराकोरम पर्वत श्रृंखलामा पर्ने ब्रोड पिक प्राविधिक रूपमा अत्यन्तै कठिन र जोखिमपूर्ण हिमाल मानिन्छ, जसको पहिलो पटक सन् १९५७ मा अस्ट्रियाली टोलीले आरोहण गरेको थियो।

articles.title: Why Nepal’s communal tensions keep returning
articles.summary:
This essay was originally published in Kalam Weekly.

8PM on Thursday, July 30, five days after sectarian violence in Nepal’s Terai-Madhesh plains killed three, injured dozens, and saw mass arson and vandalism, Prime Minister Balen Shah finally addressed the nation. Reading gravely off a teleprompter, Shah was somber, expressing sorrow for the dead and injured and calling for calm. It was one of the few instances where Shah discarded any bluster and bravado, choosing instead a restrained address that called on the public to not blame or target any single community for what is happening. It took a national crisis for Shah to finally discard his dark sunglasses and address the nation.

The Madhesh is in flames. Mobs armed with sticks and spears roam the streets, threatening and assaulting anyone they think belongs to a different religion. Homes and businesses have been burned down despite the Nepal Police, the Armed Police Force, and Nepal Army all being out in force. Three civilians have died from police bullets. Social media is stoking the fire. Anonymous or fake accounts on Facebook, TikTok, and Twitter are amplifying hateful rhetoric, spreading misinformation that Rohingya refugees are behind the carnage, that hordes of Muslims are coming in from India to take revenge, and that Nepal’s Hindus are under attack from its minority Muslims.

How did we get here?

Things began, as they often do, with a minor dispute.

On Sunday, July 26, a Hindu procession was marching towards Kaptangunj Chowk in Sunsari District’s Dewangunj Rural Municipality with water from the Koshi Barrage for the Bol Bam festival. In the Nepali month of Shrawan, Hindus don saffron robes and carry holy water in pots to offer at Shiva temples, all while chanting ‘Bol Bam’ and playing music. The procession was allegedly stopped by members of the Muslim community, who protested the playing of loud devotional music. Earlier in the day, Hindus, again allegedly, had removed a Muslim flag in the area and replaced it with a Hindu one, leading to heightened tensions.

The fracas over the Bol Bam procession and the loud music escalated, leading to a large gathering of members from both communities. As videos and images of the confrontation spread on social media, more individuals from both communities arrived, sometimes armed with improvised weapons. As the two groups faced off, the Nepal Police attempted to intervene, but things quickly spiraled out of control. Each side began pelting the other with stones, with the security forces caught in the middle. The confrontation grew more violent and continued well into the night. The Armed Police Force was mobilized to contain the mob with baton charges and tear gas. It does not seem that the police employed rubber bullets before resorting to live ammunition. Locals claim that shots rang out when the protest area was suddenly plunged into darkness. Thirty-year-old Om Prakash Mehta was struck under the left armpit and died while being taken to hospital. At least nine others were also hit by bullets fired by the security forces, mostly above the waist.

Mehta’s death and the shootings only inflamed tensions, with Hindus believing that the police had taken the side of the Muslims to fire towards them. Despite a curfew order in place, large crowds of Hindus and Muslims gathered in Kaptangunj and other nearby areas, with demonstrations spreading to nearby districts like Sarlahi, Dhanusha, Saptari, and Siraha, including the Madhesh Province capital of Janakpur. On Thursday, two more deaths were announced. Twenty-year-old Jaya Prakash Mehta died while undergoing treatment for injuries sustained during Sunday’s clash, and 17-year-old Ganesh Yadav died after being shot in the neck by security forces in Siraha’s Golbazaar. As of writing on Friday afternoon, large swathes of Madhesh Province remain tense with heavily armed police and army men patrolling the streets.

A history of violence

The ‘Sunsari incident,’ as it is being called, is just one more instance in a worrying escalation of communal violence in the Madhesh-Terai. It always seems to start the same way, where one community accuses the other of disrupting their religious celebrations and violence breaks out. Almost always, there is provocation. Religious processions are often deliberately routed through neighborhoods dominated by other religious communities. These processions play devotional music, colloquially known as ‘DJ’, through large, portable speakers, often well into the night. Any complaint or request to turn down the music is interpreted as an attack on their religion and has the potential to turn into a religious melee.

The year 2026 itself began with a communal clash in Birgunj over an allegedly provocative TikTok video shared by two Muslim youth. On January 4, the duo was corralled by local Hindus and handed over to the police, but that did not alleviate their anger. Hindus vandalized a mosque and Muslim households in Dhanusha and Parsa districts, allegedly even burning copies of the Quran. The violence and arson spread across the two districts, leading local administrations to institute a curfew and appeal to local community leaders to press for peace and dialogue.

That same month, on January 26, a clash broke out in Paroha Municipality of Rautahat district over a Hindu procession that was attempting a ritual immersion of a Saraswati idol in a nearby river. The procession was allegedly pelted with stones by members of the Muslim community, although it remains unclear what exactly incited them to do so. Again, the security forces had to intervene to prevent violence from breaking out.

Rautahat district, according to the 2021 census, has the highest concentration of Muslims in the country at 22.5 percent of the total population, and it is where clashes often break out between the minority Muslims and the majority Hindus. In February, a curfew had to be imposed on the city of Gaur in Rautahat district when clashes broke out after Muslims accused a Hindu wedding procession of playing loud DJ music near a local mosque. Hindus accused Muslims of pelting the wedding procession with stones, leading the Hindu community to retaliate by setting a mosque on fire. The Nepal Police and Armed Police Force enforced a curfew for several days before the riots came under control.

Communal clashes like these are becoming increasingly more frequent. The Armed Police Force reportedly documented 25 incidents of religious or ethnic conflict between the fiscal years 2020-21 and 2023-24. The rise in such incidents is not coincidental; there appears to be a concerted push by unsavory actors both in India and across the border in India to inflame tensions and reap political dividends. In 2023, there were reports of Muslims being told to “go back to Pakistan” during a Hindu-Muslim clash, and even today, there are videos circulating of Hindu mobs stopping Muslims to force them to chant ‘Jai Shree Ram.’ These are tactics imported from across the border.

Why the Madhesh?

For one, the Terai houses the largest concentration of Muslims in Nepal. Around 96 percent of Muslims live in the Terai plains while just around 4-5 percent live in the hills and urban centers like Kathmandu. Muslims in the Madhesh are thus a solid demographic bloc with socio-political power, not just token minorities. But despite this, Muslims sit at the intersection of two marginalised histories that often don’t overlap. Politically, they are Madhesis, but religiously, they are Muslims. They share the broad Madhesi concern with political marginalization, but their interests are distinct. Their representation in political parties is often token and instrumentalized. When there are issues, Muslims often find that they have no channels to express their grievances beyond their community.

There have always been tensions in the Madhesh-Terai between members of different communities, Hindu-Muslim or Madheshi-Pahadi. But these tensions have remained localized, with community leaders quick to step in and diffuse tensions. But we now live in the time of social media, and misinformation has already spread far and wide before local leaders can even call a deescalatory meeting. The Madhesh also sits along an open border and has deep kinship ties with Indians. Thus, the politics of religion as it plays out in the bordering states of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh easily seeps into the Madhesh. This isn’t about Hindus in the hills importing narratives from the West but about close families and relatives consuming the same media and sharing the same political consciousness. It doesn’t help that Uttar Pradesh is currently run by Yogi Adityanath, a deeply conservative radical Hindu priest who has expressed support for Nepal reverting to a Hindu kingdom.

Social media is also rife with narratives of cultural incompatibility and demographic replacement that are borrowed from the right wing in India and the West. Bad actors are pushing the argument that the Muslim population is growing exponentially and could soon threaten Nepal’s Hindu majority while ignoring the fact that Nepal’s Hindu population sits at around 82 percent, the largest in the world, while Muslims are just 5 percent, a 1 percent growth in the past three decades. But this argument doesn’t have to hold water; all it needs to do is lodge itself in idle, susceptible minds until the next time a minor dispute with a Muslim person arises.

Finally, there is federalism, or a lack of it. Despite officially being declared a federal republic in 2015, Nepal’s provinces remain legislatively hamstrung by the federal center in Kathmandu. Provinces do not have their own civil service or their own provincial police, although mandated by the constitution. So whenever something like Sunsari happens, the decisions on when and how to deploy the police are made by officials in Kathmandu. Provincial authorities have little say and often overridden by federal ministries. Instead of seeking dialogue in the community with the minimal use of force, the police come in like an invading army. This only serves to heighten tensions, especially as Madhesis have learned the hard way how the police see them.

Patterns of hate

In each of these recent incidents between Hindus and Muslims, a pattern repeats. The trigger is often loud religious music that is played well into the night. DJs accompany religious processions, especially idol-immersion rituals involving the gods Durga, Ganesh, Saraswati, and Laxmi, and turn up the volume while passing mosques and Muslim-majority neighborhoods. Alternatively, Hindus also accuse Muslims of loudly playing the azaan, or call to prayer, over loudspeakers at early hours of the morning and night.

Every incident has also taken place along the Terai border in districts with the highest concentration of Muslims — Kapilvastu, Rautahat, Sarlahi, Banke, Dhanusha, Parsa, Mahottari, Bara, and Sunsari. Residents of these districts have close cross-border ties to the Indian states of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, and there is ample evidence that radical elements have increased their presence in these border districts. In 2024, the Center for the Study of Organized Hate reported how militant Hindu groups like the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) and the Bajrang Dal have expanded across Nepal’s Terai districts. A 2023 US State Department report explicitly claimed that right-wing religious groups associated with the BJP had been funding politicians and political parties in Nepal to support a return to a Hindu kingdom.

The Hindu Swayamsevak Sangh, the Nepali offshoot of India’s Rastriya Swayamsevak Sangh, has been active in the country since the 90s, and a small political party affiliated to India’s Bharatiya Janata Party has received extensive coverage in complicit Indian media despite being a non-entity here in Nepal. The Nepal Janata Party (NJP) employs the color saffron and the lotus as its election symbol, both distinct markers of the BJP, and is active primarily in the Madhesh districts. Khem Nath Acharya, vice-president of the party, is a ‘Sanghi,’ a member of the ‘Sangh Parivar,’ the family of the Rastriya Swayamsevak Sangh, which includes the BJP, the VHP, and the Bajrang Dal. The NJP contested 20 seats, primarily in Madhesh Province, in the March election and won none. Its highest vote count was 240 in Saptari-2.

[Sidenote: Hindus in the Madhesh and online often make tall claims about extremist funding for Muslims in Nepal. However, there is no credible report from Nepal or elsewhere of any such funding. That does not necessarily mean that such support does not exist. If the claims are credible, then it is incumbent on the Nepal government to take them seriously and investigate them. So far, I have seen nothing that corroborates any claims about extremist Muslim funding.]

Political Hindutva might not have succeeded yet in Nepal, but other tactics are being employed. There are reports of how right-wing groups are operating deliberate misinformation campaigns modeled after Hindutva tactics in India. Social media is being used as a force multiplier whenever there is a local dispute. Instead of appealing for the calming of tensions, instigators on social media amplify hate and misinformation, prompting communities to react emotionally in anger. This allows radical elements on both sides to portray the disputes as a civilizational clash that requires an active and often violent response. Even after tensions cool, resentment remains, fueling recruitment into extremist ideologies and organizations.

Then, there is also the incipient pattern of state response. Every large-scale communal clash results in the same cycle of a heavy-handed police response, a curfew being imposed, an appeal for reconciliation, and the formation of an investigative committee whose report is rarely published publicly. Local administrators appeal to community leaders from both sides, which often works in the short term, but does little to alleviate deep-seated anger and resentment, which only feeds the next cycle of violence.

The Balendra Shah response

The government has also indulged in the same pattern, deploying security forces, instituting a curfew, and constituting an investigative committee. In doing so, it has repeated the same mistakes of the past. The committee is led by Bhupendra Thapa, Joint Secretary at the Home Ministry, and includes Nepal Police Superintendent Bipin Regmi, APF Superintendent Bikram Humagain, Energy Ministry Undersecretary Shaligram Bhandari, and Sunsari Assistant Chief District Officer Poshan Lamichhane. The committee includes no Madhesi representation and no Muslim representation, limiting its ability to understand and adequately analyze the sentiments that lead to such recurring instances of communal violence. Such committees do little to prevent the next cycle of violence.

The response of the current administration has also been largely motivated by security. The deaths of Om Prakash Mehta, Jay Prakash Mehta, and Ganesh Yadav have already raised concerns about the security forces’ use of force. It is unclear why the Nepal Police and APF resorted to live ammunition without exhausting all other non-lethal means of crowd control, but if we go by past reports, Nepal’s security forces have displayed a tendency to use excessive or lethal means when facing protests in the Madhes-Terai. In 2015, over 40 Madhesis were killed by security forces in protests over the constitution. Impunity has only contributed to this propensity. Even after the much-publicized shootings last year in Kathmandu that killed 19 unarmed protesters in a single day, not a single member of the Nepal Police or the Armed Police Force has been prosecuted or even disciplined.

The government has acted too little, too late. Prime Minister Balen Shah and Home Minister Sudan Gurung spent the first crucial days ducking the public. Shah issued a public statement on Facebook on Tuesday, and even then, many demanded that he release a video message rather than a Facebook status that no one would read. Belatedly, on Friday, Shah finally held a meeting with influential politicians from the Madhesh. Gurung, despite being the man in charge of internal security, did not visit Sunsari until Thursday evening. When he finally got there, he was hounded by irate locals.

Instead of the executive government, it is the ruling party that has taken a political approach to resolving tensions. Rastriya Swatantra Party chair Rabi Lamichhane called an all-party meeting on Wednesday, July 29, though neither Shah nor Gurung attended. Unlike Shah, Lamichhane seems to have seen the problem for what it is — a political issue that cannot be handled through brute force. The parties, which included Madhesh-based parties not represented in Parliament, pledged to mobilise local units and representatives to conduct dialogue to prevent any further escalation.

What is to be done?

The larger question, ultimately, regards how to prevent such instances from recurring in the future. Nepal has been largely spared the kinds of communal violence that have engulfed the rest of South Asia, but the spectre of religious hate is now materialising. If the state doesn’t mount a pervasive, long-term response to nip this in the bud, incidents like that in Sunsari will only recur.

The first element is intelligence. Nepal’s security forces – the Nepal Police, Armed Police Force, Nepal Army and National Investigation Department – all need real-time intelligence around potential flashpoints, especially in the Madhesh. It was a broad intelligence failure that led to the killings, arson, and violence during the Gen Z protests, and not much seems to have changed since then. But even where there is intelligence available, governments have failed to act. The Kathmandu Post reports that the APF had flagged the potential for organised communal violence in Sunsari in a report three years ago, but nothing came of it. The Shah government must work closely with the security agencies to identify where extremist rhetoric is coming from and block it at its source, whether it is Muslim or Hindu.

The security forces themselves need a major overhaul, too. The Nepal Police, the most public-facing security organization, must be able to work with communities, building relationships and acquiring sources instead of coming in at the last moment armed with batons, tear gas, and bullets. Policing needs to be preventive and community-based, not punitive and reactionary. Perhaps this means deputing Madhesi officers to Madhesh districts, as they are able to speak the language and understand local dynamics. Use of force should also be carefully regulated, especially in communal cases. The cops are all too trigger-happy in the Madhesh. Already, there are accusations that the security forces sided with one community over another.

The state must also understand that this is not just a law-and-order problem; it is a socio-political one that needs prevention, not punishment. An attempt at prevention was made by the interim government of Sushila Karki. In January 2026, then Home Minister Om Prakash Aryal mandated the creation of a District Peace and Social Harmony Committee that would include members of all religious communities. So far, it appears only a handful of districts, like Rupandehi, Dang, Sarlahi, and Parbat, have created these committees. Such committees, not just at the district level but also at the local level, would help ensure that there is dialogue before incidents spiral into violence. The Shah government should reinforce these committees and empower them further.

Ultimately, it is up to Nepalis themselves. There is no question about whether Hindus and Muslims can live alongside each other in Nepal; they have done so for centuries. Disputes are natural; they are the price of living in a diverse community. But local disagreements cannot be allowed to turn into civilizational clashes fanned by bad actors here and across the border. Nepalis are tolerant; we value diversity, and we love to take part in each other’s traditions. Hindus invite Muslims over for Dashain feasts and Muslims invite Hindus over for Eid. It is the way we have always lived. What is being tested now is whether the camaraderie of the everyday can outlast the virulent hatred of social media.

This essay has been republished from Kalam Weekly, a current affairs newsletter about Nepal. You can subscribe to the newsletter following the link here.

articles.title: Dissident Congress faction forms organising committee for national gathering
articles.summary:
The dissident faction of the Nepali Congress (NC) has appointed former general secretary Shashank Koirala as the coordinator of the main organising committee for its national gathering scheduled for August 14.

Sources close to the faction said that if efforts to restore party unity fail before the gathering, preparations are in place to register a new political party under the leadership of Koirala, the son of the late NC founder BP Koirala.

At a press conference held at the faction’s contact office in Chundevi on Saturday, the dissident group announced the formation of a 521-member main organising committee headed by Koirala.

The faction has also formed 16 sub-committees, including those responsible for political documents, contemporary political issues, organisational preparations, statute amendment drafting, economic policy and publicity.

“We have announced this national gathering to give the party a new direction. If there is no positive change or agreement by then, we will move forward in a new form,” leader Min Bishwakarma told Kantipur. “If the gathering rejects the proposal for unity, we will take an alternative path. Otherwise, Shashank Koirala will remain our leader.”

Former senior NC office-bearers and leaders, including former general secretaries Shashank Koirala, Bimalendra Nidhi, Prakash Man Singh and Krishna Prasad Sitaula, attended the press conference.

Koirala said leader Shekhar Koirala also supports the initiative.

“I have been in continuous discussions with Shekhar Dai. He was supposed to attend today’s press conference, but could not because he is in Biratnagar. He asked me to convey to the media that he extends his full support,” Shashank said.

According to a leader from the non-establishment faction, preparations for launching a new political party have accelerated as efforts to reach an agreement with the party leadership have failed to produce results.

The leader said that unless the establishment faction, led by NC president Gagan Thapa, shows sufficient flexibility on unification, the formation of a new party is increasingly likely.

“Representatives and cadres from across the country will attend the national gathering. If we fail to reach a consensus, a new party will be announced there,” the leader said. “Work on the party’s ideology, vision, organisational structure and draft statute is in its final stage.”

articles.title: Broad Peak Avalanche: What we know so far about Nirmal “Nimsdai” Purja and the missing climbers in Pakistan
articles.summary:
A rescue operation is under way on Pakistan’s 8,047-metre Broad Peak after an avalanche struck an international climbing team on Thursday, leaving several climbers, including Nepal-born mountaineer Nirmal Purja, widely known as “Nims Dai”, missing. Four bodies have been recovered so far, according to Irfan Arshad Khan, president of the Alpine Club of Pakistan.

The missing climbers include Purja, Kili Pemba Sherpa, Nima Sherpa, Gyalu Sherpa and Nawang Thindu Sherpa. The group also includes Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, Chinese climber Wang Zhong and American climber Mallory Geis.

What is the latest update on search and rescue efforts?

Search and rescue operations for climbers missing after Thursday’s avalanche on Pakistan’s 8,051-metre Broad Peak resumed on Saturday after poor weather conditions forced rescuers to suspend the mission on Friday, authorities said.

According to the Alpine Club of Pakistan, the search operation resumed, with additional Sherpas from other expeditions joining the rescue effort.

The Commissioner of Baltistan said rescue teams recovered three bodies during Friday’s operation before worsening weather conditions forced them to halt the search.

The authorities identified those recovered as Pur Bahadur Gurung of Nepal, Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy of Oman, and the remains of Sarah Mallory of the United States.

The bodies were airlifted by Pakistan Army Aviation helicopters to the Combined Military Hospital (CMH), where legal procedures and identification formalities are currently underway.

The rescue team said drone footage had identified several more bodies on the mountain, although recovery has not yet been possible due to the difficult conditions.

The rescue mission began on Friday after tour operators formally requested assistance. Pakistan Army Aviation helicopters transported a three-member civilian rescue team, led by veteran mountaineer Sirbaz Khan, to the Broad Peak base camp. The team then proceeded on foot towards Camp II, where the recovered bodies were found.

The avalanche struck at around 8 pm local time on Thursday as the 10-member international expedition was climbing between Camp II and Camp III at an altitude of about 6,600 metres. The team had last been in contact with its tour operator at 9 am that day.

The expedition comprised climbers from Nepal, Pakistan, the United Kingdom, the United States, China and Oman.

The Commissioner of Baltistan said the operation was being conducted in extremely challenging terrain and severe high-altitude conditions by the Pakistan Army in coordination with local climbers and rescue teams.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs said it is closely monitoring the situation following the avalanche.

In a statement issued on Friday afternoon, the ministry said the Nepali Embassy in Islamabad is coordinating with the Pakistani authorities, including the Alpine Club of Pakistan, to support the swift and safe search and rescue of all climbers affected by the avalanche.

The ministry added that the Pakistani authorities have assured Nepal they will mobilise all available resources to carry out the search and rescue operation as quickly as possible.

Pakistan mobilised helicopters, drones and ground teams to search for the missing climbers, Nepal’s ambassador to Pakistan Rita Dhital said.

Speaking to Kantipur from Pakistan, Dhital said rescue teams, equipment and helicopters had been deployed from Skardu.

The Alpine Club of Pakistan said it was coordinating with government authorities and other agencies to ensure all available resources were deployed.

“Every possible effort is being made to ensure that helicopter support and all available rescue resources are mobilised at the earliest opportunity, subject to weather and operational conditions,” the club said.

How did the avalanche unfold?

The avalanche struck the climbing team on Broad Peak in the Karakoram mountain range around midday on Thursday, according to the Alpine Club of Pakistan.

At 8,047 metres, Broad Peak is the world’s 12th-highest mountain and is considered one of the most challenging peaks for high-altitude expeditions. The mountain lies in Pakistan’s Karakoram range, near K2, the world’s second-highest mountain.

Thaneshwar Guragain, general manager of Seven Summit Treks, said some climbers swept away by the avalanche were brought back to base camp through an overland rescue effort. The bodies were found during that operation.

Poor weather conditions initially prevented helicopter flights, slowing rescue efforts.

What is the status of the climbers?

Two of the dead have so far been identified. The Alpine Club of Pakistan said the bodies of Nepal’s Pur Bahadur Gurung, known as “Yukta”, and Oman’s Nadhira Al Harthy have been recovered.

Al Harthy’s body is being airlifted by helicopter to Skardu, while arrangements are underway to transport Gurung’s remains.

Al Harthy was the first Omani woman to summit Mount Everest.

Who is Nirmal Purja?

Purja, widely known as Nimsdai, became internationally known in 2019 after climbing all 14 peaks above 8,000 metres in just over six months, setting a world record.

Before becoming a professional mountaineer, he served in the British Army and later joined the Royal Marines.

His mountaineering career began after a 2012 trek to Everest Base Camp, when he decided to continue towards the summit of Everest instead of returning as originally planned. He holds multiple world records on high-altitude mountaineering.

This is a developing story and the story will be updated throughout the day.

articles.title: सहकारी ठगीका मुद्दा हेर्न समर्पित इजलास गठन गर्न अनुरोध
articles.summary:
भूमि व्यवस्था, सहकारी, संघीय मामिला तथा सामान्य प्रशासन मन्त्रालयले सहकारी ठगीसम्बन्धी मुद्दाको छिटो र छरितो ढंगले न्याय निरूपण गर्नका लागि सहकारी कसुर हेर्ने ‘समर्पित इजलास’ गठन गर्न भन्दै सर्वोच्च अदालतका प्रधानन्यायाधीशलाई प्रतिवेदन पेस गरेको छ।

सहकारी ठगीसम्बन्धी मुद्दाको चाप बढिरहेकाले सो मुद्दा फर्छ्यौटका लागि समर्पित इजलास गठन गर्न अनुरोध गरिएको हो। मन्त्रालयले समर्पित इजलास गठन गर्नुको आवश्यकता र औचित्यको विषयमा कार्यदल गठन गरेर तयार पारेको प्रतिवेदन प्रधानन्यायाधीशलाई बुझाइएको मन्त्रीको निजी सचिवालयले जनाएको छ।

सर्वोच्च अदालतले २०८२ माघ ११ गते जारी गरेको निर्देशनात्मक आदेशमा सहकारी कसुरसम्बन्धी मुद्दाको चाप बढी भएका जिल्ला अदालतमा आवश्यकताअनुसार समर्पित इजलास स्थापना गर्न अध्ययन गरी निष्कर्षका आधारमा कार्यान्वयन गर्ने आदेश दिएपछि मन्त्रालयले अध्ययन कार्यदल गठन गरेको थियो।

भूमि व्यवस्था, सहकारी, संघीय मामिला तथा सामान्य प्रशासनमन्त्री प्रतिभा रावलले कार्यदलका सदस्यसहित उक्त प्रतिवेदन सर्वोच्च अदालतका प्रधानन्यायाधीश डा मनोज शर्मालाई बुझाएकी हुन्।

कार्यदलको प्रतिवेदनमा सहकारी कसुरलाई सामान्य ठगीको घटनाभन्दा फरक, ठूलो सङ्ख्यामा नागरिकको जीवन, सम्पत्ति र मुलुकको वित्तीय प्रणालीसँग प्रत्यक्ष सम्बन्धित सामाजिक-आर्थिक अपराधका रूपमा व्याख्या गरिएको छ।

यस्ता मुद्दाको प्रभावकारी र छिटो सुनुवाइका लागि विशेष प्राथमिकतासहित समर्पित इजलास आवश्यक रहेको निष्कर्ष प्रतिवेदनले निकालेको छ। प्रतिवेदनमा सहकारी ठगीका मुद्दा लामो समयसम्म विचाराधीन रहँदा पीडित बचतकर्ताले आफ्नो बचत फिर्ता पाउन नसक्ने, न्यायमा ढिलाइ हुने तथा दोषीलाई विभिन्न प्रकारका संरक्षण हुने जोखिम बढ्ने उल्लेख गरिएको छ।

सो प्रतिवेदनमा पीडितलाई समयमै न्याय दिलाउन, सहकारी क्षेत्रप्रतिको जनविश्वास पुनःस्थापित गर्न तथा वित्तीय सुशासन कायम गर्न समर्पित इजलास गठन अपरिहार्य रहेको कार्यदलको निष्कर्ष छ।

articles.title: मानव–वन्यजन्तु द्वन्द्व : पीडा धेरै, प्रमाण कम
articles.summary:
नेपालले बाघ संरक्षणमा विश्वमै उदाहरणीय सफलता हासिल गरेको छ। पछिल्लो राष्ट्रिय बाघ गणना २०८२ अनुसार देशभर ४२९ वटा वयस्क बाघ पुगेका छन्। संरक्षणको यो उपलब्धिसँगै निकुञ्ज र संरक्षण क्षेत्र आसपास बस्ने समुदाय भने बढ्दो मानव–वन्यजन्तु द्वन्द्वको मारमा परिरहेका छन्।

वन्यजन्तुको आक्रमणबाट हुने क्षतिभन्दा पनि त्यसपछि राहत पाउनुपर्ने जटिल प्रक्रिया, प्रमाण जुटाउने झन्झट र प्रशासनिक सास्ती उनीहरूका लागि अझ ठूलो समस्या बनेको छ।

मकवानपुर, बाँके, बर्दिया, कञ्चनपुर, बागलुङ, रुकुम (पूर्व) र काठमाडौंका निकुञ्ज तथा आरक्ष प्रभावित क्षेत्रका महिलाहरूको अनुभव लगभग एकै छ। वन्यजन्तुको आक्रमणबाट हुने क्षति एउटा पीडा हो भने त्यसको राहत पाउन सरकारी कार्यालय धाउनु अर्को ठूलो सास्ती बनेको उनीहरूको साझा भनाइ छ।

पर्सा राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जको मध्यवर्ती क्षेत्रमा पर्ने मकवानपुरको मनहरी गाउँपालिका वडा नं. ४ का बासिन्दा दिनहुँ वन्यजन्तुको त्रास र सरकारी उपेक्षा खेप्न बाध्य छन्। राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जबाट आउने वन्यजन्तुले बालीनाली र चौपाया नष्ट गर्दा पनि उचित क्षतिपूर्ति नपाएको र प्रक्रियागत सास्ती खेप्नुपरेको गुनासो छ।

स्थानीय लक्ष्मी प्रजाका अनुसार निकुञ्जबाट आउने बँदेल, हात्ती, गैँडा र बाघले गाउँमा निरन्तर क्षति पुर्‍याउँदै आएका छन्। हालै मात्र सोही वडाका कुमार चेपाङका चार वटा बाख्रा बाघले मारेको तर त्यसको कुनै क्षतिपूर्ति नपाएको उनले बताइन्।

'निवेदन दिन जाँदा आउने क्षतिपूर्तिभन्दा तेब्बर खर्च भइसक्छ,' उनले भनिन्, 'सरकारले तोकेबमोजिमको राहत र क्षतिपूर्ति हामीले सहजै पाउन सकेका छैनौँ।'

करिब ६-७ वर्ष अगाडि घाँस काट्न गएकी ५८ वर्षीया स्थानीय महिलाको हात्तीको आक्रमणबाट ज्यान गएको घटना सम्झँदै उनले पहुँच र प्रभावका आधारमा मात्र क्षतिपूर्ति पाइने गरेको आरोप लगाइन्। पहुँचवालाहरूले दबाब दिएर क्षतिपूर्ति पाउने गरे पनि आदिवासी, चेपाङ तथा सीमान्तकृत समुदायले भने वर्षौँ धाउँदा पनि राहत पाउन नसकेको उनको भनाइ छ।

स्थानीय सरकार र निकुञ्ज प्रशासनले आफूहरूको समस्या नसुनेको आरोप लगाउँदै लक्ष्मीले थपिन्, 'हाम्रो समस्या स्थानीय सरकारले एउटा कानले सुन्छ, अर्को कानले उडाइदिन्छ। निकुञ्जबाट पनि हामीलाई सधैँ हस्तक्षेप र सास्ती मात्र छ।'

गाउँमा बाटोघाटो बने पनि वास्तविक चेपाङ समुदायले पाउनुपर्ने हक र अधिकारका कुराहरू अझै ओझेलमा परेको उनको गुनासो छ। २०७२ सालको भूकम्पले चिरा परेका काठ र माटोका कच्ची घरहरूमा अझै जोखिम मोलेर बस्न बाध्य भएको उनी बताउँछिन्। हरेक वर्ष निवेदन दिँदा पनि सुरक्षित आवासका लागि सरकारले कुनै सुनुवाइ नगरेको उनले गुनासो गरिन्।

यस्तै, बाँके राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज आसपासका बासिन्दा दिनहुँ जङ्गली जनावरको उच्च जोखिम र त्रासका बिच जीवनयापन गर्न बाध्य छन्। घाँस-दाउरा, पशुपालन र गिट्टी-बालुवा सङ्कलनका लागि जङ्गल तथा खोला-नालामा जानुपर्ने बाध्यता रहेका स्थानीयवासी बाघ, चितुवा, हात्ती र भालुलगायतका वन्यजन्तुको निरन्तर आक्रमणको त्रासमा परेका छन्।

निकुञ्ज क्षेत्रकी स्थानीय भूमिका पुनका अनुसार गाउँमा बाघ, चितुवा र बाँदरको आतङ्क अत्यधिक छ। जङ्गलमा घाँस-दाउरा गर्न जाँदा बेला-बेलामा बाघले आक्रमण गर्न खोज्ने र भाग्ने क्रममा धेरै मानिस घाइते हुने गरेका छन्। केही स्थानीयले वन्यजन्तुको आक्रमणबाट ज्यानसमेत गुमाउनुपरेको उनले बताइन्।

वन्यजन्तुको डरकै कारण एक्लै जङ्गल जान असम्भव जस्तै बनेपछि स्थानीय महिलाहरू समूह बनाएर मात्र घाँस-दाउरा गर्न जाने गरेको उनले सुनाइन्। जङ्गल जाँदा अपनाइने सतर्कताबारे पुनले भनिन्, 'रातो वा हरियो जस्ता गाढा रङका कपडा जनावरले टाढैबाट देख्ने भएकाले त्यस्ता कपडा लगाउँदैनौँ। जङ्गलमा जाँदा हरक्षण अगाडि-पछाडि हेर्दै र सानो खसुर-खसुर आवाजमा पनि सतर्क भएर हिँड्नुपर्छ।'

वन्यजन्तुको त्रासले स्थानीयको दैनिक जीवन र मानसिक स्वास्थ्यमा गम्भीर असर पारेको छ। भोलिपल्ट घाँस काट्न जानुपर्ने भए अघिल्लो दिनदेखि नै वन्यजन्तुसँग भेट हुने वा आक्रमणमा परिने हो कि भन्ने चिन्ताले सताउने गरेको उनी बताउँछिन्।

मानवीय क्षति भएमा सरकारले दिने क्षतिपूर्ति तथा राहत रकम पाउन निकै कठिन र झन्झटिलो रहेको उनको गुनासो छ। कानुनी र प्रशासनिक प्रक्रिया पूरा गर्नका लागि धेरै धाउनुपर्ने र सो क्रममा राहतको आधा रकम कागजी प्रक्रियामै खर्च हुने गरेको पुनले बताइन्।

विशेष गरी जनजाति र सीमान्तकृत समुदायका मानिसहरूले आफ्ना अधिकारका कुरा स्पष्टसँग राख्न नसक्दा र प्रशासनिक भाषाको समस्याका कारण पाएको राहत पनि हात पार्न नसकेको उनको आरोप छ। 'बोल्न सक्नेले मात्रै राहत पाउँछन्, जनजाति महिलाहरू स्पष्टसँग बोल्न अप्ठ्यारो मान्ने हुनाले उनीहरूले समयमा र पूरा राहत रकम पाउँदैनन्,' उनले भनिन्।

यसबाहेक, खोला-नालाबाट जीविकोपार्जनका लागि गिट्टी-बालुवा उठाउनसमेत निकुञ्ज प्रशासनले कडाइ गर्ने गरेको र एक ट्रलीको १२ देखि १५ सय रुपैयाँसम्म तिर्न बाध्य पारिएको भन्दै उनले जीविकोपार्जनका लागि थप सकस भइरहेको गुनासो गरेकी छन्।

ढोरपाटन शिकार आरक्षको कोर तथा मध्यवर्ती क्षेत्रमा पर्ने बागलुङको निसीखोला गाउँपालिका वडा नं. ५ का स्थानीयवासी वन्यजन्तुको निरन्तर आतङ्क र कडा कानुनी प्रावधानका बिच सास्ती खेप्न बाध्य छन्। आरक्षबाट आउने वन्यजन्तुले बालीनाली र घरपालुवा चौपाया नष्ट गर्दा पनि झन्झटिलो कागजी प्रक्रियाका कारण पीडितहरूले क्षतिपूर्ति पाउन नसकेको गुनासो गरेका छन्।

स्थानीय कमला पुन मगरका अनुसार गाउँमा बाघ, भालु, बँदेल, दुम्सी र बोसो जस्ता वन्यजन्तुले ठुलो सास्ती दिने गरेका छन्। बँदेल र दुम्सीले बालीनाली नष्ट गर्ने तथा बाघ, भालु र बोसोले गाउँका गाई-भैँसी र बाख्रामाथि आक्रमण गरी क्षति पुर्‍याउने गरेको उनले बताइन्। वन्यजन्तुको आक्रमणबाट विशेष गरी सीमान्तकृत आदिवासी जनजाति र दलित समुदायका मानिसहरू बढी प्रभावित भएका छन्।

पहिले-पहिले स्थानीय बासिन्दाले आवाज निकालेर वा भरुवा बन्दुक पड्काएर वन्यजन्तुलाई तर्साउने र बस्तीबाट टाढा भगाउने गर्थे। तर, अहिले आरक्षको कडा नियम र प्रतिबन्धका कारण वन्यजन्तु धपाउन वा नियन्त्रण गर्न नसकिएको उनको भनाइ छ। 'अहिले नियम-कानुनका कारण वन्यजन्तुलाई तर्साउन पनि पाइँदैन,' मगरले भनिन्, 'खुकुरी वा भालाले वन्यजन्तु भागैनन्, जसले गर्दा हाम्रो जीविकोपार्जन झन्-झन् गाह्रो बन्दै गएको छ।'

यस्तै, शिवपुरी नागार्जुन राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज आसपासका बस्तीहरूमा पनि वन्यजन्तुको जोखिम र त्रास पछिल्लो समय तीव्र रूपमा बढेको छ। निकुञ्जबाट आउने बँदेल, बाँदर, बाघ र भालुका कारण स्थानीय बासिन्दाको धनजन र बालीनालीमा निरन्तर क्षति पुगिरहेको छ।

स्थानीय विष्णुमाया तामाङका अनुसार पछिल्लो समय गाउँमा बाघको त्रास अत्यधिक बढेको छ। रातिको समयमा बाघ बस्तीमा छिरेर गोठबाटै बाख्रा तानेर लैजाने क्रम बढेको उनले बताइन्। 'यसपालि मात्रै गाउँका चार-पाँच जनाको गोठबाट बाघले बाख्रा तानेर लगिसक्यो,' तामाङले भनिन्, 'पहिले-पहिले यति विधि डर थिएन, तर अहिले जुनसुकै बेला मानिसमाथि नै आक्रमण गर्छ कि भन्ने ठुलो डर र चिन्ता छ।'

बाघको त्राससँगै बँदेल र बाँदरले बालीनाली नष्ट गर्दा किसानहरू ठुलो मारमा परेका छन्। खेतबारीमा लगाएको मकै तथा अन्य बालीनाली बाँदर र बँदेलले व्यापक रूपमा नष्ट गर्ने गरे पनि निकुञ्ज वा स्थानीय सरकारबाट पाइने रकम अत्यन्तै न्यून रहेको उनको भनाइ छ।

स्थानीय सरकार र निकुञ्जले दिने रकमबारे असन्तुष्टि जनाउँदै विष्णुमायाले भनिन्, 'बँदेल र बाँदरले धेरै ठुलो परिमाणमा मकै र बालीनाली खाएर नष्ट गर्छन्। निकुञ्ज तथा सरकारले त क्षतिपूर्ति नै दिएकै भन्छन्, तर क्षति धेरै भए पनि दुई-तीन हजार रुपैयाँ मात्र दिइन्छ। त्यो क्षतिपूर्तिभन्दा पनि नाम मात्रको राहत जस्तै छ।'

त्यसैगरी, रुकुम पूर्वको पुथा उत्तरगंगा गाउँपालिकाका १४ मध्ये ५ वटा वडाहरू ढोरपाटन शिकार आरक्ष क्षेत्रभित्र पर्दछन्। आरक्षको कडा नियम र सुरक्षाकर्मीको व्यवहारका कारण स्थानीय बासिन्दाले दैनिक जीविकोपार्जनका साथै आफ्नो पुर्ख्यौली संस्कृति नै गुमाउनुपर्ने अवस्था आएको गुनासो गरेका छन्।

पुथा उत्तरगंगा वडा नं. १ मैकोतीकी स्थानीय मलति पुनका अनुसार पहाडी भेगका सर्वसाधारण बिहान-बेलुकाको छाक टार्न कृषि, वन-जङ्गल, पशुपालन र जडीबुटीमा निर्भर छन्। तर आरक्षको स्थापनापछि बाबु-बाजेको पालादेखि चल्दै आएको गाईगोठ (थोलो) कब्जा गरिएको, भेडा-बाख्रा र गाईबस्तु चराउन रोक लगाइएको र कर तिर्न दबाब दिने गरिएको छ। यसले गर्दा पुर्ख्यौली 'माछा चरण' (तल्लो भेगको खेतीकिसानी) र 'डाँफे चरण' (बुकीमा भेडा-बाख्रा चराउने) जस्ता मगर समुदायका परम्परा तथा संस्कृति लोप हुने अवस्थामा पुगेको उनी बताउँछिन्।

स्थानीयको मुख्य आर्थिक स्रोत मानिने यार्चागुम्बा सङ्कलनका लागि जाँदा प्रतिव्यक्ति दुईदेखि तीन हजार रुपैयाँसम्म सिफारिस शुल्क लिने गरिएको छ। आरक्षको पोष्टमा जाँचका नाममा सर्वसाधारणको भारी खोतल्ने र सास्ती दिने काम भइरहेको उनको भनाइ छ।

'हामी मगर समाजमा सुकुटी खाने चलन छ। तर बाटोमा जाँच गर्दा सुकुटीसमेत थुतेर फालिदिने र मानसिक तर्साउने गरिन्छ,' पुनले भनिन्, 'सामान्य जडीबुटी निकाल्दा वा आरक्ष बाहिरकै रुख ढाल्दासमेत ५० हजारदेखि ६० हजार रुपैयाँसम्म चर्को जरिवाना माग्ने गरिन्छ। यसले गरिब जनता अझ गरिब बन्दै गएका छन्।'

उक्त क्षेत्रमा नाउर, झारल, कस्तुरी, डाँफे र हिउँ चितुवा जस्ता वन्यजन्तु पाइन्छन्। तर आरक्ष र मध्यवर्ती क्षेत्र (बफर जोन) को नीति पहाडी जीवनशैली अनुकूल नभएकाले तराई र पहाडका लागि फरक-फरक नियम बनाउनुपर्ने उनको माग छ।

कञ्चनपुरको बेलडाँडी गाउँपालिकाका बासिन्दा वन्यजन्तुको निरन्तर आक्रमण र क्षतिबाट सास्ती खेप्न बाध्य छन्। जङ्गलको किनारमै रहेको यस बस्तीमा दिनहुँ जसो हात्ती र बाघ पसेर घरपालुवा चौपाया र बालीनाली नष्ट गर्ने गरेको छ।

स्थानीय इश्वरी रानाका अनुसार जङ्गल नजिकै बस्ती भएकाले वन्यजन्तुले ठुलो क्षति पुर्‍याउँदै आएका छन्। 'बाघ बस्तीमा छिरेर बाख्रा र गाईका बाछोलाई लखेटेर जङ्गलतिर लग्छ,' उनले भनिन्, 'हात्ती त दिउँसै ३–४ बजेतिरै जङ्गलबाट निस्किएर बालीनाली नष्ट गर्छ र घरहरूसमेत भत्काइदिन्छ।'

गाउँमा वन्यजन्तुको आक्रमणबाट सर्वसाधारण घाइते हुने क्रम बढ्दै गएको छ। गत असार २५ गते जङ्गलमा च्याउ टिप्न गएका स्थानीय बासिन्दामाथि बाघले आक्रमण गरेको घटना सुनाउँदै रानाले भनिन्, 'फर्किने क्रममा पछाडि रहेका दुई जनामाथि बाघले पञ्जा हानेर गम्भीर घाइते बनायो। उनीहरूलाई पुरै टाँका लगाउनुपर्ने घाउ भयो र बेहोस नै भए।'

यसरी आक्रमणमा परेर गम्भीर घाइते हुँदा पनि पीडितहरूले कुनै क्षतिपूर्ति पाउन सकेका छैनन्। जङ्गल प्रवेश गरेको भन्दै निकुञ्ज वा वन कार्यालयबाट उल्टै कारबाही हुने वा पैसा तिराउने डर देखाइएकाले पीडित पक्षले क्षतिपूर्तिको लागि आवाजसम्म उठाउन नसकेको उनको भनाइ छ।

बर्दिया राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज आसपासका बासिन्दा पनि एकातिर दिनहुँ बाघ र हात्तीको त्रासका बिच बस्न बाध्य छन् भने अर्कातिर निकुञ्ज प्रशासनको सीमा अतिक्रमण र अव्यवहारिक कानुनी प्रक्रियाका कारण दोहोरो मारमा परेका छन्। निकुञ्ज आसपासका नम्बरी जग्गा कटान हुँदा निकुञ्जले कब्जा गर्ने तर सोही क्षेत्रमा मानिस र पशुचौपायामाथि वन्यजन्तुले क्षति पुर्‍याउँदा कुनै जिम्मेवारी नलिने गरेको गेरुवा गाउँपालिकाकी श्यामकुमारी चौधरीको आरोप छ।

चौधरीका अनुसार सो क्षेत्रमा बाघ र हात्तीको जोखिम अत्यधिक छ। वि.सं. २०७७/७८ सालतिर गेरुवा गाउँपालिका–४ राजीपुरका धनबहादुर सिंहलाई बाघले घर नजिकैबाट घिसारेर निकुञ्जको मुख्य (कोर) एरियामा लगेर मारेको थियो। पछि डिएनए परीक्षण गर्दा समेत शव उनकै भएको पुष्टि भयो। तर, पीडित परिवारलाई प्रहरीको मुचुल्का बनाउने क्रममा प्रक्रियागत ज्ञान नहुँदा र प्रहरीले वास्तविक अवस्था नबुझाइदिँदा राहत पाउनबाट वञ्चित हुनु परेको घटना उनले सुनाइन्।

बाघको आक्रमणबाट ज्यान गुमाएका सिंहको परिवार भूमिहीन छ। मृतकका बालबच्चा साना भएकाले अहिले उनीहरू भारतमा गएर मजदुरी गरी जीविकोपार्जन गर्न बाध्य छन्। 'मुचुल्का उठाउने क्रममा सोझा मान्छेलाई राहत प्रक्रियाबारे कसैले सम्झाएनन्, पछि राहत माग्न जाँदा मुचुल्काको प्राविधिक कारण देखाएर अस्वीकार गरियो,' चौधरीले भनिन्, 'दौडधुप गर्दागर्दै पीडित परिवारको ३०–४० हजार रुपैयाँ खर्च भयो, तर सरकारबाट हजार रुपैयाँ पनि पाइएन।'

यस विषयमा स्थानीय सरकारले पनि प्रभावकारी भूमिका नखेलेको र पीडितको हकका लागि कडा रूपमा प्रस्तुत नभएको उनको भनाइ छ।

उनका अनुसार गाउँ र निकुञ्जको सीमा जोडिएकाले स्थानीयहरू राति आफ्नै घरमा सुतिरहेका बेलासमेत सुरक्षित छैनन्। हात्तीले घर भत्काइदिने र बाघले गोठबाटै बाख्रा तथा भैँसी तानेर लैजाने गरेकाले दैनिक जीवन अत्यन्तै कष्टकर बनेको छ।

स्थानीयवासीले जटिल प्रशासनिक प्रक्रिया, प्रहरी मुचुल्का वा कागजी प्रमाण मात्र खोज्नुभन्दा गाउँ-समाज, छरछिमेकी, बुद्धिजीवी, र थारू समुदायका 'बडघर' तथा चौकिदारको साक्षी एवं सिफारिसलाई आधार मानेर राहत र क्षतिपूर्ति दिने गरी ऐन तथा नियम संशोधन गर्न सरकारसँग उनले माग गरेकी छन्।

बाघ बढ्दै, द्वन्द्व पनि बढ्ने चिन्ता

नेपालमा पछिल्लो राष्ट्रिय बाघ गणना २०८२ अनुसार देशभरका संरक्षित क्षेत्र तथा तिनसँग जोडिएका वन क्षेत्रमा ४२९ वटा वयस्क बाघ भेटिएका छन्। सबैभन्दा बढी चितवन राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जमा १४५, बर्दियामा ११२, पर्सामा ७१, बाँकेमा ५१ र शुक्लाफाँटामा ५० वटा बाघ छन्।

अघिल्लो गणनामा चितवनमा १२८, बर्दियामा १२५, पर्सामा ४१, शुक्लाफाँटामा ३६ र बाँकेमा २५ वटा बाघ थिए। यस आधारमा चितवनमा १७, पर्सामा ३०, शुक्लाफाँटामा १४ र बाँकेमा २६ वटा बाघ थपिएका छन् भने बर्दियामा १३ वटा घटेका छन्।

पाँच वर्षमा १४६ जनाको मृत्यु

मानव–वन्यजन्तु द्वन्द्वका घटनाले पछिल्ला वर्षहरूमा गम्भीर रूप लिएका छन्। चितवनको भरतपुर महानगरपालिका–२३ बेलहठ्ठाकी २५ वर्षीया आशिका बोटे र उनका चार वर्षीय छोराको गत असार २० गते राति जंगली हात्ती 'ध्रुवे' को आक्रमणबाट ज्यान गयो। हात्ती धपाउन आगो बाल्ने क्रममा परिवारको कच्ची घरसमेत जलेको थियो।

त्यस्तै, गत माघ १२ गते चितवनको माडी नगरपालिका–२३ का अशोक भट्टराई खेतमा हिँडिरहेका बेला गैंडाको आक्रमणबाट मारिए।

राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज विभागका अनुसार पछिल्लो पाँच वर्षमा हात्ती, बाघ, गैंडा, चितुवा, भालु, जंगली कुकुरलगायत वन्यजन्तुको आक्रमणबाट १४६ जनाको मृत्यु भएको छ। यस अवधिमा ३९९ जना सख्त घाइते र २५१ जना सामान्य घाइते भएका छन्।

वन्यजन्तुले मानिसको ज्यान मात्र होइन, बालीनाली, घर, गोठ र पशुधनमा समेत ठूलो क्षति पुर्‍याइरहेका छन्। हात्ती, बाघ, भालु, गैंडा, चितुवा, हिउँचितुवा, ब्वाँसो, जंगली बँदेल, अर्ना, मगर गोही र चौरीगाईसँगको द्वन्द्व देशका अधिकांश संरक्षित क्षेत्र आसपास जारी छ।

articles.title: कीर्तिमानी पर्वतारोही ‘निम्सदाई’ को निधनले शोकमग्न विश्व : बियर ग्रिल्स र रेनहोल्ड मेसनर स्तब्ध
articles.summary:
संसारभरका पर्वतारोहीहरू माझ अलग पहिचान बनाएका प्रख्यात नेपाली पर्वतारोही निर्मल ‘निम्सदाई’ पुर्जाको पाकिस्तानको ब्रोड पिक हिमालमा आएको विनाशकारी हिमपहिरोमा परी निधन भएको छ।

बिहीबार ८ हजार ४७ मिटर अग्लो ब्रोड पिकमा पुर्जाले १० जनाको अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय अभियान टोलीको नेतृत्व गरिरहेका बेला उक्त भीषण हिमपहिरो गएको थियो। शुक्रबार बिहानैदेखि पाकिस्तानी सेनाको हेलिकप्टर, ड्रोन र विशेष उद्धार टोली परिचालन गरिए पनि शनिबार उनको सह-स्वामित्व रहेको साहसिक कम्पनी ‘एलिट एक्स्पेड’ ले ४३ वर्षीय पुर्जासहित अभियानका अन्य सदस्यहरूको निधन भएको पुष्टि गरेको हो। उनको यो अप्रत्याशित निधनले नेपाली पर्वतारोहण क्षेत्र मात्र नभएर विश्वभरका साहसिक प्रेमीहरूलाई शोकमग्न बनाएको छ।

पुर्जाको निधनप्रति प्रसिद्ध साहसी तथा टेलिभिजन होस्ट एडवर्ड माइकल ‘बियर’ ग्रिल्स र इटालियन पर्वतारोही रेनहोल्ड मेसनरले गहिरो शोक व्यक्त गरेका छन्। ग्रिल्सले इन्स्टाग्राममार्फत श्रद्धाञ्जली दिँदै लेखेका छन्, ‘विश्वभरका धेरै पर्वतारोहीहरूका लागि यो हृदय विदारक समाचार हो। हामी तपाईंलाई र तपाईंको अटुट आत्मालाई कहिल्यै बिर्सने छैनौं।’

त्यस्तै, इतिहासकै महान् उच्च-उचाइ पर्वतारोही मेसनरले भनेका छन्, ‘निम्सले साहस र जोशका साथ आफ्नो बाटो रोजे। अब उनको निधनको शोक मात्र होइन, उनले बाँचेको वास्तविक जीवनको सम्झना बाँकी छ।’

भूतपूर्व ब्रिटिश एलीट स्पेशल फोर्सका सैनिक पुर्जाले सन् २०१९ मा संसारका सबै १४ वटा ८ हजार मिटरभन्दा अग्ला हिमालहरू मात्र ६ महिना ६ दिनमा सफलतापूर्वक चढेर विश्व रेकर्ड बनाएका थिए। उनको यो ऐतिहासिक सफलतालाई नेटफ्लिक्सको चर्चित वृत्तचित्र ‘१४ पिक्स: नथिङ इज इम्पसिबल’ मा देखाइएको छ। सन् २०२१ को जाडोयाममा इतिहासमै पहिलोपटक केटु हिमालको सफल आरोहण गरेर उनले पर्वतारोहणमा नयाँ इतिहास रचेका थिए।

निधन हुनुअघि उनी संसारका सबै १४ वटा ८ हजार मिटरभन्दा अग्ला हिमालहरू पूरै दुई पटक र त्यो पनि कृत्रिम अक्सिजनबिना सफलतापूर्वक चढ्ने इतिहासकै पहिलो व्यक्ति बन्ने यात्रामा थिए। उनले सन् २०२६ जुलाई २१ मा मात्र अक्सिजनबिना ग्यासरब्रुम-२ हिमाल आरोहण गरेका थिए र यो रेकर्ड पूरा गर्न ब्रोड पिक र चो ओयु हिमाल मात्र बाँकी थिए।

यो दुई पटकको आरोहण रेकर्डबाहेक उनको जीवनकै सबैभन्दा ठूलो, महत्वाकांक्षी र दीर्घकालीन मिसन ‘ह्याट-ट्रिक प्रोजेक्ट’ थियो। यस मिसनअन्तर्गत उनले संसारका सबै १४ वटा ८ हजार मिटरभन्दा अग्ला हिमालहरू र संसारका सातै महादेशका सर्वोच्च शिखरहरू तीन फरक-फरक पटक आरोहण गरेर अभूतपूर्व कीर्तिमान रच्ने योजना बनाएका थिए।

साहस र दृढ इच्छाशक्तिका प्रतिमूर्ति पुर्जाको यो महत्वाकांक्षी सपना उनीसँगै ब्रोड पिकको हिउँमा विलिन भएको छ, तर उनले विश्व पर्वतारोहण इतिहासमा छोडेर गएको पदचाप सधैं अमर रहनेछ।

articles.title: सामाजिक सद्भाव र धार्मिक सहिष्णुता कायम राख्न सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेश सरकारको अपिल
articles.summary:
सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेश सरकारले सुनसरीको कप्तानगञ्ज घटनापछि उत्पन्न परिस्थितिलाई दृष्टिगत गर्दै सामाजिक सद्भाव, धार्मिक सहिष्णुता र शान्ति कायम राख्न सबैमा अपिल गरेको छ।

मुख्यमन्त्री कमलबहादुर शाहले आज एक अपिल जारी गर्दै नेपाल बहुजातीय, बहुभाषिक र बहुधार्मिक विशेषता बोकेको मुलुक भएकाले सामाजिक, सांस्कृतिक तथा धार्मिक उत्सवहरू मनाउँदा एकअर्काको भावना र शान्तिमा खलल नपुग्ने गरी मर्यादित व्यवहार गर्न आग्रह गरेका छन्। साथै सामाजिक सञ्जालमा अफवाह, घृणायुक्त अभिव्यक्ति वा भ्रामक सामग्री पोस्ट वा साझा गरेर समाजमा वैमनस्य फैलाउने कार्य नगर्न पनि अनुरोध गरेका छन्।

प्रदेश सरकारले कानुन हातमा लिने, सामाजिक सद्भाव भड्काउने तथा अराजकता फैलाउने गतिविधिमा संलग्नलाई कानुनी दायरामा ल्याउन राज्यका निकाय सक्रिय रहेको जनाएको छ। प्रदेशका नागरिकलाई संयमता अपनाई कुनै गतिविधि गर्नु परे स्थानीय तह, प्रशासन र सुरक्षा निकायसँग समन्वय गर्न पनि आग्रह गरिएको छ।

सुनसरी घटनाको सम्भावित प्रभावलाई दृष्टिगत गर्दै खुला सीमाका कारण हुन सक्ने घुसपैठ तथा अवाञ्छित गतिविधि रोक्न सुदूरपश्चिमका सीमा क्षेत्रमा विशेष सतर्कता अपनाउन सुरक्षा निकायलाई निर्देशन दिइएको पनि अपिलमा उल्लेख छ। प्रदेशका सबै जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय र सुरक्षा निकायलाई पूर्ण तयारी अवस्थामा रही सुरक्षा व्यवस्था चुस्त बनाउनसमेत निर्देशन दिइएको जनाइएको छ।

यस्तै, सामाजिक सञ्जाल वा अन्य माध्यमबाट समाजमा उत्तेजना, घृणा र वैमनस्य फैलाउने गरी सार्वजनिक अफवाह र गलत सूचना प्रवाह गर्ने जो–कोहीलाई कडा कानुनी कारबाही गरिने चेतावनी पनि दिइएको छ। साथै सञ्चारकर्मी तथा सञ्चारमाध्यमलाई सामाजिक सद्भावमा आँच आउने खालका सामग्री प्रसारण नगरी सत्य, तथ्य र वस्तुनिष्ठ समाचार मात्रै सम्प्रेषण गर्न आग्रह गरिएको छ।

विज्ञप्तिमा भनिएको छ, ‘शान्ति, सुरक्षा, सामाजिक एकता, धार्मिक सहिष्णुता र पारस्परिक भाइचारा कायम राख्न सरकार, राजनीतिक दल, नागरिक समाज, धार्मिक अगुवा, उद्योगी–व्यवसायी, सामाजिक संस्था, सञ्चारमाध्यम र आमनागरिक सबैको सहकार्य आवश्यक छ। त्यसका लागि सामाजिक एकता थप बलियो बनाउने कार्यमा योगदान गर्न सबैमा आह्वान गर्दछु।’

सुनसरी र अन्य जिल्लामा प्रदर्शनका क्रममा ज्यान गुमाएकाप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जलि व्यक्त गर्दै शोकसन्तप्त परिवारप्रति समवेदना तथा घाइतेहरूको शीघ्र स्वास्थ्यलाभको कामना पनि गरिएको छ।

articles.title: सहकारी ठगीका मुद्दा हेर्न समर्पित इजलास गठन गर्न अनुरोध
articles.summary:
भूमि व्यवस्था, सहकारी, संघीय मामिला तथा सामान्य प्रशासन मन्त्रालयले सहकारी ठगीसम्बन्धी मुद्दाको छिटो र छरितो ढंगले न्याय निरूपण गर्नका लागि सहकारी कसुर हेर्ने ‘समर्पित इजलास’ गठन गर्न भन्दै सर्वोच्च अदालतका प्रधानन्यायाधीशलाई प्रतिवेदन पेस गरेको छ।

सहकारी ठगीसम्बन्धी मुद्दाको चाप बढिरहेकाले सो मुद्दा फर्छ्यौटका लागि समर्पित इजलास गठन गर्न अनुरोध गरिएको हो। मन्त्रालयले समर्पित इजलास गठन गर्नुको आवश्यकता र औचित्यको विषयमा कार्यदल गठन गरेर तयार पारेको प्रतिवेदन प्रधानन्यायाधीशलाई बुझाइएको मन्त्रीको निजी सचिवालयले जनाएको छ।

सर्वोच्च अदालतले २०८२ माघ ११ गते जारी गरेको निर्देशनात्मक आदेशमा सहकारी कसुरसम्बन्धी मुद्दाको चाप बढी भएका जिल्ला अदालतमा आवश्यकताअनुसार समर्पित इजलास स्थापना गर्न अध्ययन गरी निष्कर्षका आधारमा कार्यान्वयन गर्ने आदेश दिएपछि मन्त्रालयले अध्ययन कार्यदल गठन गरेको थियो।

भूमि व्यवस्था, सहकारी, संघीय मामिला तथा सामान्य प्रशासनमन्त्री प्रतिभा रावलले कार्यदलका सदस्यसहित उक्त प्रतिवेदन सर्वोच्च अदालतका प्रधानन्यायाधीश डा मनोज शर्मालाई बुझाएकी हुन्।

कार्यदलको प्रतिवेदनमा सहकारी कसुरलाई सामान्य ठगीको घटनाभन्दा फरक, ठूलो सङ्ख्यामा नागरिकको जीवन, सम्पत्ति र मुलुकको वित्तीय प्रणालीसँग प्रत्यक्ष सम्बन्धित सामाजिक-आर्थिक अपराधका रूपमा व्याख्या गरिएको छ।

यस्ता मुद्दाको प्रभावकारी र छिटो सुनुवाइका लागि विशेष प्राथमिकतासहित समर्पित इजलास आवश्यक रहेको निष्कर्ष प्रतिवेदनले निकालेको छ। प्रतिवेदनमा सहकारी ठगीका मुद्दा लामो समयसम्म विचाराधीन रहँदा पीडित बचतकर्ताले आफ्नो बचत फिर्ता पाउन नसक्ने, न्यायमा ढिलाइ हुने तथा दोषीलाई विभिन्न प्रकारका संरक्षण हुने जोखिम बढ्ने उल्लेख गरिएको छ।

सो प्रतिवेदनमा पीडितलाई समयमै न्याय दिलाउन, सहकारी क्षेत्रप्रतिको जनविश्वास पुनःस्थापित गर्न तथा वित्तीय सुशासन कायम गर्न समर्पित इजलास गठन अपरिहार्य रहेको कार्यदलको निष्कर्ष छ।

articles.title: Nirmal Purja, who redrew the limits of human endurance and reshaped Nepali mountaineering, dies in Broad Peak avalanche
articles.summary:
Nirmal Purja, the Nepal-born former special forces soldier who stunned the mountaineering world by summiting all 14 of the planet’s 8,000-metre peaks in six months, has died in an avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak. He was 43.

Purja's death was confirmed in a statement by Elite Expedition on its social account on Saturday. "It is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nirmal "Nimsdai" Purja tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak," the statement said. "We have also received confirmation that other members of the expedition sadly did not survive."

Purja was on Broad Peak as part of an expedition when an avalanche struck the team on July 30, 2026. Pakistani mountaineering authorities said there had been no communication with the group since the incident. Mingma Gyabu Sherpa, a member of Nepal’s House of Representatives and Purja’s business partner, had said that tracking data showed Purja’s position had shifted after the avalanche — first appearing to have been swept downhill, then moving again from where the signal had stopped.

Known across Nepal and the global climbing world as “Nims Dai,” Purja became one of the most recognisable figures in modern mountaineering after completing what he called Project Possible — an attempt, in 2019, to climb all 14 of the world’s eight-thousanders in seven months. He finished in six months and six days, shattering a previous record by more than seven years.

Purja spent much of his career testing the outer limits of human endurance, driven by an unshakeable belief that anything was achievable if a person set their mind to it.

“I am quite lucky with my physiology but I have also been trained by the best unit on earth,” he told the Post in an interview in 2019, referring to his military training. “So when you combine that with a positive mindset, you can do anything.”

Purja was born on July 25, 1983, in Dana village in Myagdi district, and grew up largely in Chitwan. He came from a family with a long history of military service: his father and three older brothers all served in Nepal’s Gurkha regiments. Purja followed that path himself, serving six years as a British Gurkha before becoming the first Nepali to be accepted into the British Special Boat Service, an elite unit of the Royal Navy. “Being a Gurkha was my only dream,” he wrote in his book. “It was the only thing I wanted to do.”

Across a military career spanning roughly 16 years, he later became a subject-matter expert in extreme cold-weather warfare within the SBS’s mountain unit. He was appointed a Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE) in 2018 for his military service and mountaineering achievements.

On the morning of October 30, 2019, Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu was packed with journalists waiting for him. Purja emerged from the arrival hall buried under flower garlands so heavy he could barely move his neck.

To finance that expedition, Purja resigned from the Special Boat Service, gave up his military pension and sold his house in the UK. “I gave up my job in the United Kingdom. I gave up my pension and sold my house for this high-altitude, high-speed quest,” he told reporters at the time. “Nobody believed it could be done. Everyone was laughing at me when I launched Project Possible.”

Purja did not come to mountaineering through a conventional path. His climbing career traces back to a 2012 trek to Everest Base Camp, originally planned as a simple hike, that he extended into a summit push, an experience he later said had ignited his ambition for the mountains.

He went on to compress what typically takes climbers years or decades into months. His 2019 record-breaking expedition, chronicled in the Netflix documentary “14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible,” carried him across Nepal, Pakistan and Tibet, closing with Shishapangma on October 29, 2019. His team included Mingma David Sherpa, Gesman Tamang, Galjen Sherpa, Lakpa Dendi Sherpa and Halung Dorchi Sherpa.

For Purja, the record was never simply about speed. On April 23, 2019, while descending Annapurna, Purja interrupted his own expedition to help rescue Malaysian climber Chin Wui Kin, who had been stranded without food, water or supplemental oxygen for around 40 hours. Purja brought him down, though Chin later died from his injuries after being evacuated to Singapore. Weeks later, during the ascent of Kanchenjunga, Purja again gave up his own summit push to help others. “At 8,450 metres, we had to give our oxygen and start rescuing three other climbers,” he recalled. “That was a suicidal attempt and probably the hardest moment.”

His final obstacle on the expedition came not from weather or altitude but politics: with only Shishapangma left to climb, Chinese authorities repeatedly delayed his climbing permit, which was finally granted on October 15 after Nepal’s government intervened diplomatically with Beijing. “From rescuing people at high altitudes to fixing ropes, from supplying oxygen to opening routes and going nights without sleeping, we were doing multiple jobs and were testing our limits,” Purja said afterward. “But we delivered.”

Purja called the feat “extremely, horrendously good,” despite setbacks along the way, including having his oxygen supply stolen while climbing Lhotse. Speaking to reporters in Kathmandu after his return, Purja said he hoped his record would show the next generation of Nepali climbers that “anything is possible with determination.”

In doing so, he broke South Korean climber Kim Chang-ho’s previous record of seven years, ten months and six days, and eclipsed Polish climbing legend Jerzy Kukuczka, who had become the first person to complete all 14 eight-thousanders, in 1987, after nearly eight years. Purja’s own record proved short-lived: on July 27, 2023, Norwegian climber Kristin Harila and her Nepali climbing partner, Tenjen (Lama) Sherpa, completed all 14 peaks in just 92 days.

His 2019 schedule bordered on the unbelievable. He climbed Annapurna and Dhaulagiri, moved to Kanchenjunga, then summited Everest, immediately traversed to adjoining Lhotse, flew to Makalu Base Camp and climbed Makalu — all within 48 hours. His campaign then continued through Pakistan, where he climbed Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Gasherbrum II, Broad Peak and K2, before returning to Nepal to finish Manaslu, Cho Oyu and, finally, Shishapangma.

During that same expedition, Purja took a photograph that would become one of the defining mountaineering images of the decade: a long queue of climbers near Everest’s summit, widely described as a “traffic jam,” which ran on front pages worldwide, including in The Kathmandu Post, and helped push Nepal’s government to tighten climbing regulations.

He later co-founded Elite Exped with Mingma David Sherpa and, in January 2021, was part of a 10-member all-Nepali team, alongside Mingma Gyalje Sherpa, that achieved the first winter ascent of K2 — one of the last unclaimed milestones in Himalayan mountaineering, a peak he told The Post was the only one among the 14 that genuinely scared him.

His journey reached a global audience beyond Nepal in 2021, when the documentary “14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible” introduced viewers in 191 countries to Nepal’s climbing community and made Purja one of the world’s most recognisable mountaineers almost overnight. Purja published a memoir, “Beyond Possible” in 2020, tracing his path from a 16-year military career to record-setting mountaineer, and continued to add to his list of Guinness World Records in high-altitude climbing in the years that followed.

Purja’s rise made him one of Nepal’s most prominent public figures internationally, and he used that platform to campaign for greater recognition of Nepali climbers, and for the welfare of high-altitude workers and communities through the Nimsdai Foundation. He also served on international panels addressing sustainability in mountain regions. Beyond mountaineering, he also expanded into aviation, serving as chairman of Mustang Helicopters.

“He was daring. He loved challenges. He was frank,” said Tashi Gyalzen Sherpa, 30, who climbed Everest four times within 15 days last spring and who helped Purja retrieve bodies from Shishapangma in 2024. “It is a big loss to the climbing fraternity.”

Tashi said Purja fundamentally altered the mindset of Nepal’s climbing community. “He was overly ambitious. He taught Sherpas to not just climb — but climb for a purpose.”

But his career was not without controversy. Nepal’s Department of Tourism investigated Purja and Elite Exped over allegations that an unauthorised helicopter had flown directly to Everest’s Camp II and that high-altitude training had been conducted without permission. He faced criticism over his company’s handling of compensation following an oxygen-cylinder explosion in 2022 at a rented property linked to his company, which a court later ordered the company to pay compensation for after the blast destroyed the house and caused deaths. During the climbing season in 2024, he drew criticism within the mountaineering community after sharing a viral video alleging rival Sherpas had deliberately cut fixed ropes above Everest’s South Summit, claims that sparked heated debate and a government investigation. In 2024, two female mountaineers accused him of sexual harassment, which was reported in the New York Times. Purja said he unequivocally denied any wrongdoing.

Purja is married to Suchi Purja, the daughter of a Gurkha soldier, and the couple have a daughter, Himani. The family divided time between the UK and Nepal. Purja obtained Non-Resident Nepali citizenship three years ago.

articles.title: US makes visa bond scheme permanent for Nepalis, others
articles.summary:
The US Department of State has announced that it will make its visa bond programme permanent for citizens of 50 countries, including Nepal, effective from Monday. Soon after the State Department introduced the scheme as a pilot programme last year, the Nepali government took up the issue with senior US officials, urging them to review the policy.

The move makes permanent a 12-month Visa Bond Pilot Program that took effect on August 20, 2025. The scheme applies to certain applicants for temporary business and tourist (B1/B2) visas.

This rule finalises the temporary final rule that went into effect on August 20, 2025, which launched a 12-month long Visa Bond Pilot Program (Pilot Program), and establishes a permanent visa bond program, reads a State Department statement issued on Friday.

“An alien applying for a visa as a temporary visitor for business or pleasure (B1/B2) may be required to submit a bond (‘visa bond’) to ensure that the alien maintains his or her nonimmigrant status and departs as required,” the State Department said in the 34-page rule.

The bond is refundable if the visa holder leaves the United States within the authorised period of stay, does not travel before the visa expires, or is denied admission at a US port of entry.

The rule also raises the maximum bond amount from $15,000 under the pilot programme to $20,000. Applicants may be asked to post a bond of $10,000, $15,000 or $20,000 depending on their purpose of travel, employment, income and other factors. Under the pilot programme, bond amounts ranged from $5,000 to $15,000.

Consular officers are generally expected to require a $15,000 bond, although they may impose a lower or higher amount based on individual circumstances.

The programme affects nationals of several African countries as well as Nepal, Bangladesh and Bhutan in South Asia.

In January this year, the US Embassy in Kathmandu announced that Nepalis who were otherwise eligible for B1/B2 visas could be required to post a bond of up to $15,000. The embassy said applicants would be informed during their visa interview if they were required to pay the bond.

Applicants were also advised not to pay through third-party websites and not to make any payment until instructed by a consular officer. B1/B2 visas would not be issued until the required bond had been paid, the embassy said.

According to the State Department, visa bonds may be required for applicants from countries with high visa overstay rates, inadequate information sharing, weak identity verification systems, incomplete criminal records, or deficiencies in travel document security and screening procedures.

Senior officials at Nepal’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs told the Post that Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal had repeatedly raised the issue with visiting US officials over the past four months.

According to the officials, Khanal discussed the matter with Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asian Affairs Paul Kapur, Trump’s special envoy and US ambassador to India Sergio Gor, and Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs Allison Hooker during separate meetings and conversations.

US officials told their Nepali counterparts that the visa bond requirement was linked primarily to visa overstays, document fraud and other immigration violations by Nepali nationals.

“They said the system is automatically reviewed and countries with improved compliance receive better scores. If Nepal’s performance improves, it could eventually be removed from the list,” a senior Foreign Ministry official said. “We will continue raising the issue.”

Officials at the Foreign Ministry and Nepal’s Embassy in Washington said document fraud, visa overstays and the misuse of public benefits reserved for US citizens were among the reasons Nepal was included in the programme.

According to one official, the latest US assessment found that Nepali applicants continued to submit fraudulent documents and that 3.34 percent of Nepali nationals had accessed certain US government-funded public benefits reserved for citizens.

Based on 2024 arrival data, Nepali nationals were among the higher users of some subsidised public services, prompting increased scrutiny of visa compliance, officials at the Nepali Embassy in Washington said.

The United States has also temporarily suspended the issuance of immigrant visas to Nepali nationals, citing concerns over compliance with immigration rules and public-benefit regulations.

The State Department said the programme is intended to encourage foreign governments to reduce visa overstays, strengthen identity verification, improve information sharing and enhance the security of travel and civil documents.

“By its design and intention, the programme is a tool of diplomacy,” the department said.

articles.title: Nepal’s SAFF Championship hopes hinge on FIFA lifting ANFA suspension
articles.summary:
Nepal have been drawn into Group A alongside hosts Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Bhutan for the upcoming SAFF Men’s Championship 2026, following the official draw ceremony held in Thimphu, Bhutan, on Saturday.

However, Nepal’s participation in South Asia’s premier international football tournament hinges on a critical condition: FIFA must lift the current suspension on the All Nepal Football Association (ANFA) before the stipulated SAFF deadline on September 30.

Nepali football was suspended by FIFA indefinitely on June 24 citing third-party interference.

If the suspension remains in place past the deadline, the tournament will proceed as a six-nation event without Nepal, leaving Group A with three teams (Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Bhutan). Group B features regional heavyweights India, the Maldives, and Pakistan.

It could be the first SAFF Championship without Nepal if the suspension is not lifted by the SAFF deadline.

The 15th edition of the flagship regional tournament is scheduled to take place in Dhaka, Bangladesh, from November 4 to 17.

SAFF is also preparing to use VAR in the tournament.

Nepal, runners-up in the 2021 edition, face an anxious wait off the pitch as administrative hurdles threaten to derail their participation on the regional stage. Should the suspension be cleared in time, Nepal will jump straight into action in Group A, expanding the group to four teams without disruption to the scheduled fixtures.

“September 30 has been kept as the deadline so that we can have sufficient time to finalise the fixtures and complete other registration procedures for the tournament,” SAFF’s general secretary Purushottam Kattel told the Post.

articles.title: गृहमन्त्री गुरुङसँग संयुक्त हिन्दु मोर्चाको १३ बुँदे माग (पत्रसहित)*
articles.summary:
गृहमन्त्री सुदन गुरुङ र संयुक्त हिन्दु मोर्चाबिच १३ बुँदे मागपत्रमा सहमति भएको छ। शनिबार जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय धनुषाको परिसरमा भएको वार्तामा मोर्चाले अघि सारेका १३ बुँदा माग पूरा गर्ने प्रतिबद्धा गृहमन्त्री गुरुङले जनाएसँगै आन्दोलन स्थगितसहितका विषयमा सहमति भएको हो।

हिन्दु राष्ट्र कायम गर्न तीन महिनाभित्र सर्वदलीय बैठकमार्फत प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढाउने र आन्दोलनरत संयुक्त हिन्दु मोर्चाले आन्दोलन स्थगित गर्ने सहमति दुई पक्षबीच भएको छ।

आन्दोलनरत हिन्दु मोर्चाले गृहमन्त्री गुरुङसमक्ष १३ बुँदे प्रस्ताव राखेको थियो।

संयुक्त हिन्दु मोर्चाको माग पत्रका १३ बुँदाहरू

१. दिगो शान्ति, सामाजिक सद्भाव, धार्मिक सहिष्णुता तथा धार्मिक सहअस्तित्वको प्रवर्द्धनका लागि किराँत, बौद्ध, सहित ८१ प्रतिशत हिन्दुहरूको बहूल्यता भएको नेपाल राष्ट्रलाई हिन्दु राष्ट्र कायम गर्ने विषयमा स्पष्ट समयसीमा तोकी सर्वदलीय बैठकमार्फत छलफल प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढाउने (तीन महिनाभित्र)।

२. जुनसुकै धर्म, सम्प्रदाय वा समुदायले मनाउने चाडपर्व तथा धार्मिक अवसरहरूमा हातहतियार प्रदर्शन गर्ने कार्यलाई नियन्त्रण गर्ने। यस्तो कार्य गर्ने व्यक्ति वा समूहलाई कानुनबमोजिम कारबाही गर्ने।

३. मठ, मन्दिर, मस्जिद, मदरसा, गुम्बा र चर्चलगायत धार्मिक स्थलमा जडान गरिएका बाहिरी हर्न (लाउडस्पिकर) तथा ध्वनि विस्तारक उपकरणको प्रयोगलाई नियन्त्रण गर्ने। आवश्यक धार्मिक गतिविधिका लागि परिसरभित्र मात्र सीमित ध्वनि प्रयोग गर्ने व्यवस्था मिलाउने।

४. मन्दिर, मस्जिद, गुम्बा, चर्च तथा अन्य धार्मिक स्थलमा बसोबास गर्ने सम्पूर्ण व्यक्तिहरूको अभिलेखिकरण र पहिचान खुलाउने तथा विदेशी नागरिक भए सो को अभिलेख सम्बन्धित निकायले राखी निगरानी र व्यवस्थापन गर्ने।

५. सामाजिक सञ्जाल वा अन्य माध्यमबाट धार्मिक, साम्प्रदायिक, जातीय हिंसा, द्वेष, चरित्र हत्या वा अतिवादी सोच फैलाउने व्यक्तिहरूको पहिचान गरी प्रचलित कानुनअनुसार कारबाही गर्ने।

६. सुनसरी देवानगञ्ज घटनापछि भएको आन्दोलनका क्रममा पक्राउ परेका व्यक्तिहरूमाथि दर्ता भएका मुद्दाहरूको पुनरावलोकन गरी आवश्यक निर्णय लिने तथा सम्बन्धित व्यक्तिहरूलाई कानुनी प्रक्रियाअनुसार रिहा गर्ने।

७. आन्दोलनका क्रममा घाइते भएका व्यक्तिहरूको उपचार तथा आवश्यक स्वास्थ्य सेवाको व्यवस्था गर्ने।

८. धार्मिक आयोगहरूको औचित्य आवश्यकता र कानुनी आधारहरूको पुनरावलोकन गरी आवश्यक प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढाउने।

९. आन्दोलनमा सहभागी नागरिकहरूको सुरक्षा तथा शान्ति सुरक्षाको प्रत्याभूति नेपाल सरकारले गर्ने।

१०. २०६२/२०६३ सालदेखि हालसम्म प्रदान गरिएको नेपाली नागरिकताको सम्बन्धमा छानबिन गरी विदेशी नागरिकहरूको सम्बन्धमा आवश्यक कानुनी प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढाउने।

११. मदरसा, मस्जिद तथा अन्य धार्मिक संस्थाहरूमा विभिन्न फन्डहरूको छानबिन गरी अनुगमन र नियमन गरी तत्काल कारबाहीको प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढाउनु पर्ने।

१२. १२ वर्षीय आनन्द दासको घटनामा संलग्न व्यक्तिको पहिचान गरी कानुनी कारबाही गरी पीडितलाई क्षतिपूर्ति समेत दिने।

१३. संयुक्त हिन्दु मोर्चाले आन्दोलनका सबै कार्यक्रम आजैको मितिबाट तत्काल स्थगित गर्ने।

माग पत्र हेर्नुस्

articles.title: दीपमाला ढकालले जितिन मिस नेपाल २०२६ को ताज
articles.summary:
दीपमाला ढकालले मिस नेपाल २०२६ को उपाधि जितेकी छन्।

ललितपुरस्थित द प्लाजामा शनिबार आयोजित ग्रान्ड फिनालेमा २३ जना प्रतिस्पर्धीलाई पछि पार्दै ढकालले मिस नेपाल २०२६ को ताज पहिरिएकी हुन्।

प्रतियोगितामा कशिस सुब्बाले मिस नेपाल कस्मो २०२६ को उपाधि जितिन् भने आर्या निशात मिस नेपाल इन्टरनेशनल २०२६ घोषित भइन्।

विभिन्न चरणको प्रतिस्पर्धा, प्रस्तुति तथा निर्णायक मण्डलको मूल्याङ्कनपछि विजेताहरूको घोषणा गरिएको हो।

मिस नेपाल प्रतियोगिता हरेक वर्ष आयोजना हुँदै आएको राष्ट्रियस्तरको प्रतिष्ठित सौन्दर्य तथा व्यक्तित्व विकाससम्बन्धी प्रतियोगिता हो। यसमार्फत विजेताहरूले अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय सौन्दर्य प्रतियोगितामा नेपालको प्रतिनिधित्व गर्ने अवसर प्राप्त गर्नेछन्।

articles.title: स्थानीय तहमा कानुन निर्माण कमजोर, प्रशासकीय अधिकृत सरुवाले समस्या
articles.summary:
राष्ट्रिय सभा अन्तर्गतको विधायन व्यवस्थापन समितिले नेपालमा ऐन कार्यान्वयनको मापन, यसको महत्त्व, अभ्यास, चुनौती र आगामी बाटोबारे अभिमुखीकरण कार्यक्रम सम्बन्धी छलफल गरेको छ ।

शनिबार सिंहदरबारमा बसेको समितिको बैठकमा सार्वजनिक नीति तथा प्रत्यायोजित विधायन समितिकी सभापति पूजा चौधरीले स्थानीय तहमा आवश्यक कानुन निर्माण र कार्यान्वयनमा अझै कमजोरी देखिएको बताएकी छन्।

उनले आफू सभापति बनेपछि विभिन्न पालिकाको भ्रमणका क्रममा स्थानीय तहलाई आवश्यक कानुनबारे सोध्दा धेरै ठाउँमा त्यससम्बन्धी स्पष्ट जानकारी नभेटिएको बताइन्।

चौधरीले भनिन्, ‘म सभापति भएपछि धेरै नगरपालिकामा त गएको छैन। तर एउटा नगरपालिकामा जाँदा सोध्यौँ–‘तपाईँहरूको स्थानीय तहमा चाहिने कतिवटा कानुन बनेका छन् ?’ उहाँहरूलाई नै थाहा थिएन । सङ्घबाट आएका कानुन त थिए, तर स्थानीय आवश्यकता अनुसार आफैँले बनाउनुपर्ने कानुन बनाएका रहेनछन् ।’

उनले स्थानीय तहमा प्रमुख प्रशासकीय अधिकृतको बारम्बार सरुवा हुने समस्याले पनि कानुन निर्माण र कार्यान्वयन प्रभावित भएको बताइन् ।

‘धेरैजसो पालिकामा प्रशासकीय अधिकृत तीन–चार महिनापछि बल्ल आउँछन्, आएको एक हप्तामै फेरि सरुवा भइहाल्छ । त्यसले पनि कानुन निर्माणको काम प्रभावित भएको छ,’ उनले भनिन् ।

चौधरीले उत्तर विधायकी परीक्षण प्रतिवेदनको नमुना ढाँचालाई आधार बनाएर कानुनको मूल्याङ्कन र सुधार गर्न सकिने उल्लेख गर्दै विधायन प्रक्रियामा विज्ञको भूमिका अपरिहार्य रहेको बताइन्।

उनले समितिले पुस्तकालय नीति निर्माणका क्रममा विज्ञ नियुक्त गरेर विभिन्न सामुदायिक तथा निजी पुस्तकालयको अध्ययन गरेको अनुभव सुनाउँदै बजेट अभावका कारण विज्ञलाई निरन्तर परिचालन गर्न कठिन हुने गरेको बताइन्।

उनले भनिन्, ‘हामी कानुनका विद्यार्थी होइनौँ। कुनै ऐन आवश्यक छ भन्ने थाहा हुन्छ, तर त्यसलाई कानुनी रूपमा कसरी तयार गर्ने भन्ने विषयमा विज्ञकै सहयोग चाहिन्छ । तर बजेट अभावका कारण पटक–पटक विज्ञलाई बोलाउन पनि अप्ठ्यारो हुन्छ । यसतर्फ राष्ट्रिय सभाले पनि आवश्यक व्यवस्था गर्नुपर्छ।’

बैठकमा राष्ट्रिय सभा सदस्य रामकुमारी झाँक्रीले कानुनको संख्या बढाउनुभन्दा त्यसको आवश्यकता, प्रभाव र कार्यान्वयन क्षमतामा ध्यान दिनुपर्ने धारणा राखिन्।

उनले नेपालसहित बेलायत, भारत लगायत वेस्टमिन्स्टर प्रणाली अपनाउने मुलुकमा सरकारले नै मुख्य रूपमा विधेयक ल्याउने अभ्यास रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै अमेरिकाको प्रणाली भने फरक रहेको बताइन्।

झाँक्रीले भनिन्, ‘हामी यत्तिधेरै चिन्तित भइरहनुपर्ने जस्तो लाग्दैन। आफ्नो विधायकी जिम्मेवारी पूरा गरेनौँ कि भन्ने गिल्टी बोकेर हिँड्न आवश्यक छैन। बेलायत, भारतलगायत वेस्टमिन्स्टर प्रणाली अपनाउने मुलुकमा सरकारले नै विधेयक ल्याउने अभ्यास छ । अमेरिकामा भने कार्यपालिकालाई संसद्मा विधेयक दर्ता गर्ने अधिकार छैन।’

उनले कानुन निर्माण गर्दा राज्यको आर्थिक तथा प्रशासनिक क्षमता पनि विचार गर्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिइन्।

‘जहाँ पनि कानुन बनाउनु भनेको राज्यको अतिरिक्त दायित्व सिर्जना गर्नु हो। त्यसैले नयाँ कानुन आवश्यक छ भने त्यो कार्यान्वयन गर्ने क्षमता राज्यसँग छ कि छैन भन्ने पनि हेर्नुपर्छ,’ उनले भनिन्।

नयाँ संविधानपछि धेरै कानुन बन्न बाँकी रहेको भन्ने बहसभन्दा कानुन नबन्दा नागरिकको जीवनमा कस्तो असर परेको छ भन्ने विषयमा केन्द्रित हुनुपर्ने उनको भनाइ थियो।

‘कानुन बनेन भनेर मात्रै भन्नुभन्दा त्यसले नागरिकलाई के असर ग¥यो भन्ने मूल्याङ्कन गर्नुपर्छ । नागरिकलाई सेवा दिन राज्यसँग आवश्यक स्रोत र क्षमता छ कि छैन भन्ने विषय पनि उत्तिकै महत्त्वपूर्ण हो,’ उनले भनिन् ।

उनले नेपालको संघीयता अन्य मुलुकको जस्तो नभई सहकार्य र सहअस्तित्वमा आधारित आफ्नै मोडल भएको उल्लेख गर्दै प्रदेश र स्थानीय तहको वित्तीय व्यवस्थालाई केवल नकारात्मक रूपमा मूल्याङ्कन गर्नु उचित नहुने बताइन्।

articles.title: वीरगञ्जमा हट्यो निषेधाज्ञा, जनजीवन सामान्य बन्दै
articles.summary:
जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय पर्साले जारी गरेको निषेधाज्ञा हटाएको छ।

पर्साका प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी (सिडिओ) भोला दाहालका अनुसार साउन १४ गते बिहीबार साँझ ५ः०० देखि बिहान ६ः०० बजेसम्म लागू हुँदै आएको निषेधाज्ञा आजदेखि हटाइएको छ। उनले वीरगञ्जमा पछिल्ला दिनमा देखिएको जुलुस तथा हुलदङ्गा सामान्य बन्दै गएपछि निषेधाज्ञा हटाउने निर्णय गरिएको जानकारी दिएका छन्।

सिरहाको गोलबजार घटनाका पीडित परिवार र सरकारबीच आठबुँदे सहमति भएपछि मृतकको अन्त्येष्टि प्रक्रिया अघि बढेसँगै केही दिनदेखि आन्दोलनरत हिन्दू समाज तथा विभिन्न हिन्दूवादी सङ्घसंस्थाहरूले आफ्ना सबै विरोधका कार्यक्रम तत्कालका लागि स्थगित गरेका छन्।

आन्दोलन स्थगित भएसँगै वीरगञ्ज तथा आसपासका क्षेत्रको जनजीवन, बजार, उद्योगधन्दा र यातायात सेवा पुनः नियमित बन्दै गएको छ। रासस
